questions.subject: Constitutional Law
questions.question:
Congress enacted a statute directing U.S. ambassadors to send formal letters to the governments of their host countries, protesting any violations by those governments of international treaties on weapons sales. The President prefers to handle violations by certain countries in a less formal manner and has directed ambassadors not to comply with the statute.
Is the President's action constitutional?

choices.A: No, because Congress has the power to implement treaties, and therefore the statute is binding on the President.
choices.B: No, because Congress has the power to regulate commerce with foreign nations, and therefore the statute is binding on the President.
choices.C: Yes, because Congress has no jurisdiction over matters outside the U.S. borders.
choices.D: Yes, because the President and his subordinates are the exclusive official representatives of the United States in foreign affairs.

questions.explanation:
Assessing the validity of presidential actions

Did President act pursuant to
exclusive Article II power?
  • Nominate principal officers
  • Veto bills
  • Prosecute/pardon federal offenses
  • Communicate/negotiate with foreign governments
  • Recognize foreign governments
  • Enter executive agreements
Yes ➔
Valid
No ▼
What has Congress done?
(Youngstown framework)
Authorized action
▼
Likely valid
Remained silent
▼
Middle zone
Opposed action
▼
Likely invalid

Article II vests the President with authority over a wide array of domestic and foreign policy areas. When the President shares authority with Congress over a particular area (eg, federal agencies), the validity of the President's actions is determined by the Youngstown framework. But when the President does not share authority with Congress, the President can exercise that exclusive Article II power without adhering to congressional directives.

One exclusive Article II power is the authority to communicate and negotiate with foreign governments as the official U.S. representative in foreign affairs. The President can exercise this power directly or through his/her subordinates—including ambassadors and other executive-branch officials. Therefore, it was constitutional for the President to direct the ambassadors not to comply with the federal statute regarding formal letters to foreign governments.

(Choice A) Congress has the power to implement treaties through appropriate legislation under the necessary and proper clause. But such legislation cannot restrict the President's ability to exercise an exclusive Article II power (as seen here).

(Choices B & C) Congress has some jurisdiction over matters outside U.S. borders—eg, the power to declare war and to regulate commerce with foreign nations. But this does not give Congress the power to bind the President (or his/her subordinates) on matters within the President's exclusive authority.

📌 Educational Objective

When the President does not share power with Congress over a particular area—eg, communicating with foreign governments—the President can exercise that exclusive Article II power without congressional interference.

📚 References
  • United States v. Curtiss-Wright Exp. Corp., 299 U.S. 304, 319 (1936) (stating that "the President alone has the power to speak or listen as a representative of the nation").
questions.zh-question:
国会颁布了一项法规，指示美国大使向其驻在国政府发出正式信函，抗议这些政府违反关于武器销售的国际条约。总统倾向于以不那么正式的方式处理某些国家的违规行为，并已指示大使不遵守该法规。
总统的行为是否合宪？

zh-choices.A: 否，因为国会有权执行条约（implement treaties），因此该法规对总统具有约束力。
zh-choices.B: 否，因为国会有权规范与外国的商业活动（regulate commerce with foreign nations），因此该法规对总统具有约束力。
zh-choices.C: 是，因为国会对美国境外事务没有管辖权（jurisdiction）。
zh-choices.D: 是，因为总统及其下属是美国在外交事务中的专属官方代表。

questions.zh-explanation:
MBE 考点解析

Constitutional Law: Separation of Powers - Domestic Power

本题真正考的是

一句话定位考点

本题真正考的是：总统在自己独享的 Article II 对外事务权限内，能不能无视国会要求，指挥大使不要照做。

三秒认题路径：

对外关系 → 总统独权 → 国会没同权 → 不能绑定 → 选 Yes

核心法律规则

总统（President）在对外事务里有些权力是自己独有的，考场意思：这类事不是国会和总统一起分的活。

其中包括和外国政府 沟通与谈判（communicate and negotiate），考场意思：总统可以亲自做，也可以通过 ambassadors（大使） 这些下属去做。

如果题干碰到的是这类独占权限，国会就不能用普通立法把总统拴住；这题里总统叫大使别发正式抗议信，属于他自己的对外代表动作。

核心判例：United States v. Curtiss-Wright Export Corp. - 强调总统独自作为国家代表对外说话或保持沉默的权限。

思维导图

先问：总统是在做 独占 Article II 权力 吗？
YES：对外沟通 / 谈判 / 指示大使 → 不受国会这条命令约束 → 答案：Yes
NO：再看 Youngstown：国会授权 → 可能有效；国会沉默 → 中间区；国会反对 → 大概率无效。
本题卡点：国会不是不能管任何涉外事项，而是不能管到总统这项 独占对外代表权 上。

考点陷阱

你可能会想：国会既然能通过 necessary and proper clause 实施条约，就能顺手要求总统照着发信。

但考试真正问的是：这是不是撞上了总统自己的独占对外权；如果是，国会就不能拿一般立法去改写他的做法。

司法考试看的是「法律程序上能不能救济」，而不是「物理上的秘密有没有泄露」。

正确答案与干扰项排除

为什么选 D？

题干关键在 ambassadors 代表国家对外发声；这属于总统独占的对外代表权，所以他可以让下属不执行国会命令。

❌ 概念混淆 | 条约实施误判

✕ A: 把 treaties 当成国会能管总统独权的通行证。

❌ 法律适用 | 商业权外推误判

✕ B: 看到 commerce 就乱套，但这题不是国内贸易监管。

❌ 事实误判 | 境外无权偷换

✕ C: 以为在境外国会就完全没戏，忽略了它仍可碰到部分涉外事务。

这题建议用什么方法？

先看是不是总统独占对外权，再判断国会命令有没有碰到 Youngstown 以外的硬边界。

考场速记

记住一句：“总统独占对外代表权，国会一般命令绑不住”。

遇到涉外沟通、承认国家、谈判、下达给大使的命令，先想总统是不是在做自己的 exclusive Article II power。

questions.subject: Constitutional Law
questions.question:
A county district attorney opened a criminal investigation into the President's business transactions conducted before the President assumed office. The district attorney brought the case before a grand jury, which validly issued a subpoena duces tecum requiring the President to produce various financial records related to the business transactions at issue. The President has refused to produce the financial records, citing absolute immunity and executive privilege.
Under what circumstances, if any, may the grand jury compel production of the financial records over the President's assertions of absolute immunity and executive privilege?

choices.A: It may compel production only if the subpoena seeks critical evidence that cannot be obtained by any other means.
choices.B: It may compel production without providing any additional justification.
choices.C: It may not compel production under any circumstances because the disclosure of financial records is protected by executive privilege.
choices.D: It may not compel production under any circumstances because the President has absolute immunity from complying with a subpoena.

questions.explanation:
Presidential immunity & privilege
Immunity Absolute immunity from civil suits seeking damages for official executive actions
  • No immunity for actions that occurred before taking office
  • No immunity for actions unrelated to executive functions
  • No immunity from criminal subpoena
Privilege Power to withhold official documents & communications:
  • National security secrets – afforded greatest deference
  • Civil case – afforded greater deference than in criminal trial
  • Criminal case – afforded least deference (disclosure required if prosecution shows need)

As the head of the executive branch, the President possesses all Article II powers, including the power to execute federal laws and serve as the commander in chief of the armed forces. To safeguard the President's ability to perform these important duties, the President has the following protections in judicial proceedings:

  • Executive privilege – prevents the disclosure of confidential documents and communications made in performance of official duties and responsibilities
  • Absolute immunity – prevents civil suits for damages against the President for any act performed as part of the President's official duties and responsibilities

However, these protections are not infinite. For example, executive privilege does not extend to documents and communications that were made in performing private functions (i.e., private papers). Since the financial records at issue here relate to the President's private affairs before taking office—not official conduct while in office—the records are not protected by executive privilege (Choice C).

Additionally, the President is not absolutely immune from complying with a validly issued subpoena that seeks the President's private papers in a criminal proceeding (Choice D). Instead, the President must comply with the subpoena just like any other citizen. Since the grand jury validly issued the subpoena duces tecum in this case, the President must produce the requested financial records. As a result, the grand jury need not provide any additional justification to compel production of those records.

(Choice A) The grand jury does not need to meet a heightened standard of need by showing that the subpoena seeks critical evidence that cannot be obtained by any other means. The reason is that, in the absence of a need to protect the President, the public interest in fair and effective law enforcement favors access to such evidence.

📌 Educational Objective

Executive privilege and absolute immunity safeguard a President from liability when performing official duties and responsibilities. However, these protections are not absolute and will not shield the President from complying with a criminal subpoena that seeks the President's private papers.

📚 References
  • Trump v. Vance, 140 S. Ct. 2412, 2430 (2020) (holding that the President is not absolutely immune from state criminal subpoenas seeking his private papers and is not entitled to a heightened standard of need).
questions.zh-question:
一名县地方检察官启动了一项刑事调查，针对总统就职前进行的商业交易。该地方检察官将此案提交给大陪审团，大陪审团合法地发出了一份 **subpoena duces tecum**，要求总统提交与所涉商业交易相关的各种财务记录。总统拒绝提交这些财务记录，理由是享有 **absolute immunity**（绝对豁免权）和 **executive privilege**（行政特权）。
在何种情况下（如果有的话），大陪审团可以强制要求提交这些财务记录，以对抗总统提出的 **absolute immunity** 和 **executive privilege** 主张？

zh-choices.A: 只有当该 **subpoena** 寻求的是无法通过任何其他方式获取的关键证据时，大陪审团才可以强制要求提交。
zh-choices.B: 大陪审团可以在不提供任何额外理由的情况下强制要求提交。
zh-choices.C: 在任何情况下都不能强制要求提交，因为财务记录的披露受到 **executive privilege** 的保护。
zh-choices.D: 在任何情况下都不能强制要求提交，因为总统享有遵守 **subpoena** 的 **absolute immunity**。

questions.zh-explanation:
MBE 考点解析

Constitutional Law: Separation of Powers - Separation of Powers

本题真正考的是

一句话定位考点

本题真正考的是：总统对 私有商业记录（private papers） 主张 绝对豁免（absolute immunity） 和 行政特权（executive privilege） 时，能不能挡住有效的刑事传票（subpoena duces tecum）。

三秒认题路径：

总统被传票 → 刑事大陪审团 → 私人记录 → 不是公职行为 → 可强制提交

核心法律规则

总统的 行政特权（executive privilege） 只保护履行公职时形成的机密文件和沟通，考场意思：私人事务的材料不在这个保护里。

绝对豁免（absolute immunity） 主要挡的是因官方行为引发的民事赔偿诉讼，考场意思：它不是总统对刑事传票的通行证。

所以，只要传票有效，而且要的是总统上任前的私人财务记录，陪审团一般可以直接要求交出，不需要再证明“特别需要”。

核心判例： Trump v. Vance — 总统不能以绝对豁免或行政特权，挡住针对其私人文件的州刑事传票，也不能要求更高的证明标准。

思维导图

先问：这是 终局判决（final judgment） 吗？
否继续看有没有法定中间上诉；本题没有。
再问：能否走 附带命令原则（collateral-order doctrine）？
要过三关：重要性、独立性、终局后是否仍可有效复审。
卡死点：这里不是“秘密一旦泄露就完了”，因为终局后仍可撤销、重审、排除使用，所以通常仍可复审。
最后落点：有效刑事传票（valid subpoena） 要的是私人记录 → 现在就得交
结论选 B：不需要额外理由，也不能用绝对豁免或行政特权挡住。

考点陷阱

你可能会想：既然是总统文件，而且交出去就泄密了，那应该直接不让披露。

但考试真正问的是：法律程序上能不能救济，而不是这些私人财务记录有没有“看起来很重要”。

司法考试看的是「法律程序上能不能救济」，而不是「物理上的秘密有没有泄露」。

正确答案与干扰项排除

为什么选 B？

题干点明是 valid subpoena 追的是上任前的私人财务记录，所以总统不能再加额外门槛，必须交出。

❌ 法律适用 | 高门槛套错

✕ A: 把 critical evidence 当成必过门槛了，但本题根本不要求这个标准。

❌ 概念混淆 | 特权范围误判

✕ C: 误把私人财务记录当成 executive privilege 保护的官方文件。

❌ 事实误判 | 绝对豁免泛化

✕ D: 把 absolute immunity 扩到刑事传票上了，题干事实不支持这种挡法。

这题建议用什么方法？

先分清是公职文件还是私人记录，再看是民事豁免还是刑事传票，最后才判断能否立即强制提交。

考场速记

记住这句：官方行为 才更容易触发 行政特权（executive privilege）；私人纸张（private papers） 不享受这层保护。

本题口诀：“私事材料，别想硬挡；有效传票，直接提交。” 看到总统 + 私人文件 + 刑事大陪审团，先想 Trump v. Vance。

reason.en: The issue is whether immunity for official conduct extends to compliance with this criminal subpoena.

reason.en: It incorrectly imposes a heightened need standard for private presidential records.

A.text: cannot be obtained by any other means

label.zh: 其他途径不可获得要求

reason.en: No last-resort showing is required for this valid criminal subpoena.

reason.en: This overstates executive privilege as an absolute bar.
reason.zh: 其将行政特权错误夸大为绝对障碍。

reason.en: Executive privilege does not cover private business records created before office.
reason.zh: 行政特权不涵盖就职前形成的私人商业记录。

reason.en: This falsely treats presidential immunity as universally applicable.
reason.zh: 其错误地将总统豁免视为普遍适用。

D.text: absolute immunity from complying with a subpoena

label.zh: 不存在的传票遵守豁免

reason.en: A President has no absolute immunity from a criminal subpoena seeking private papers.
reason.zh: 总统对索取私人文件的刑事传票不享有绝对豁免。

highlights.text: conducted before the President assumed office

reason.en: This places the transactions outside the President's official duties.
reason.zh: 该事实使相关交易不属于总统公务行为。

highlights.text: validly issued a subpoena duces tecum

reason.en: Validity triggers the ordinary obligation to produce unprotected records.
reason.zh: 传票有效即触发提交不受保护记录的通常义务。

highlights.text: financial records related to the business transactions at issue

reason.en: These are private papers rather than official executive communications.
reason.zh: 这些属于私人文件，而非行政公务通信。

highlights.text: over the President's assertions of absolute immunity and executive privilege

reason.en: The question tests whether either asserted protection defeats the subpoena.
reason.zh: 本题考查两项总统保护主张是否能够阻止传票执行。

questions.subject: Constitutional Law
questions.question:
Congress enacted a statute over the President's veto establishing a program to protect areas in the United States that are rich in biological diversity. The program is consistent with the terms of an environmental treaty that the President objected to and did not sign.
The statute creates an executive agency and authorizes it to designate parts of federal lands for inclusion in the program in accordance with criteria taken from the treaty. In an inseverable provision, the statute further provides that the agency must report each designation to a committee of Congress and that the committee may overturn the agency's designation by a majority vote.
Why is the statute unconstitutional?

choices.A: It authorizes a committee of Congress to overturn an executive decision.
choices.B: It constitutes an invalid delegation of legislative authority to an executive agency.
choices.C: It interferes with the exercise of the President's paramount authority in foreign affairs.
choices.D: It requires an executive agency to report its decisions to Congress.

questions.explanation:
Federal legislative process (requirements for legislative action)
Bill proposed in Congress
Bicameralism
Bill passes both houses
Presentment
President
signs bill

vetoes bill
President takes
no action

(two-thirds vote)

Bill becomes law

The nondelegation doctrine prohibits Congress from delegating purely legislative powers (eg, making or repealing laws). But it allows Congress to delegate its incidental powers (eg, regulating federal lands) to executive agencies if it provides an intelligible principle—ie, a clear statement defining:

  • the policy Congress seeks to advance (eg, protect areas in the United States that are rich in biodiversity)
  • the agency to carry out that policy (eg, the agency created by statute here) and
  • the scope of that agency's authority (eg, designate parts of federal lands for inclusion in the environmental protection program) (Choice B).

But once Congress has delegated authority to an executive agency, Congress cannot authorize a committee to veto (ie, overturn) that agency's executive decisions. Such decisions can only be overturned through new legislation, which requires:

  • bicameralism—which entails a majority vote in both the House of Representatives and the Senate (not merely a congressional committee)—and
  • presentment to the President for approval or disapproval (which did not occur here).

Therefore, the statute is unconstitutional because it authorizes a committee of Congress to overturn an executive decision.

(Choice C) Article II gives the President paramount authority in foreign affairs, so Congress could not have forced the President to sign the environmental treaty. But since Congress has the power to enact domestic laws, it can implement this program protecting areas in the United States despite the President's objection to the treaty.

(Choice D) Congress can require executive agencies to report their decisions to Congress if this is necessary and proper for (ie, reasonably related to) implementing federal law. But Congress cannot veto executive agency decisions without adhering to bicameralism and presentment.

📌 Educational Objective

Congress can only overturn an executive agency's actions by enacting new legislation. This requires both (1) passage by majority vote in the House of Representatives and the Senate (ie, bicameralism) and (2) presentation to the President for approval or disapproval (ie, presentment).

📚 References
  • Gundy v. United States, 139 S. Ct. 2116, 2123 (2019) (explaining that the nondelegation doctrine allows Congress to delegate power as long as it provides an intelligible principle to guide the delegate's use of discretion).
  • INS v. Chadha, 462 U.S. 919, 946–59 (1982) (striking down the congressional-veto provision of an immigration statute since it bypasses bicameralism and presentment).
questions.zh-question:
国会推翻总统否决，颁布了一项法规，设立了一个旨在保护美国境内生物多样性丰富区域的项目。该项目符合总统反对且未签署的一项环境条约的条款。
该法规设立了一个行政机构，并授权其根据条约中的标准，指定部分联邦土地纳入该项目。在一项不可分割的条款中，该法规进一步规定，该机构必须向国会的一个委员会报告每项指定，并且该委员会可以通过多数票推翻该机构的指定。
该法规为何违宪？

zh-choices.A: 它授权国会委员会推翻一项行政决定。
zh-choices.B: 它构成将立法权无效授权给行政机构。
zh-choices.C: 它干涉了总统在外交事务中行使的最高权力。
zh-choices.D: 它要求行政机构向国会报告其决定。

questions.zh-explanation:
MBE 考点解析

Constitutional Law: Separation of Powers - Delegation of legislative power

本题真正考的是

一句话定位考点

本题真正考的是：国会不能用一个小委员会直接推翻行政机关的决定，因为这等于绕开了立法的 bicameralism（两院通过） 和 presentment（呈交总统）。

三秒认题路径：

行政决定 → 委员会否决 → 绕开立法 → 违背两院与呈交 → 选 A

核心法律规则

国会可以把执行细节交给行政机关，这叫 delegation（授权），考场意思：只要国会先给出 intelligible principle（清楚指引），通常不算越权。

但国会不能在授权之后，再让某个委员会单独撤销行政机关的最终决定；那不是“监督”，而是在偷偷做新的立法。要真正改掉这个决定，必须重新走 bicameralism（两院通过） + presentment（呈交总统）。

所以这题的关键不是“能不能授权”，而是“国会能不能用委员会一票翻案”；答案是不能。

核心判例： INS v. Chadha —— 国会一旦想用委员会否决行政决定，就必须重新走立法程序，不能跳过两院与总统。
补充判例： Gundy v. United States —— 只要有 intelligible principle（清楚指引），把执行权交给行政机关通常可以。

思维导图

先看：这是不是“国会自己改法律”？
不是 → 国会只是先授权行政机关做执行细节
再看 → 授权有没有 intelligible principle（清楚指引）？
有：保护生物多样性 + 依照条约标准划定土地，授权本身不死
真正卡死点 → 不是授权，而是“委员会能否推翻行政决定”
不能：这等于没经过两院通过 + 呈交总统
结论：委员会否决条款无效 → 选 A

考点陷阱

你可能会想：题目一直在讲环境条约、总统反对、行政机关执行，好像是在考总统外事权或非授权原则。

但考试真正问的是：国会能不能让一个 committee of Congress（国会委员会） 直接撤销行政决定。

司法考试看的是「法律程序上能不能救济」，不是「国会有没有参与」，更不是「政策目标看起来合不合理」。

正确答案与干扰项排除

为什么选 A？

题干的 committee may overturn 直接跳过两院通过和呈交总统，所以违宪点在国会用委员会否决行政决定。

❌ 概念混淆 | 授权越界误判

✕ B: 把 delegation 当成问题核心了，其实授权本身有清楚指引。

❌ 法律适用 | 外事权泛化误判

✕ C: 看到条约就联想到总统外事权，但题目考的是国内立法程序。

❌ 事实误判 | 报告义务偷换

✕ D: 把 report 和否决混为一谈了，单纯报告可以，翻案不行。

这题建议用什么方法？

先分清“授权”与“立法否决”，再盯住是否绕开两院通过和呈交总统。

考场速记

记住这句：行政机关能做执行，国会委员会不能替立法翻案。

碰到中间程序例外时，再想口诀：In Certain Circumstances, An Appeal Can Be Made Prematurely，对应 injunction、certification、class action 等法定例外。

questions.subject: Constitutional Law
questions.question: Which of the following acts by the United States Senate would be constitutionally IMPROPER?

choices.A: The Senate appoints a commission to adjudicate finally a boundary dispute between two states.
choices.B: The Senate decides, with the House of Representatives, that a disputed state ratification of a proposed constitutional amendment is valid.
choices.C: The Senate determines the eligibility of a person to serve as a senator.
choices.D: The Senate passes a resolution calling on the President to pursue a certain foreign policy.

questions.explanation:
Independent legislative powers
(legislative-action process not required)
Legislative body Powers
House of Representatives
  • Impeach federal officials
  • Elect President (when electoral-college threshold not met)
  • Determine internal rules & members' eligibility
  • Punish/expel members for bad behavior
Senate
  • Try impeached federal officials
  • Confirm/reject presidential appointments
  • Approve/reject treaties
  • Determine internal rules & members' eligibility
  • Punish/expel members for bad behavior
Full Congress
  • Propose constitutional amendments
  • Decide disputes regarding ratification of amendments

Article I prescribes the method Congress (ie, the House of Representatives and the Senate) must use to take any action that alters the legal rights of persons outside the legislative branch (ie, legislative action). Under this method, most legislative action must be:

  • approved by both houses of Congress (ie, bicameralism) and
  • presented to the President for approval or disapproval (ie, presentment).

But certain legislative powers are independent and do not require bicameralism and/or presentment. These include:

  • the power of the Senate, together with the House of Representatives, to decide disputes regarding the ratification of amendments (no presentment required) (Choice B) and
  • the power of the Senate to determine a person's eligibility to serve as a senator (no bicameralism or presentment required) (Choice C).

These independent legislative powers do not include the power to appoint a commission to adjudicate boundary disputes between two states. Therefore, it would be constitutionally improper for the Senate to do so without adhering to bicameralism and presentment.

(Choice D) A resolution does not amount to legislative action because it is a nonbinding recommendation that has no effect on the legal rights of persons outside the legislative branch. Therefore, the Senate can pass a resolution calling on the President to pursue a certain foreign policy without adhering to bicameralism or presentment.

📌 Educational Objective

Absent narrow exceptions, all legislative action must be approved by both houses of Congress (ie, bicameralism) AND presented to the President for approval or disapproval (ie, presentment).

📚 References
  • Coleman v. Miller, 307 U.S. 433, 456 (1939) (explaining that Congress controls the promulgation of the adoption of constitutional amendments).
  • INS v. Chadha, 462 U.S. 91, 952 (1983) (explaining that legislative action is subject to bicameralism and presentment when Congress alters the legal rights, duties, and relations of persons outside the legislative branch).

questions.zh-explanation:
MBE 考点解析

Constitutional Law: Separation of Powers - Separation of Powers

本题真正考的是

一句话定位考点

本题真正考的是：国会有没有越过 立法行动（legislative action） 的程序门槛，去做本来必须经过 两院制（bicameralism） 和 呈交总统（presentment） 的事。

三秒认题路径：

国会行为 → 改变权利？ → 要两院制？ → 要总统呈交？ → 看是否例外

核心法律规则

先抓住规则骨架

立法行动（legislative action），考场意思：只要国会的动作会改变外部人的法律权利、义务或关系，就不能只在内部喊一声算数。

默认规则是：大多数立法行动都要经过 两院制（bicameralism） 和 呈交总统（presentment），所以如果少了这一步，通常就不合宪。

但有少数 独立立法权（independent legislative powers） 是例外，考场意思：这类动作本来就不走完整立法流程。

核心判例： INS v. Chadha - 只要国会行为在改外部人的法律关系，就要走两院制和呈交总统；Coleman v. Miller - 处理宪法修正案批准争议时，属于例外权力。

思维导图

先问：这个动作是不是在改外部人的法律地位？
YES：通常是 立法行动（legislative action），要过 bicameralism + presentment。
NO：如果只是内部建议、姿态性表态，可能不算正式立法行动。
再问：有没有明确的独立例外？
例外 1：宪法修正案批准争议（ratification disputes），由两院一起决定，不需要呈交总统。
例外 2：决定某人是否有资格当参议员，属于参议院的独立权力，不需要两院制，也不需要呈交总统。
本题落点：设立委员会最终裁决两州边界争议，不是这个例外，因此不能跳过正常立法程序。
结论：谁能直接这样做？
答案：不能选 A；B、C 属于已知例外，D 只是非约束性决议。

考点陷阱

你可能会想：boundary dispute 听起来很像国会内部可管的事务，所以参议院应该能直接设委员会处理。

但考试真正问的是：这是不是在替国会越过法定程序，直接改动外部人的法律权利。

司法考试看的是「法律程序上能不能救济」，而不是「物理上的边界会不会真的被争议」。

所以真正卡点不是“能不能讨论”，而是“能不能不用两院制和呈交总统就把最终法律效果做出来”。

正确答案与干扰项排除

为什么选 A？

题干的 finally adjudicate 直接做出对两州边界有法律效力的最终决定，属于立法权外的行为，不能绕开两院制和呈交总统。

❌ 概念混淆 | 规则渊源误判

✕ B: 把 ratification 当成普通立法；这题其实是修正案例外。

❌ 法律适用 | 独立权力误套

✕ C: 这是参议院独立资格判断，不是边界争议裁决。

❌ 事实误判 | 约束效果偷换

✕ D: resolution 只是建议，不会直接改法律关系。

这题建议用什么方法？

先看有没有改外部法律效果，再查是否落入国会独立例外；不能把“能表态”当成“能直接定案”。

考场速记

记住一句：改外部权利 就默认要 bicameralism + presentment，只有少数法定例外可以跳过。

口诀可以记成：In Certain Circumstances, An Appeal Can Be Made Prematurely 这类“可提前走例外”的思路，在中间程序题里先想有没有法定例外；本题则是反过来，别把例外想大了。

reason.en: The constitutional validity depends on the legal effect of the Senate's action.
reason.zh: 参议院行为的法律效果决定其是否合宪。

reason.en: The Senate has specific independent powers but generally cannot legislate alone.
reason.zh: 参议院享有特定独立权力，但通常不能单独立法。

reason.en: The question asks which unilateral Senate action violates constitutional procedure.

label.zh: 作出具有约束力的最终裁决

reason.en: Final adjudication makes the action legally binding rather than merely advisory.
reason.zh: 最终裁决使该行为具有法律约束力，而非仅为建议。

reason.zh: 无约束力的决议并非需要两院通过和提交总统的立法行为。

label.zh: 向总统提出建议性请求

reason.en: This language indicates persuasion rather than a binding command.
reason.zh: 该措辞表明这是劝告，而非具有约束力的命令。

reason.en: The resolution merely expresses the Senate's preferred policy and changes no legal rights.
reason.zh: 该决议仅表达参议院的政策偏好，不改变任何法律权利。

highlights.text: acts by the United States Senate

label.zh: 参议院单独行动权限范围

reason.en: The issue is whether the Senate may take each action without the full legislative process.
reason.zh: 核心问题是参议院能否绕过完整立法程序单独采取各项行为。

highlights.text: constitutionally IMPROPER

reason.en: The negative formulation requires selecting the action that violates constitutional procedure.

questions.subject: Constitutional Law
questions.question:
The Federal Drone Safety Act establishes the Federal Drone Safety Commission, authorizes the Commission to issue licenses for the sale of unmanned aerial drones on terms that are consistent with the purposes of the Act, and makes the unlicensed sale of a drone a crime. The provisions of the Federal Drone Safety Act are inseverable.
A hobby store owner applied to the Federal Drone Safety Commission for a license to sell drones. The Commission held, and the store owner participated in, a trial-type proceeding on his license application. In that proceeding it was demonstrated that the store owner had repeatedly and intentionally sold drones without a license. As a result, the Commission denied the store owner's application for a license. The license denial was based on a Commission rule authorized by the Drone Safety Act that prohibited the issuance of drone licenses to persons who had engaged in such conduct. Nevertheless, the store owner continued to sell drones in his store.
The store owner was subsequently convicted of the crime of unlicensed sale of a drone. On appeal, he challenges the constitutionality of the Federal Drone Safety Act.
What will be the most likely holding of the reviewing court?

choices.A: The Act is constitutional, because Congress may use the authority vested in it by the commerce clause to regulate the sale of drones and the provisions of the Act do not violate any prohibitory provision of the Constitution.
choices.B: The Act is constitutional, because the Constitution generally authorizes Congress to enact all laws that are necessary and proper to advance the general welfare, and Congress could reasonably believe that the sale of drones by people like the store owner constitutes a threat to the general welfare.
choices.C: The Act is unconstitutional, because Congress may not impose a criminal penalty on action that is improper only because it is inconsistent with an agency rule.
choices.D: The Act is unconstitutional, because the mere sale of a drone is a wholly local matter that is beyond the regulatory authority of Congress.

questions.explanation:
Nondelegation doctrine

Congress delegated:
Exclusive legislative power
Examples:
  • making/repealing laws
  • declaring war
  • impeaching federal officers
Incidental legislative power
Examples:
  • rulemaking
  • carrying out legislation
  • enforcing regulations
Yes
Yes
Unconstitutional
No
Congress provided
intelligible principle defining:
  • policy it seeks to advance
  • agency carrying out policy
  • scope of agency's authority

The commerce clause gives Congress broad authority to regulate interstate commerce. This power even extends to in-state activities that, singly or in the aggregate, substantially affect interstate commerce. A substantial effect is presumed when the activity is economic in nature. So, though drone sales are wholly local, it is presumed that this economic activity substantially affects interstate commerce (Choice D). Therefore, Congress can regulate these sales so long as it complies with prohibitory constitutional provisions.

One such provision is Article I, section 1 and its implied nondelegation doctrine. This doctrine prohibits Congress from delegating purely legislative powers. But it allows Congress to delegate its incidental powers (eg, rulemaking, legislative enforcement) if it provides an intelligible principle—ie, a clear statement defining:

  • the policy Congress seeks to advance (eg, drone safety)
  • the agency to carry out that policy (eg, the Federal Drone Safety Commission) and
  • the scope of that agency's authority (eg, issue licenses on terms consistent with the Act's purpose).

Since Congress properly delegated its regulatory authority to the Federal Drone Safety Commission—and there is no evidence that the Act violates any other prohibitory provision of the Constitution—the reviewing court will likely hold that the Act is constitutional.

(Choice B) Article I authorizes Congress to tax and spend for the general welfare and to enact legislation necessary and proper to exercise this enumerated power. The Act here seeks to regulate drone sales—not tax or spend—for the general welfare. And since the commerce clause gives Congress direct authority to regulate this economic activity, its powers under the necessary and proper clause are unnecessary here.

(Choice C) The unlicensed sale of a drone is criminalized by the Act itself—not an agency rule. And Congress could impose a criminal penalty on an action that is inconsistent with an agency rule so long as the rule was created within the scope of the agency's delegated authority.

📌 Educational Objective

Congress has broad authority to regulate economic activities since it is presumed that they substantially affect interstate commerce. But Congress can only delegate its incidental powers to another entity if it gives that entity an intelligible principle (policy, agency, scope) on which to base its regulations.

📚 References
  • Gonzales v. Raich, 545 U.S. 1, 17 (2005) (holding that Congress can regulate purely local activities that are part of an economic class of activities that substantially affect interstate commerce).
  • Gundy v. United States, 139 S. Ct. 2116, 2123 (2019) (explaining that the nondelegation doctrine allows Congress to delegate power as long as it provides an intelligible principle to guide the delegee's use of discretion).
questions.zh-question:
联邦无人机安全法案设立了联邦无人机安全委员会，授权该委员会根据符合法案宗旨的条款颁发无人机销售许可证，并将无证销售无人机定为犯罪。联邦无人机安全法案的各项规定是不可分割的。
一名爱好商店店主向联邦无人机安全委员会申请无人机销售许可证。委员会就其许可证申请举行了一场审判式程序，该店主也参与其中。在该程序中，证实该店主曾多次故意无证销售无人机。因此，委员会驳回了该店主的许可证申请。许可证的驳回是基于无人机安全法案授权的一项委员会规则，该规则禁止向从事此类行为的人员颁发无人机许可证。尽管如此，该店主仍继续在他的商店销售无人机。
随后，该店主因无证销售无人机罪被定罪。在上诉中，他质疑联邦无人机安全法案的合宪性。
复审法院最有可能的裁决是什么？

zh-choices.A: 该法案是合宪的，因为国会可以利用商业条款（commerce clause）赋予的权力来监管无人机的销售，并且该法案的规定没有违反宪法的任何禁止性条款。
zh-choices.B: 该法案是合宪的，因为宪法通常授权国会制定所有为促进公共福利（general welfare）而必要且适当的法律，并且国会有理由相信像该店主这样的人销售无人机对公共福利构成威胁。
zh-choices.C: 该法案是违宪的，因为国会不得仅因某行为不符合一项机构规则（agency rule）而对其施加刑事处罚。
zh-choices.D: 该法案是违宪的，因为仅仅销售无人机是一个纯粹的本地事务，超出了国会的监管权力（regulatory authority）。

questions.zh-explanation:
MBE 考点解析

Constitutional Law: Separation of Powers - Separation of Powers

本题真正考的是

一句话定位考点

本题真正考的是：国会把立法权（legislative power）交给行政机构时，只要给了可识别原则（intelligible principle），通常就不违反非授权原则（nondelegation doctrine）。

三秒认题路径：

国会设委会 → 许可规则 → 有原则指引 → 只是执行 → 合宪

核心法律规则

国会可以通过商业条款（Commerce Clause）调控经济性活动；像无人机销售这种交易，考试上通常会被看成会影响州际商业，所以国会先有权管。

但国会不能把纯粹的立法权（legislative power）直接甩给机构；它可以授权机构做附带性权力（incidental power），前提是法案说清楚三件事：要推进什么政策、哪个机构来做、机构权限多大。

这道题里，法案已经把无人机安全（drone safety）、联邦无人机安全委员会（Federal Drone Safety Commission）和“按法案目的发许可”的范围都写出来了，所以授权有效。

核心判例： Gundy v. United States - 说明只要国会给了可识别原则，授权机构裁量一般就站得住；Gonzales v. Raich - 说明经济性本地活动也可能落入商业条款。

思维导图

先问：这题是在打“无权管”还是“管了但授权过头”？
1. 先看国会有没有权力：无人机销售是经济性活动，Commerce Clause 先给国会管的底盘。
别被“全在本州”骗走：本地也可能因经济属性而被管。
2. 再看有没有越过非授权红线：国会不能把纯立法权全扔出去，但可以让机构做执行和规则制定。
看三样：policy、agency、scope。
本题三样都写进法案了，所以不是“无标准的乱授权”。
3. 结论直达：授权有效 → 许可证规则有效 → 无证卖 drone 仍可定罪 → 选 A。

考点陷阱

你可能会想：既然店主是被agency rule卡住的，那国会是不是把犯罪标准交给机构了。

但考试真正问的是：刑罚写在法案里，不是机构自己创罪；只要机构规则在授权范围内，国会仍然可以据此设定违反法案的后果。

司法考试看的是「法律程序上能不能救济」，而不是「物理上的秘密有没有泄露」。

正确答案与干扰项排除

为什么选 A？

题干已经把无人机销售放进经济性管制场景里，而且法案清楚写了政策、机构和权限范围，所以国会的授权没有踩到非授权红线。

❌ 概念混淆 | 一般福利混搭

✕ B: 把general welfare硬搬来这里，抓错了授权来源。

❌ 法律适用 | 刑罚来源误判

✕ C: 误以为罪名来自agency rule，其实刑罚写在国会法案里。

❌ 事实误判 | 本地性夸大

✕ D: 把wholly local当成免管理由，漏掉经济活动可被联邦规制。

这题建议用什么方法？

先认出是商业条款（Commerce Clause）加非授权原则（nondelegation doctrine），再看法案有没有把政策、机构和权限说清楚。

考场速记

记住一句：国会能管经济活动，也能授权机构执行，但必须给可识别原则（intelligible principle）。

看到“政策 + 机构 + 权限”都写明了，通常就直接判合宪；别被“本地销售”四个字带偏。

reason.en: Raises whether Congress validly delegated rulemaking authority to the Commission.
reason.zh: 引出国会是否向委员会有效授权规则制定权的问题。

B.text: necessary and proper to advance the general welfare

D.text: beyond the regulatory authority of Congress

reason.zh: 错误缩小了国会对经济活动的监管权。

highlights.text: authorizes the Commission to issue licenses for the sale of unmanned aerial drones on terms that are consistent with the purposes of the Act

reason.en: Identifies the delegated authority and the intelligible principle constraining it.
reason.zh: 确定了被授权的权力以及约束该权力的可理解原则。

highlights.text: makes the unlicensed sale of a drone a crime

reason.en: Defeats the claim that the agency itself improperly created the criminal offense.
reason.zh: 否定了行政机关本身不当创设犯罪的主张。

highlights.text: The provisions of the Federal Drone Safety Act are inseverable

reason.en: Makes the validity of the delegation potentially dispositive of the entire Act.
reason.zh: 使授权的有效性可能决定整部法律的效力。

highlights.text: continued to sell drones in his store

reason.zh: 该行为的商业性质支持依据商业条款进行联邦监管。

questions.subject: Constitutional Law
questions.question:
Terrorists in a foreign country kidnapped the United States ambassador to that country. They threatened to kill her unless the President of the United States secured the release of an identified person who was a citizen of the foreign country and was being held in a state prison in the United States pursuant to a valid conviction by that state.
The President responded by entering into an agreement with the foreign country which provided that the foreign country would secure the release of the United States ambassador on a specified date in return for action by the President that would secure the release of the identified person held in the state prison. The President then ordered the governor of the state to release the prisoner in question. The governor refused. No federal statutes are applicable.
Which of the following is the strongest constitutional argument for the authority of the President to take action in these circumstances requiring the state governor to release the prisoner?

choices.A: The duty of the President to faithfully execute the laws authorizes him to resolve any conflicts between state and federal interests, making the determination of such matters wholly nonjusticiable.
choices.B: The power of the President to appoint ambassadors authorizes him to take any action that he may think desirable to protect them from injury because those officials become agents of the President upon appointment.
choices.C: The power of the President to conduct the foreign affairs of the United States includes a plenary authority to take whatever action the President deems wise to protect the safety of our diplomatic agents.
choices.D: The power of the President to negotiate with foreign nations impliedly authorizes him to make executive agreements with them which prevail over state law.

questions.explanation:
Article II executive powers
Domestic powers
  • Manage federal executive agencies & officers
  • Execute federal laws
  • Recommend legislation to Congress
  • Sign or veto bills
  • Appoint/remove federal officers
  • Prosecute & grant pardons for federal crimes
Foreign powers
  • Serve as commander in chief
  • Negotiate/enter treaties (with 2/3 Senate approval) & executive agreements
  • Recognize foreign governments
  • Appoint/receive foreign diplomats

Article II gives the President a wide range of domestic and foreign powers. In foreign affairs, the President's power is at its zenith because it is imperative that the nation speak with one voice on the international stage. One such power is that the President can negotiate and enter into agreements with foreign nations. These agreements can take the form of either:

  • treaties – formal agreements that take effect once the Senate gives advice and consents by a two-thirds vote or
  • executive agreements – less formal agreements that take effect as soon as the President enters into them (ie, no Senate advice and consent required).

Here, the President entered into an executive agreement with the foreign country to secure the release of that country's citizen from state prison. And under the supremacy clause, executive agreements—which carry the force of federal law—prevail over conflicting state laws. Therefore, this is the strongest constitutional argument for the President's authority to require the governor to release the foreign country's citizen from state prison.

(Choice A) The President's duty to faithfully execute federal laws does not authorize him/her to resolve conflicts between state and federal interests. Instead, these conflicts are justiciable and must be resolved in court.

(Choices B & C) Article II grants the President the power to appoint ambassadors, who then become agents of the President. But this does not give the President plenary (ie, absolute) authority to take any action that he/she deems desirable or wise to protect them because the President must comply with the Constitution, treaties, and federal laws.

📌 Educational Objective

The President has extensive powers in foreign affairs, including the power to negotiate and enter into executive agreements with foreign countries. And under the supremacy clause, executive agreements prevail over conflicting state laws.

📚 References
  • Am. Ins. Assoc. v. Garamendi, 539 U.S. 396, 415–17 (2003) (explaining the creation of executive agreements and their supremacy over conflicting state laws).
questions.zh-question: 某外国的恐怖分子绑架了美国驻该国大使。他们威胁要杀死她，除非美国总统确保释放一名被确认身份的外国公民，该公民因该州的有效定罪而被关押在美国的一个州监狱中。总统通过与该外国达成一项协议作为回应，协议规定该外国将在指定日期确保释放美国大使，以换取总统采取行动确保释放被关押在州监狱中的该身份确认人员。总统随后命令该州州长释放该囚犯。州长拒绝了。没有适用的联邦成文法。以下哪项是总统在此类情况下，要求州长释放囚犯的权力最强有力的宪法论据？

zh-choices.A: 总统忠实执行法律的职责授权他解决州与联邦利益之间的任何冲突，使得此类事项的裁决完全不可司法审查（nonjusticiable）。
zh-choices.B: 总统任命大使的权力授权他采取任何他认为可取的行动来保护他们免受伤害，因为这些官员一经任命就成为总统的代理人（agents）。
zh-choices.C: 总统处理美国对外事务的权力包括一项全权（plenary authority），可以采取总统认为明智的任何行动来保护我们的外交人员（diplomatic agents）的安全。
zh-choices.D: 总统与外国谈判的权力默示授权他与外国签订行政协议（executive agreements），这些协议优先于州法律。

questions.zh-explanation:
MBE 考点解析

Constitutional Law: Separation of Powers - Foreign Affairs

本题真正考的是

一句话定位考点

本题真正考的是：总统在对外事务中通过执行协定（executive agreement）与外国达成安排时，能否凭其联邦法效力压过冲突的州法，从而要求州长放人。

三秒认题路径：

对外谈判 → 执行协定 → 联邦法效力 → 压过州法 → 选D

核心法律规则

在外交事务（foreign affairs）里，总统的权力最强，考场意思：国家对外要“一个声音”。总统可以代表美国与外国谈判并进入执行协定（executive agreement），这种协定一旦成立，就像联邦法一样生效。

在最高条款（Supremacy Clause）下，执行协定考场意思：只要它和州法冲突，州法就让路，所以州长不能拿州刑事拘押去挡住总统已经承诺的对外安排。

核心判例： Am. Ins. Assoc. v. Garamendi —— 说明总统在外交领域可通过执行协定处理对外承诺，而且其效力可排除冲突州法。

思维导图

题干先看什么？总统是在处理对外事务（foreign affairs），不是普通国内行政。
先找权力来源：总统可谈判并缔结执行协定（negotiate and enter executive agreements）。
再看法律效力：协定一旦成立，按最高条款（Supremacy Clause），像联邦法一样压过冲突州法。
卡死点：不是问州长愿不愿意，而是看州法能不能挡住已生效的对外协定；这里通常挡不住。
结论：总统有最强论证要求州长释放囚犯，答案指向 D。

考点陷阱

你可能会想：总统是在救美国大使，听起来很紧急，所以他应该“想做什么就做什么”。

但考试真正问的是：他有没有一个能压过州法的联邦层级依据。

司法考试看的是「法律程序上能不能救济」，而不是「物理上的秘密有没有泄露」。

所以不要被“保护外交人员”的故事性带偏；真正能撑住命题的是执行协定（executive agreement） + 最高条款（Supremacy Clause），不是泛泛的总统好意。

正确答案与干扰项排除

为什么选 D？

题干的执行协定是总统对外谈判的产物，具有联邦法效力，所以可以压过冲突的州法并支持放人。

❌ 概念混淆 | 执行职责误判

✕ A: 把faithfully execute当成万能冲突处理权了。

❌ 事实误判 | 使节身份误判

✕ B: appoint ambassadors 不等于可随意放人。

❌ 法律适用 | 权力泛化误判

✕ C: 只靠plenary authority太空泛，题目要的是具体对外协定。

这题建议用什么方法？

先锁定外交协定，再问它能否借最高条款直接压过州法。

考场速记

记住：总统在外交事务里最容易拿分的点，就是执行协定（executive agreement）可以当联邦法用。

口诀：“对外先谈协定，冲突州法让路。”

reason.en: Creates the federal-state conflict that must be resolved through federal supremacy.
reason.zh: 产生须依联邦优先原则解决的联邦与州之间的冲突。

B.text: take any action that he may think desirable

C.text: whatever action the President deems wise

reason.en: This language ignores constitutional and legal limits on presidential action.
reason.zh: 该措辞忽视了宪法和法律对总统行动的限制。

reason.zh: 该权力支持总统订立行政协定。

label.zh: 具有约束力的总统国际协定

reason.en: Executive agreements may carry federal legal force without Senate treaty approval.
reason.zh: 行政协定无需参议院条约批准即可具有联邦法律效力。

label.en: federal supremacy over conflicting state law
label.zh: 联邦法优先于冲突州法

reason.en: This supplies the constitutional basis for requiring the governor to release the prisoner.
reason.zh: 这为要求州长释放囚犯提供了宪法依据。

highlights.text: entering into an agreement with the foreign country

reason.en: This activates the President's recognized authority to make executive agreements in foreign affairs.
reason.zh: 该事实触发总统在外交事务中订立行政协定的公认权力。

highlights.text: ordered the governor of the state to release the prisoner in question

reason.en: This presents the precise conflict between the executive agreement and state authority.
reason.zh: 这构成行政协定与州权力之间的直接冲突。

highlights.text: The governor refused

reason.en: The refusal makes federal supremacy and the agreement's preemptive effect central.
reason.zh: 该拒绝使联邦优先原则及协定的排除效力成为核心。

highlights.text: No federal statutes are applicable

reason.en: The President must rely on independent Article II foreign-affairs authority and the executive agreement itself.
reason.zh: 总统必须依赖第二条规定的独立外交权力及行政协定本身。

questions.subject: Constitutional Law
questions.question:
A federal statute imposes a $250 tax on all new motorcycles sold in the United States, with all proceeds of the tax being allocated to a special fund for local police departments in every state to purchase body armor.
Is the statute likely constitutional?

choices.A: No, because equipping local police departments is not one of the enumerated powers of Congress.
choices.B: No, because the tax is not rationally related to the use of the proceeds.
choices.C: Yes, because it is a reasonable exercise of Congress's power to tax and spend.
choices.D: Yes, because providing police officers with body armor is a compelling government interest.

questions.explanation:
Congress's taxing power
Type of tax
Direct (ie, tax on person or property)
  • Apportioned evenly among states
  • Reasonably related to revenue raising
Constitutional
Indirect (eg, sales, excise)
  • Uniformly applied in every state
  • Reasonably related to revenue raising
Constitutional
Export (ie, tax on goods leaving U.S.)
Unconstitutional

The Taxing and Spending Clause (i.e., General Welfare Clause) grants Congress broad authority to raise revenue through taxation. This allows Congress to impose an indirect tax (e.g., sales tax) so long as it is:

  • imposed uniformly in every state where the taxed goods are found and
  • reasonably related to revenue raising on its face.

The General Welfare Clause has been interpreted to permit Congress to exercise power to tax for any public purpose—not just to pursue other enumerated powers within its authority.

Here, Congress enacted a federal statute imposing a $250 tax on all new motorcycles sold within the United States (i.e., an indirect sales tax). It appears that this tax will be imposed uniformly in all states and is reasonably related to raising revenue. Although the purpose of the tax is to allocate proceeds to a special fund for local police departments in every state to purchase body armor, Congress may impose taxes for any public purpose—not just its enumerated powers (Choice A). Therefore, the statute is likely constitutional.

(Choice B) The tax need not be rationally related to the use of the proceeds. Instead, the tax imposed by Congress will generally be upheld if it is reasonably related to revenue raising.

(Choice D) Congress need not demonstrate that providing police with body armor is a compelling government interest because the General Welfare Clause permits Congress to impose taxes for any public purpose.

📌 Educational Objective

The Taxing and Spending Clause allows Congress to impose an indirect tax so long as it is imposed uniformly in every state where the taxed goods are found and reasonably related to revenue raising on its face. This clause permits Congress to exercise power to tax for any public purpose.

📚 References
  • U.S. Const. art. 1, § 8 (the General Welfare Clause).
questions.zh-question:
一项联邦法规对在美国销售的所有新摩托车征收250美元的税，所有税收收益将拨入一个专项基金，用于各州的当地警察部门购买防弹衣。
该法规是否可能符合宪法（constitutional）？

zh-choices.A: 否，因为为当地警察部门配备装备不属于国会的列举权力（enumerated powers）。
zh-choices.B: 否，因为该税收与收益的使用之间没有合理关联（rationally related）。
zh-choices.C: 是，因为这是国会税收和支出权力（power to tax and spend）的合理行使。
zh-choices.D: 是，因为为警察提供防弹衣是一项令人信服的政府利益（compelling government interest）。

questions.zh-explanation:
MBE 考点解析

Constitutional Law: Separation of Powers - Separation of Powers

本题真正考的是

一句话定位考点

本题真正考的是：国会用征税与支出权（Taxing and Spending Clause）给全国摩托车加税，再把钱指定给地方警局买防弹衣，这种税是否仍属合宪的公共目的税。

三秒认题路径：

先看税种 → 再看统一性 → 再看创收性 → 再看公共目的 → 选合宪

核心法律规则

国会的征税与支出权（Taxing and Spending Clause）很宽，考场意思：只要税本身是为了筹资，而且表面上统一适用（uniformly applied），通常就过关。间接税（indirect tax）比如销售税、消费税，重点不是用途写得多漂亮，而是它是不是看起来合理地在revenue raising。而且这条权力不只限于国会其他列举权力（enumerated powers），所以就算钱最后拿去做地方公共项目，也不必先证明那个项目本身属于联邦列举权力。

核心判例：本题逻辑符合对General Welfare Clause的宽泛理解：只要税款设计合理、面向筹资，国会可以为任何公共目的征税。

思维导图

国会这笔钱是怎么收的？
是税，不是处罚：新摩托车每辆加征 250 美元，属于间接税（indirect tax），先看能不能作为筹资工具。
这笔税本身有没有过线？
看统一性：全国新摩托车都收，属于统一适用。
看创收性：表面上和revenue raising有关，就先站得住。
钱最后拿去干什么，能不能毁掉这笔税？
卡死点：用途是买防弹衣，不影响税本身合宪。
国会可为任何公共目的（public purpose）征税，不必局限于自己的列举权力。
最后怎么选？
所以结论：C 合宪

考点陷阱

你可能会想：既然钱是给地方警局买防弹衣，那国会是不是在做一件不属于联邦权限的事。

但考试真正问的是：税本身能不能成立，不是最后花钱的项目像不像联邦列举权力。

司法考试看的是「法律程序上能不能救济」，而不是「物理上的秘密有没有泄露」。

正确答案与干扰项排除

为什么选 C？

题干是全国统一征收的new motorcycles tax，而且表面上用于筹资；国会可为任何公共目的征税，所以合宪。

❌ 概念混淆 | 规则渊源误判

✕ A: 把税的用途误当成列举权力门槛。

❌ 法律适用 | 中间关系误判

✕ B: 盯着 use of the proceeds，但税不要求和花钱方式一一对应。

❌ 事实误判 | 严格审查偷换

✕ D: 把公共目的税硬套成compelling审查。

这题建议用什么方法？

先抓税权门槛，再把“用途好不好”与“税本身合不合宪”分开看。

考场速记

记忆口诀：征税先看税本身，花钱去向不先卡死。联想到 General Welfare Clause 时，先问“统一吗、筹资吗”，别先被资金用途带跑。

questions.subject: Constitutional Law
questions.question:
Congress enacted a statute prohibiting discrimination in the rental of residential property anywhere in the United States on the basis of sexual orientation or preference by any person or entity, public or private.
Which of the following provisions provides the strongest basis for Congress's authority to enact this statute?

choices.A: The commerce clause of Article I, Section 8.
choices.B: The enforcement clause of the Fourteenth Amendment.
choices.C: The general welfare clause of Article I, Section 8.
choices.D: The privileges and immunities clause of Article IV.

questions.explanation:
Commerce Clause challenge
Does federal statute regulate interstate commerce?
People/things
Instrumentalities
Channels
Yes
Constitutional
No
Does federal statute regulate activity that substantially impacts interstate commerce?
Yes
Constitutional
No
Unconstitutional

The commerce clause of Article I, section 8 gives Congress broad regulatory authority over most activities involving two or more states. This includes the power to regulate:

  • the channels of interstate commerce (eg, airports)
  • the instrumentalities of interstate commerce (eg, planes)
  • people and things moving in interstate commerce (eg, commercial shipments) and
  • activities that, singly or in the aggregate, substantially affect interstate commerce (presumed when activity is economic in nature).

Here, Congress enacted a statute prohibiting discrimination based on sexual orientation in the rental of residential property. Since renting is an economic activity, there is a strong presumption that this activity substantially affects interstate commerce. Therefore, the commerce clause provides the strongest basis for Congress's authority to enact this statute to regulate that activity.

(Choice B) Under the Fourteenth Amendment's enforcement clause, Congress can enact legislation to enforce the amendment's other provisions against state actors—but not private actors (eg, residential landlords).

(Choice C) The Article I, section 8 taxing and spending clause (ie, general welfare clause) only empowers Congress to tax and spend for the general welfare—not to prohibit rental discrimination.

(Choice D) The Article IV privileges and immunities clause prohibits states from discriminating against out-of-state citizens by denying them a right of state citizenship. But this clause is a limitation on state power—not a basis for congressional authority.

📌 Educational Objective

The commerce clause grants Congress extensive authority to regulate (1) the channels of interstate commerce, (2) the instrumentalities of interstate commerce, (3) persons and things moving in interstate commerce, and even (4) activities that substantially affect interstate commerce.

📚 References
  • Heart of Atlanta Motel, Inc. v. United States, 379 U.S. 241, 258 (1964) (holding that the commerce clause allows Congress to prohibit racial discrimination by local motels serving travelers).

国会颁布了一项法规，禁止任何个人或实体（无论是公共还是私人）在美国任何地方基于性取向或偏好在住宅物业租赁中进行歧视。
以下哪项条款为国会颁布这项法规的权力提供了最强的依据？

zh-choices.A: 《第一条第八款》的Commerce Clause（商务条款）。
zh-choices.B: 《第十四修正案》的Enforcement Clause（执行条款）。
zh-choices.C: 《第一条第八款》的General Welfare Clause（一般福利条款）。
zh-choices.D: 《第四条》的Privileges and Immunities Clause（特权与豁免条款）。

questions.zh-explanation:
MBE 考点解析

Constitutional Law: Separation of Powers - Commerce

本题真正考的是

一句话定位考点

本题真正考的是：国会能不能用商业条款（Commerce Clause）去管一项看起来是本地住宅租赁、但本质上属于经济活动的私营歧视规则。

三秒认题路径：

私人租赁 → 经济活动 → 影响州际商业 → 商业条款 → 选 A

核心法律规则

国会可以用商业条款（Commerce Clause）管三类东西：州际商业的渠道（channels）、工具（instrumentalities），以及会实质影响州际商业的活动。考场意思：只要题干是在管经济活动（economic activity），通常就很容易落进国会权力范围。

这题的关键是住宅租赁属于经济活动，所以不用硬找宪法第十四修正案，也不用把它塞进税收支出权。考场意思：这里问的是国会有没有立法权，不是州能不能歧视、也不是道德上对不对。

核心判例：Heart of Atlanta Motel, Inc. v. United States — 说明国会可以用商业条款打击会影响州际旅行和交易的歧视。

思维导图

先看：联邦法是不是在管州际商业（interstate commerce）？
是管渠道 / 工具 / 人和货物
直接成立：国会有权力，结论=合宪
不是再看：是不是在管会实质影响州际商业的活动？
本题事实：住宅租赁（rental of residential property） + 歧视（discrimination） = 经济活动
经济活动通常推定会影响州际商业，所以仍然合宪
结论题干不需要第十四修正案，也不需要税收支出权
答案锁定：A

考点陷阱

你可能会想：题干在管“歧视”，是不是应该先想到第十四修正案执行条款（enforcement clause）。

但考试真正问的是：这是不是一个能被国会直接管到的经济活动；只要是私人住宅租赁，商业条款通常就够了。

司法考试看的是「法律程序上能不能救济」，而不是「物理上的秘密有没有泄露」。

正确答案与干扰项排除

为什么选 A？

题干抓的是私人住宅租赁这种经济活动，国会可用商业条款（Commerce Clause）直接规制私人歧视。

❌ 概念混淆 | 私人主体误判

✕ B: 把Fourteenth Amendment当成管私人房东的通用钥匙。

❌ 法律适用 | 支出权误套

✕ C: 看到general welfare就以为能直接禁歧视。

❌ 事实误判 | 权力来源偷换

✕ D: 把privileges and immunities误当成国会授权条款。

这题建议用什么方法？

先抓“国会权力来源”，再问题干是不是经济活动；是的话优先看商业条款。

考场速记

记忆口诀：商业条款（Commerce Clause）先看渠道、工具、人员和货物流动，再看经济活动有没有实质影响州际商业。

这题一句话背法：private rental discrimination + economic activity = Commerce Clause，先选 A，再排 B/C/D。

questions.subject: Constitutional Law
questions.question:
Congress passed a statute prohibiting racial discrimination in the making and enforcing of contracts. A couple applied to have their child admitted to a private elementary school. The school denied the application because their child was Black. The couple, on behalf of their child, brought an action against the school under this statute. In response, the school challenged the constitutionality of the statute.
Is the school's challenge of the statute's constitutionality likely to succeed?

choices.A: No, because the Obligations of Contracts Clause of Article I only applies to state legislation.
choices.B: No, because the Thirteenth Amendment enables Congress to pass this statute.
choices.C: Yes, because the statute interferes in the making of contracts between private parties.
choices.D: Yes, because the statute regulates purely private conduct.

questions.explanation:
Civil War Amendments
Thirteenth Prohibits slavery & involuntary servitude
Fourteenth Prohibits denial of equal protection, due process, or privileges/immunities of national citizenship
Fifteenth Prohibits denial or abridgment of voting rights based on race, color, or previous servitude

The Civil War Amendments (Thirteenth, Fourteenth, and Fifteenth Amendments) contain provisions that authorize Congress to enact appropriate legislation to enforce the civil rights guaranteed therein. The Thirteenth Amendment specifically authorizes Congress to adopt legislation that is rationally related to eliminating the badges or incidents of slavery. This authority has been broadly interpreted to encompass private and government action, including racial discrimination by private home sellers, private schools, and private employers.

Here, the couple brought an action against the private school based on a federal statute prohibiting racial discrimination in the making and enforcing of contracts after their child was denied admission on the basis of race. Although the statute regulates purely private conduct, Congress may enact the statute because it is rationally related to eliminating racial discrimination (Choice D). And because the Thirteenth Amendment enables Congress to pass this statute, the school's challenge of its constitutionality is unlikely to succeed.

(Choice A) The Obligations of Contracts Clause of Article I applies only to state legislation. But under the Thirteenth Amendment, Congress may enact federal legislation to regulate private conduct if it is rationally related to eliminating racial discrimination.

(Choice C) State legislation that substantially impairs a contract between private parties is unconstitutional unless the state can show that the interference was reasonable and necessary to serve an important state interest. However, this provision is inapplicable to federal legislation (as seen here).

📌 Educational Objective

The Thirteenth Amendment authorizes Congress to adopt legislation that is rationally related to eliminating the badges or incidents of slavery. This authority has been broadly interpreted to encompass private and government action, including racial discrimination by private schools.

📚 References
  • Runyon v. McCrary, 427 U.S. 160, 170 (holding that Congress may regulate racial discrimination by private school under the authority of the Thirteenth Amendment).
questions.zh-question:
国会通过了一项成文法，禁止在订立和执行合同中存在种族歧视。一对夫妇申请让他们的孩子进入一所私立小学。该学校因他们的孩子是黑人而拒绝了申请。这对夫妇代表他们的孩子，根据这项成文法对学校提起了诉讼。作为回应，学校质疑该成文法的合宪性。
学校对该成文法合宪性的挑战很可能成功吗？

zh-choices.A: 否，因为宪法第一条的“合同义务条款”（Obligations of Contracts Clause）仅适用于州立法。
zh-choices.B: 否，因为第十三修正案（Thirteenth Amendment）授权国会通过这项成文法。
zh-choices.C: 是，因为该成文法干涉了私人当事人之间订立合同。
zh-choices.D: 是，因为该成文法规制了纯粹的私人行为。

questions.zh-explanation:
MBE 考点解析

Constitutional Law: Separation of Powers - Separation of Powers

本题真正考的是

一句话定位考点

本题真正考的是：国会能否依据第十三修正案（Thirteenth Amendment）授权，禁止私立学校的种族歧视合同行为。

三秒认题路径：

私校歧视 → 联邦法 → 第十三修正案 → 能管私行 → 选 B

核心法律规则

第十三修正案（Thirteenth Amendment）不只是废奴；它还允许国会制定与消除奴隶制的标记或遗产（badges or incidents of slavery）“合理相关”的法律，考场意思：只要目标是打击种族歧视，国会就能管到私人行为。私立学校（private school）、私营雇主、私人卖方都可能落入这个范围。

所以这题里，虽然学校在做的是私人招生决定，但联邦法禁止合同中的种族歧视仍可成立；学校的宪法挑战大概率失败。

核心判例：Runyon v. McCrary — 认可国会可借第十三修正案规制私立学校的种族歧视。

思维导图

先看国会有没有权力管到“私人合同里的种族歧视”？
YES第十三修正案：可为消除种族歧视而立法
题干关键事实：私立学校拒绝黑人儿童入学
法律效果：这属于私人行为，但和消除badges or incidents of slavery有关
结论国会可立法，学校的合宪性挑战失败 → B
NO如果只是普通私人交易、又没有第十三修正案授权，才会去想“国会是不是越权”
本题不是这个路子，直接被第十三修正案挡住

考点陷阱

你可能会想：这只是private conduct，国会怎么能插手？

但考试真正问的是：第十三修正案有没有给国会一个专门入口，而答案是有。

司法考试看的是「法律程序上能不能救济」，而不是「物理上的秘密有没有泄露」。

正确答案与干扰项排除

为什么选 B？

题干私立学校拒绝黑人入学，正落在第十三修正案可规制的私人种族歧视范围内，所以国会能立法。

❌ 概念混淆 | 规则渊源误判

✕ A: 把Obligations of Contracts当成国会授权来源了。

❌ 法律适用 | 联邦错套州规

✕ C: 这是把州宪法的合同审查规则硬搬到联邦立法上。

❌ 事实误判 | 私行即无权误读

✕ D: 看到purely private conduct就以为国会一定不能管。

这题建议用什么方法？

先找国会权力来源，再看它能否触及私人歧视，不要被“私人行为”四个字带偏。

考场速记

记住：第十三修正案（Thirteenth Amendment）能让国会针对“消除奴隶制遗留痕迹”的私人种族歧视立法，像私校招生这种题，先想 Runyon。

速记：第十三修正案管“私下歧视”，不是只管州政府。

questions.subject: Constitutional Law
questions.question:
Congress enacted a statute providing grants of federal funds for the restoration and preservation of courthouses that were built before 1900 and are still in use. The statute contains an inseverable condition requiring that any courthouse restored with the aid of such a grant must be equipped with ramps and other facilities necessary to accommodate physically handicapped people.
A state law requires public buildings in the state to have ramps and other facilities for handicapped people. It exempts from those requirements any building that is more than 70 years old if the State Board of Architects finds that the installation of such facilities would destroy the architectural integrity of the building.
A county courthouse in the state was built in 1895 and is still in use. It does not contain ramps or other special facilities for handicapped people. The State Board of Architects has determined that the installation of those facilities would destroy the architectural integrity of the building. Nevertheless, the county applies for a federal grant to restore and preserve that county's courthouse.
If the county restores the courthouse with the aid of a federal restoration and preservation grant, is the county bound to install ramps and other facilities for handicapped people in that building?

choices.A: No, because any acceptance of this condition by the county would, as a matter of law, be considered to be under duress.
choices.B: No, because the Constitution does not authorize the federal government to direct the actions of the states or any of their political subdivisions with respect to matters affecting their own governmental buildings.
choices.C: Yes, because Congress may impose reasonable conditions related to the public welfare on grants of federal funds to public bodies when the public bodies are free to accept or reject the grants.
choices.D: Yes, because the rights of handicapped and disabled people are fundamental rights that take precedence, as a constitutional matter, over considerations of architectural integrity.

questions.explanation:
Conditional federal funding (Article I, section 8 spending clause)

Conditions must meet all the following criteria:

  • clearly stated & unambiguous
  • reasonably related to federal interest in funded program
  • do not require states to engage in unconstitutional activity
  • do not unduly coerce states into accepting

The taxing and spending clause gives Congress broad discretion to tax and spend for the general welfare (ie, for any public purpose). Congress may use its spending power to incentivize state or local governments to act in certain ways by placing conditions on their receipt of federal funds. But these conditions are only valid if they:

  • are clearly stated and unambiguous so that potential recipients may make an informed decision
  • are reasonably related to the purpose for which the funds will be expended
  • do not require recipients to engage in unconstitutional activity and
  • are not unduly coercive—ie, are not so extreme that they amount to a "gun to the head."

Here, Congress imposed a condition on the receipt of federal grants for the restoration and preservation of historic courthouses (public welfare). That condition is valid—and the county will be bound to that condition if it restores its courthouse with the aid of such a grant—because:

  • it unambiguously requires any courthouse restored with the aid of such a grant to be equipped with facilities for handicapped people
  • installing handicap facilities in courthouses is reasonably related to restoring and preserving those buildings
  • recipients are not required to do anything unconstitutional and
  • being required to install handicap facilities is a relatively minor condition for receiving funds to restore and preserve an entire courthouse (ie, no undue coercion) (Choice A).

(Choice B) Under the Tenth Amendment, the federal government cannot direct states or their political subdivisions (eg, counties) to enact legislation or enforce federal law. But Congress may incentivize them to act through conditional federal funding (as seen here).

(Choice D) Handicapped and disabled people enjoy the same fundamental rights as everyone else—but no such rights are implicated here.

📌 Educational Objective

Conditional federal funding is valid if the conditions (1) are clear and unambiguous, (2) are reasonably related to the purpose for which the funds are expended, (3) do not require recipients to engage in unconstitutional activity, and (4) are not unduly coercive.

📚 References
  • South Dakota v. Dole, 483 U.S. 203, 207–12 (1987) (holding that conditions on states' receipt of federal funds must be unambiguous, related to the purpose of the funding, and noncoercive).

国会颁布了一项法令，为修复和保护1900年前建造且仍在使用的法院提供联邦资金拨款（grants of federal funds）。该法令包含一项不可分割的条件（inseverable condition），要求任何通过此类拨款修复的法院必须配备坡道和其他必要设施，以容纳身体残障人士。

某州法律要求该州的公共建筑必须配备坡道和其他残障人士设施。该法律豁免了任何超过70年历史的建筑，如果州建筑师委员会（State Board of Architects）认定安装此类设施会破坏建筑的建筑完整性（architectural integrity）。

该州某县法院建于1895年，目前仍在投入使用。该法院不包含坡道或其他残障人士专用设施。州建筑师委员会已认定安装这些设施会破坏该建筑的建筑完整性。尽管如此，该县仍申请联邦拨款以修复和保护该县法院。

如果该县在联邦修复和保护拨款的帮助下修复法院，该县是否有义务在该建筑中安装坡道和其他残障人士设施？

zh-choices.A: 否，因为该县接受此条件在法律上将被视为处于胁迫（duress）之下。
zh-choices.B: 否，因为宪法并未授权联邦政府就影响各州或其任何政治分支机构自身政府建筑的事项，指导其行动。
zh-choices.C: 是，因为当公共机构可以自由选择接受或拒绝联邦资金拨款（grants of federal funds）时，国会可以对这些拨款施加与公共福利相关的合理条件。
zh-choices.D: 是，因为残障人士的权利是基本权利（fundamental rights），在宪法层面上优先于对建筑完整性（architectural integrity）的考量。

questions.zh-explanation:
MBE 考点解析

Constitutional Law: Separation of Powers - Taxation And Spending

本题真正考的是

一句话定位考点

本题真正考的是：国会用联邦拨款条件（conditional federal funding）要求州或县接受补助时，是否可以顺便绑定无障碍设施要求。

三秒认题路径：

拨款条件 → 自愿接受 → 条件合理 → 不违宪 → 不胁迫

核心法律规则

税收与支出权（Taxing and Spending Clause）允许国会为了公共福利发放联邦资金，并附带条件。考场意思：州或县可以选择拿钱，也可以选择不拿钱，所以不是“联邦直接命令”。

但条件必须清楚明确（clearly stated and unambiguous），并且和资助项目合理相关（reasonably related）。考场意思：你拿的是修复老法院的钱，国会要求顺便装无障碍设施，和“修复并保存法院”是同一条线。

另外，条件不能要求受领者去做违宪行为（unconstitutional activity），也不能过度胁迫（unduly coercive）。考场意思：这里只是拿补助要多做一点配套改造，不是“枪顶头”的硬逼。

核心判例： South Dakota v. Dole — 联邦拨款条件只要明确、相关、非违宪、不过度胁迫，就可以绑定州政府。

思维导图

先看：这是不是国会直接命令州县去立法？
不是：这是条件性拨款（conditional spending），不是 Tenth Amendment 禁止的直接指挥。
再看：条件有没有过关？
1. 条件写得清楚 → 县知道“拿钱就要装无障碍设施”。
2. 和项目相关 → 资助目的就是修复并保存法院，配套可及性改造合理。
3. 不要求违宪行为 → 只是修缮条件，不是叫它做非法事。
4. 不会胁迫到“没得选”。
卡死点：这里是“拿不拿补助你自己选”，不是 gun to the head。
结论
答：县若接受拨款，就要遵守无障碍设施条件，对应选项 C。

考点陷阱

你可能会想：州法已经给老建筑开了例外，联邦是不是就不能再加条件了。

但考试真正问的是：联邦有没有通过拨款把条件合法地“挂”上去，而不是州法本身愿不愿意放行。

司法考试看的是「法律程序上能不能救济」，而不是「物理上的秘密有没有泄露」。

这里最容易把 联邦诱导（incentivize） 和 联邦强制（commandeer） 混成一团；本题是前者，不是后者。

正确答案与干扰项排除

为什么选 C？

题干的 federal restoration and preservation grant 允许国会附带合理条件；县若自愿接受，就必须装无障碍设施。

❌ 概念混淆 | 规则渊源误判

✕ A: 把自愿接受拨款说成 duress，但这里不是强迫签字。

❌ 法律适用 | 反命令误套

✕ B: 只盯着联邦不能直接命令州，却漏看了条件拨款这条合法路径。

❌ 事实误判 | 基础权利偷换

✕ D: 把无障碍改造硬说成 fundamental rights，题目根本没在考这个。

这题建议用什么方法？

程序姿态优先：先分清是直接命令还是条件拨款，再检查条件是否明确、相关、非违宪且不过度胁迫。

考场速记

记忆口诀：In Certain Circumstances, An Appeal Can Be Made Prematurely 这类口诀是中间上诉例外专用；本题记住另一句就够了：拿钱可以附条件，前提是自愿、明确、相关、不过度胁迫。

questions.subject: Constitutional Law
questions.question:
In order to provide funds for a system of new major airports near the 10 largest cities in the United States, Congress levies a tax of $25 on each airline ticket issued in the United States. The tax applies to every airline ticket, even those for travel that does not originate in, terminate at, or pass through any of those 10 large cities.
Is this tax constitutional as applied to the issuance in the United States of an airline ticket for travel between two cities that will not be served by any of the new airports?

choices.A: No, because the burden of the tax outweighs its benefits for passengers whose travel does not originate in, terminate at, or pass through any of the 10 largest cities.
choices.B: No, because the tax adversely affects the fundamental right to travel.
choices.C: Yes, because an exemption for the issuance of tickets for travel between cities that will not be served by the new airports would deny the purchasers of all other tickets the equal protection of the laws.
choices.D: Yes, because Congress has broad discretion in choosing the subjects of its taxation and may impose taxes on subjects that have no relation to the purpose for which those tax funds will be expended.

questions.explanation:
Congressional taxing power
Type of tax Definition Constitutional requirements
Direct
  • Taxes on persons or their property
  • Payment cannot be avoided
 Allowed if:
  • apportioned proportionately among states
  • reasonably related to revenue production
Indirect
  • Taxes on goods/transactions
  • Payment can be avoided or shifted to another (eg, consumer)
 Allowed if:
  • identical taxation in every state
  • reasonably related to revenue production
Export
  • Taxes on goods/services leaving the country
 Not allowed

The taxing and spending clause grants Congress the broad power to impose indirect taxes on the subject of its choosing. The taxed subject need not have any relation to the purpose for which the tax funds will be spent. Instead, an indirect tax is constitutional as long as it is (1) identical in every state and (2) reasonably related to revenue production.

Here, Congress has imposed a $25 tax on airline tickets. This indirect tax is identical in every state since it applies to all airline tickets issued in the U.S. And the tax is reasonably related to raising revenues for a system of new major airports near the 10 largest cities. Therefore, this tax is constitutional—even as applied to airline tickets for travel between cities that will not be served by the new airports.

(Choice A) Courts do not weigh the burdens and benefits of a tax to determine its constitutionality.

(Choice B) The Fifth Amendment due process clause generally prohibits the federal government from substantially impairing persons' fundamental rights (eg, the right to travel). And though a tax on airline tickets may affect the right to travel, a minimal tax of $25 would not substantially impair this right.

(Choice C) This type of exemption—which does not appear in the tax levied by Congress—may raise equal protection concerns since it treats similarly situated passengers differently. But the exemption would not deny passengers equal protection of the laws since it (1) does not substantially impact a fundamental right or protected class and (2) would likely pass rational basis scrutiny.

📌 Educational Objective

Under the taxing and spending clause, Congress can impose indirect taxes on goods or transactions as long as the taxes are (1) identical in every state and (2) reasonably related to revenue production. This is true even if the taxes have no relation to the purpose for which the funds will be spent.

📚 References
  • Fernandez v. Wiener, 326 U.S. 340, 355–63 (1945) (holding that an IRS inheritance tax is constitutional since it is indirect, identical in every state, and reasonably related to revenue production).

zh-choices.B: 否，因为这项税收不利地影响了基本的旅行权。

questions.zh-explanation:
MBE 考点解析

Constitutional Law: Separation of Powers - Taxation And Spending

本题真正考的是

一句话定位考点

本题真正考的是：国会的征税与支出权（taxing and spending power）能否对间接税（indirect tax）设立一个与具体支出目的无关的统一税种。

三秒认题路径：

统一票税 → 间接税 → 各州一致 → 不看支出用途 → 选 D

核心法律规则

一眼记住的规则

征税与支出条款（Taxing and Spending Clause）给国会很宽的权限：只要税种是 间接税（indirect tax），并且在各州是一样的、还能合理带来收入，就通常合宪。考场意思：它不要求“这笔税的钱必须花在让每位纳税人直接受益的地方”。

直接税（direct tax）要看是否按州比例分摊；但本题的机票税是对交易征收，属于 间接税（indirect tax），所以重点只看“各州是否一致”和“是否为了筹集收入”。

核心判例： Fernandez v. Wiener — 说明间接税只要各州一致、并且合理服务于收入筹集，就不因为资金用途和征税对象不完全对应而失效。

思维导图

先看什么 本题事实 法律关卡 结论
税的性质 对每张机票统一加收 $25 这是对交易征收的 间接税（indirect tax） 进入“间接税”规则
是否各州一致 美国境内所有机票都适用 “每州不同”这条不成立 满足一致性要求
是否要对票客受益 新机场只建在前 10 大城市附近 税收用途不必和每张票的乘客直接对应 不能用“没坐到新机场”推翻税
最后答案 飞往不经过新机场的城市 只要税用于筹集收入，仍可合宪 选 D

考点陷阱

你可能会想：这笔税对没用到新机场的人不公平，所以应该无效。

但考试真正问的是：国会能不能给“机票这种交易”统一征税，不是这笔税是不是按乘客得到的服务来分配。

司法考试看的是「法律程序上能不能救济」，而不是「物理上的秘密有没有泄露」。

这里最容易被 burden outweighs benefits 带偏，但法院不会做这种成本收益平衡来判定税是否合宪。

正确答案与干扰项排除

为什么选 D？

题干的 统一机票税 属于间接税，只要各州一致、且合理用于筹集机场资金，就不要求和每位乘客的航线直接对应。

❌ 事实误判 | 成本收益偷换

✕ A: 把 burden outweighs benefits 当成合宪标准了。

❌ 法律适用 | 权利受损夸大

✕ B: 机票税只是轻微影响 right to travel，没到实质剥夺。

❌ 概念混淆 | 平等保护乱套

✕ C: 题干根本没设 equal protection 例外，不能拿虚构豁免来判税无效。

这题建议用什么方法？

先认税种，再看是否各州一致，最后直接排除“用途不对应就无效”的想法。

考场速记

记住一句话：间接税（indirect tax）看“统一 + 为筹资”，不看“每个纳税人是否直接受益”。

记忆口诀：“In Certain Circumstances, An Appeal Can Be Made Prematurely” 是中间上诉例外口诀；但这题不是上诉题，别把它套进来。

questions.subject: Constitutional Law
questions.question:
The United States found itself involved in a foreign conflict. Congress enacted a statute that established a military court in a foreign country to determine if individuals captured in an active combat zone should be classified as enemy combatants and detained until the cessation of hostilities. The statute provides that the military court may hear evidence presented by the captured individual at its discretion.
A man, a U.S. citizen, was captured in an active combat zone and tried by the military court. After the government presented its evidence, the court determined that the man was an enemy combatant and ordered that he be detained until the end of hostilities. The man was not permitted to provide a defense.
The man seeks to overturn his detention in a habeas corpus proceeding in a federal district court, claiming that the statute is unconstitutional as applied to him.
How is the federal court likely to rule in this action?

choices.A: It will set aside the military court's ruling, because Congress has no enumerated power to establish military courts.
choices.B: It will set aside the military court's ruling, because the man was entitled to a fair opportunity to rebut the government's factual assertions before a neutral decision-maker.
choices.C: It will uphold the military court's ruling, because an individual in a foreign country does not possess constitutional rights.
choices.D: It will uphold the military court's ruling, because federal courts do not have jurisdiction to review decisions issued by military courts.

questions.explanation:

Constitutional

The necessary and proper clause allows Congress to take actions that are reasonably necessary to carry out its enumerated Article I powers. Congress may therefore establish military courts and tribunals to carry out its enumerated powers to regulate the military and make rules regarding captures on land and sea (Choice A). Congress may grant military courts jurisdiction over enemy combatants, enemy civilians, and current members of the U.S. military.*

However, Congress must afford procedural due process to U.S. citizens classified and detained as enemy combatants. Procedural due process requires that U.S. citizens be given:

  • • notice of the factual basis for the citizen's classification as an enemy combatant and
  • • a fair opportunity to rebut the government's factual assertions before a neutral decision-maker.

A U.S. citizen detained as an enemy combatant who does not receive these protections may file a petition for a writ of habeas corpus in a federal court unless Congress has explicitly suspended the writ (not seen here). The federal court has jurisdiction to then set aside an unlawful detention (Choice D).

Here, the man was captured in an active combat zone and classified as an enemy combatant by the military court. The statute gives the military court the discretion whether to allow a captured individual to provide evidence in his/her defense. However, the man is entitled to rebut the government's factual assertions because he is a U.S. citizen. Since the military court did not provide the man that opportunity, the statute is unconstitutional as applied to him. Therefore, the federal court will likely set aside the military court's ruling.

*Military courts and tribunals do not have jurisdiction over U.S. civilians who are not classified as enemy combatants unless hostilities have forced state and federal civilian courts to close.

(Choice C) U.S. citizens, including citizens in foreign countries, always possess constitutional rights.

📌 Educational Objective

Congress may establish military courts and tribunals but must afford U.S. citizens classified as enemy combatants procedural due process. This requires (1) notice of the factual basis for the citizen's classification and (2) a fair opportunity to rebut those facts before a neutral decision-maker.

📚 References
  • U.S. Const. art. I, § 8, cl. 14 (power to make rules regarding capture).
  • Hamdi v. Rumsfeld, 542 U.S. 507, 533 (2004) (O'Connor, J., plurality) (holding that detained U.S. citizens seeking to challenge enemy combatant status are entitled to procedural due process).

美国卷入了一场对外冲突。国会颁布了一项法令，在外国设立了一个军事法庭，以确定在活跃战区捕获的个人是否应被归类为敌方战斗人员（enemy combatants），并拘留直至敌对行动停止。该法令规定，军事法庭可酌情听取被俘人员提交的证据。
一名美国公民在活跃战区被捕，并由该军事法庭审理。在政府提交证据后，法庭认定该男子为敌方战斗人员，并命令将其拘留直至敌对行动结束。该男子未被允许提供辩护。
该男子在联邦地区法院提起人身保护令（habeas corpus）程序，寻求推翻其拘留，声称该法令对他适用时违宪（unconstitutional as applied to him）。
联邦法院在此诉讼中可能如何裁决？

zh-choices.A: 它将撤销军事法庭的裁决，因为国会没有设立军事法庭的列举权力（enumerated power）。
zh-choices.B: 它将撤销军事法庭的裁决，因为该男子有权在中立的决策者面前获得公平机会反驳政府的事实主张。
zh-choices.C: 它将维持军事法庭的裁决，因为个人在外国不享有宪法权利。
zh-choices.D: 它将维持军事法庭的裁决，因为联邦法院没有管辖权（jurisdiction）审查军事法庭作出的裁决。

questions.zh-explanation:
MBE 考点解析

Constitutional Law: Separation of Powers - War And Defense Powers

本题真正考的是

一句话定位考点

本题真正考的是：国会可以设军事法庭审查敌对分子，但美国公民被贴上 enemy combatant（敌对战斗员） 标签后，仍有 procedural due process（程序性正当程序），不能只让政府说完就直接关起来。

三秒认题路径：

军事法庭 → 美国公民 → 不准辩驳 → 程序正当性 → 设定扣押

核心法律规则

国会可以依据 Necessary and Proper Clause（必要且适当条款），建立军事法庭来配合其 war powers（战争权） 和对俘获人员的管理权，考场意思：“能不能设这个法庭” 这一步通常不是问题。

但如果被扣押的是美国公民，政府必须给他 notice（通知），并给他在 neutral decision-maker（中立裁判者） 面前反驳政府事实指控的机会。考场意思：不是听没听见，而是能不能反驳。

所以本题的关键不是军事法庭有没有存在权限，而是这个人被认定为敌对战斗员后，是否真的拿到了 fair opportunity to rebut。没有这个机会，按正当程序就要被推翻。

核心判例： Hamdi v. Rumsfeld —— 美国公民若被当作敌对战斗员拘押，必须获得对事实基础的通知和反驳机会。

思维导图

先问：这是不是“国会能不能设军事法庭”的问题？
第1层：国会有战争权 + 必要且适当条款 → 能设军事法庭，不是卡点
再问：被扣的人是谁？
如果是美国公民：不是“人在国外就没宪法权利”。
程序要求：通知事实基础 + 在中立裁判者前反驳政府事实。
最后卡死点：他有没有得到“反驳机会”？
没有被允许辩护 → 程序性正当程序缺失 → 关押裁定应被撤销
结论：联邦法院可在 habeas corpus 中纠正这项不合法拘押。

考点陷阱

你可能会想：既然是在外国战区抓到的，而且军事法庭已认定他是敌对战斗员，那联邦法院就别再管了。

但考试真正问的是：美国公民被剥夺自由时，程序上有没有给他反驳政府事实的机会；司法考试看的是「法律程序上能不能救济」，而不是「物理上的秘密有没有泄露」。

“人在国外”只影响战场背景，不会自动抹掉美国公民的宪法程序保护。

正确答案与干扰项排除

为什么选 B？

题干 不准他提交辩护，正打到 procedural due process（程序性正当程序） 的核心：美国公民必须能反驳政府事实，所以军事法庭裁定会被撤销。

❌ 概念混淆 | 权力来源误判

✕ A: 把国会的设庭权误当成不能审查。

❌ 事实误判 | 国籍权利偷换

✕ C: 看到 foreign country 就以为没宪法保护。

❌ 法律适用 | 管辖结论搬错

✕ D: 联邦法院能用 habeas 纠正非法拘押。

这题建议用什么方法？

先看是不是美国公民，再看有没有给事实通知和反驳机会，最后才决定能否救济。

考场速记

记忆口诀：美国公民 + 敌对战斗员 = 要通知 + 要反驳；别被“战区”二字带跑，先抓程序正当程序。

本题不是在考军事权力有多大，而是在考：政府把人关起来之前，能不能先让他说话。

questions.subject: Constitutional Law
questions.question:
Congress passed a statute directing the United States Forest Service, a federal agency, to issue regulations to control campfires on federal public lands and to establish a schedule of penalties for those who violate the new regulations. The statute provides that the Forest Service regulations should "reduce, to the maximum extent feasible, all potential hazards that arise from campfires on Forest Service lands."
The Forest Service issued the regulations and the schedule of penalties directed by Congress. The regulations include a rule that provides for the doubling of the fine for any negligent or prohibited use of fire if the user is under the influence of alcohol or drugs.
Which of the following arguments best supports a finding that the rule providing for the fines is constitutional?

choices.A: The executive branch of government, of which the Forest Service is part, has inherent rule-making authority over public lands.
choices.B: The rule is justified by a compelling government interest in safeguarding forest resources.
choices.C: The rule relates directly to law enforcement, which is an executive rather than a legislative function, and hence it does not need specific congressional authorization.
choices.D: The rule was issued pursuant to a valid exercise of Congress's power to delegate rule-making authority to federal agencies.

questions.explanation:
Nondelegation doctrine

Congress delegated:
Exclusive legislative power
Examples:
  • making/repealing laws
  • declaring war
  • impeaching federal officers
Incidental legislative power
Examples:
  • rulemaking
  • carrying out legislation
  • enforcing regulations
Yes
Yes
Unconstitutional
No
Congress provided
intelligible principle defining:
  • policy it seeks to advance
  • agency carrying out policy
  • scope of agency's authority

The nondelegation doctrine prohibits Congress from delegating its exclusive legislative powers (eg, making or repealing laws). But Congress can delegate its incidental powers (eg, rule-making authority) if it provides an intelligible principle—ie, a clear statement defining:

  • the policy Congress seeks to advance (eg, reduce campfire hazards on Forest Service lands)
  • the agency to carry out that policy (eg, the United States Forest Service) and
  • the scope of that agency's authority (eg, issue campfire regulations and establish a penalty schedule).

Since Congress properly delegated its rule-making authority to the United States Forest Service, its rule doubling the fine for a fire if the user is under the influence of alcohol or drugs is likely constitutional.

(Choice A) The Article IV property clause gives Congress (not the executive branch) inherent rule-making authority over federal lands. But Congress can delegate this incidental power to executive agencies.

(Choice B) The rule would only have to be justified by a compelling government interest—ie, satisfy strict scrutiny—if it substantially impacted a fundamental right or intentionally discriminated against a suspect class (not seen here).

(Choice C) Although law enforcement is an executive function, it must be exercised pursuant to congressional authorization (ie, federal law).

📌 Educational Objective

Congress can delegate incidental legislative powers to federal agencies if it provides an intelligible principle—ie, a clear statement defining (1) the policy Congress seeks to advance, (2) the agency to carry out that policy, and (3) the scope of that agency's authority.

📚 References
  • Gundy v. United States, 139 S. Ct. 2116, 2123 (2019) (explaining that the nondelegation doctrine allows Congress to delegate power as long as it provides an intelligible principle to guide the delegate's use of discretion).
