questions.subject: Constitutional Law
questions.question:
A valid treaty between the United States and a foreign country provides for the elimination of all tariff barriers between the two countries. It authorizes the president of either country to issue a proclamation nullifying any state or local laws in that country that have the effect of impeding imports from the other country.
The foreign country uses the metric system of measurement, and thus all goods produced there and exported to the United States are packaged in metric sizes, such as liters and kilograms. A law of a state in the United States requires all goods sold in that state to be packaged in traditional American sizes, such as quarts or pounds. Because the state law substantially impedes imports from the foreign country, the President of the United States has issued a proclamation nullifying the state law pursuant to the treaty.
Is the President's proclamation valid?

choices.A: No, because the Constitution vests in Congress the exclusive authority to specify binding legal standards for weights and measures, and the President therefore lacks constitutional authority for the proclamation.
choices.B: No, because the principles of federalism embedded in the Constitution prohibit the President from taking action to invalidate a state law.
choices.C: Yes, because it is authorized by a valid treaty of the United States and is not prohibited by any provision of the Constitution and, therefore, is the supreme law of the land.
choices.D: Yes, because the President has inherent authority to nullify any state law that substantially impedes commerce between the United States and another country.

questions.explanation:
Treaty-making process
President negotiates & enters treaty
Senate gives advice & may approve with 2/3 vote
Treaty signed & ratified

Article II gives the President extensive power over foreign policy and international relations—including the power to negotiate and enter into treaties with foreign nations. But a treaty cannot be ratified (ie, signed into law) until it has been approved by a two-thirds Senate vote (no action by the House of Representatives required). It then becomes valid and binding on the federal and state governments:

  • immediately, if the treaty is self-executing—ie, contains explicit enforcement provisions (as seen here)—or
  • after implementing legislation or judicial action, if the treaty is non-self-executing—ie, lacks explicit enforcement provisions.

And under the supremacy clause, an executed treaty supersedes any conflicting state law so long as the treaty is consistent with other constitutional provisions.

Here, the President issued a proclamation nullifying a state law that substantially impeded imports from a foreign country. This proclamation was authorized by an explicit enforcement provision in a self-executing treaty between the U.S. and the foreign nation. And since the proclamation is not prohibited by any constitutional provision, it is the supreme law of the land and nullifies the state law.

(Choice A) Article I, section 8 gives Congress the exclusive authority to specify standards for weights and measures. The President's proclamation does not interfere with that authority because it was merely used to eliminate a state-imposed packaging requirement—not to adjust national measurement standards.

(Choice B) The principles of federalism allocate power between the federal and state governments. But federalism does not prohibit the President from invalidating state laws pursuant to a federal statute or treaty (as seen here).

(Choice D) The President has no inherent authority to nullify a state law that substantially impedes commerce between the U.S. and another country. But the President can do so if authorized by Congress (eg, under its commerce power) or a valid treaty (as seen here).

📌 Educational Objective

A treaty must be approved by a two-thirds vote in the Senate (not the House of Representatives) before it can be ratified. Once this occurs, the treaty takes precedence over any conflicting state law pursuant to the supremacy clause.

📚 References
  • Medellin v. Texas, 552 U.S. 491, 526–30 (2008) (explaining the President's powers to implement self-executing and non-self-executing treaties).
  • Ware v. Hylton, 3 U.S. 199, 236–37 (1796) (declaring that treaties take precedence over conflicting state laws).
questions.zh-question:
美国与某外国之间的一项有效条约规定，两国之间应消除所有关税壁垒。该条约授权任一国家的总统发布公告，废止该国任何具有阻碍从另一国进口效果的州或地方法律。
该外国使用公制计量系统，因此所有在该国生产并出口到美国的商品均以公制尺寸包装，例如升和千克。美国某州的法律要求在该州销售的所有商品必须以传统的美国尺寸包装，例如夸脱或磅。由于该州法律严重阻碍了从该外国的进口，美国总统已根据该条约发布公告，废止了该州法律。
总统的公告是否有效？

zh-choices.A: 否，因为宪法赋予国会专属权力来规定具有约束力的度量衡法律标准，因此总统缺乏发布该公告的宪法授权。
zh-choices.B: 否，因为宪法中蕴含的联邦制（federalism）原则禁止总统采取行动使州法律失效。
zh-choices.C: 是，因为它获得了美国有效条约的授权，且未被宪法任何条款所禁止，因此是国家的最高法律（supreme law of the land）。
zh-choices.D: 是，因为总统拥有固有权力废止任何严重阻碍美国与其他国家之间贸易的州法律。

questions.zh-explanation:
MBE 考点解析

Constitutional Law: Separation of Powers - Foreign Affairs

本题真正考的是

一句话定位考点

本题真正考的是：有效条约（valid treaty）能不能依照至上条款（Supremacy Clause）压过冲突的州法，以及总统是否能按条约授权发布废除州法的公告。

三秒认题路径：

先看条约是否有效 → 再看是否自执行 → 再看州法是否冲突 → 再看总统是否被授权 → 选能压州法的答案

核心法律规则

条约（treaty）先由总统谈判并达成，再经参议院三分之二同意（two-thirds Senate vote）后才成文生效；国会众议院不参与这个批准门槛。自执行条约（self-executing treaty）一旦有效，就可以直接产生联邦法效果；如果条约和州法冲突，且条约没有违宪，州法要让路。

考试上你要抓的是：总统这里不是凭空“管州法”，而是按照有效条约里明确给他的执行权去发公告，所以这不是联邦主义禁止的问题。supremacy clause 的意思很直接：联邦有效法源一旦覆盖到同一件事，冲突州法就失效。

核心判例：Medellín v. Texas 和 Ware v. Hylton 一起锁定本题：有效条约可以优先于冲突州法，而自执行条约可以直接被执行。

思维导图

先问：这是不是一个有效条约（valid treaty）授权总统处理州法的题？
YES
再问：条约是否已按宪法程序成立并可执行？
是
再问：州法是否和条约直接冲突、并妨碍进口？
是
州法被条约和总统公告压下去
结论：选 C
NO / 误判点
别被“weights and measures是国会管的”带跑：本题不是改全国计量标准，而是清除州级包装门槛。

考点陷阱

你可能会想：既然州法是在管商品包装，那是不是只有国会才能碰，或者总统根本不能动州法。

但考试真正问的是：总统是不是在有效条约授权下处理冲突州法，而不是在单独创设全国计量标准。

司法考试看的是「法律程序上能不能救济」，而不是「物理上的秘密有没有泄露」。

正确答案与干扰项排除

为什么选 C？

题干已经给出valid treaty和总统按条约发公告的前提；有效条约一旦与州法冲突，就能依至上条款（Supremacy Clause）压过州法。

❌ 概念混淆 | 规则渊源误判

✕ A: 把weights and measures当成本题核心，忽略这里不是在改全国标准。

❌ 法律适用 | 联邦主义泛化

✕ B: 以为联邦主义当然挡住总统，其实条约授权下联邦法本来就能压州法。

❌ 事实误判 | 固有权力偷换

✕ D: 把inherent authority硬塞给总统，题干明明靠的是条约授权，不是固有权力。

这题建议用什么方法？

先抓权力来源，再看是否有有效条约压州法，别被“州规制包装”这种背景噪音带偏。

考场速记

记忆口诀：有效条约 + 至上条款 = 冲突州法退让。遇到总统按条约发公告的题，先问条约是否有效，再问州法是否直接冲突。

reason.en: A valid treaty may operate as supreme federal law.
reason.zh: 有效条约可以作为具有最高效力的联邦法律。

reason.en: The President acts under express treaty authority rather than inherent power.

label.zh: 基于条约的州法优先排除

reason.en: This explicit enforcement mechanism makes the treaty self-executing as applied here.

reason.en: The state law satisfies the treaty's condition for presidential action.
reason.zh: 该州法满足条约规定的总统行动条件。

reason.en: This links the proclamation directly to valid treaty authority.
reason.zh: 该表述将公告直接与有效条约授权相联系。

A.text: exclusive authority to specify binding legal standards for weights and measures

reason.en: The proclamation removes a packaging restriction rather than setting national measurement standards.
reason.zh: 该公告仅取消包装限制，并未制定全国度量衡标准。

reason.zh: 联邦主义不能使与具有最高效力的有效联邦条约相冲突的州法继续有效。

B.text: prohibit the President from taking action to invalidate a state law

reason.en: This overstates federalism by disregarding valid federal authorization.
reason.zh: 该表述无视有效联邦授权，夸大了联邦主义的限制。

reason.en: This identifies the constitutional source of the President's authority.
reason.zh: 该表述指出了总统权力的宪法依据。

C.text: not prohibited by any provision of the Constitution

reason.en: A treaty cannot override an independent constitutional prohibition.
reason.zh: 条约不能推翻独立的宪法禁止性规定。

reason.en: A valid self-executing treaty supersedes conflicting state law.
reason.zh: 有效且可直接执行的条约优先于相冲突的州法。

label.zh: 无依据的总统固有权力

reason.en: The President requires treaty or statutory authorization to nullify the state law here.
reason.zh: 总统在本案中需要条约或联邦法律授权才能使州法失效。

label.zh: 过度宽泛的州法废止权

reason.en: The President has no general power to nullify every state law affecting foreign commerce.
reason.zh: 总统并无废止所有影响对外商业州法的一般权力。

reason.zh: 仅有商业影响并不会产生总统的固有权限。

highlights.text: A valid treaty between the United States and a foreign country

reason.en: Validity permits the treaty to receive Supremacy Clause effect.
reason.zh: 条约有效是其获得最高法律效力的前提。

highlights.text: authorizes the president of either country to issue a proclamation nullifying any state or local laws

label.zh: 可直接执行的条约条款

reason.en: This express enforcement provision authorizes presidential implementation without additional legislation.
reason.zh: 这一明确执行条款授权总统无需额外立法即可实施条约。

highlights.text: the state law substantially impedes imports from the foreign country

reason.en: The law's effect brings it within the treaty's nullification provision.
reason.zh: 该州法的效果使其落入条约废止条款的范围。

highlights.text: issued a proclamation nullifying the state law pursuant to the treaty

reason.en: The President followed the treaty's specified enforcement mechanism.
reason.zh: 总统采用了条约规定的执行机制。

questions.subject: Constitutional Law
questions.question:
In order to reduce the federal deficit, Congress enacted a statute imposing a five percent national retail sales tax. The tax was levied upon all retail sales in the United States and applied equally to the sales of all kinds of goods.
Is this tax constitutional as applied to retail sales of newspapers?

choices.A: No, because retail sales taxes are within the taxing power of the states.
choices.B: No, because the imposition of a tax on the sale of newspapers violates the freedom of the press.
choices.C: Yes, because it is within Congress's power to tax.
choices.D: Yes, because the tax is necessary to serve the compelling interest of balancing the federal budget.

questions.explanation:
Congress's taxing power

Type of tax
Direct
(ie, tax on person or property)
  • Apportioned evenly among states
  • Reasonably related to revenue raising
Constitutional
Indirect
(eg, sales, excise)
  • Uniformly applied in every state
  • Reasonably related to revenue raising
Constitutional
Export
(ie, tax on goods leaving U.S.)
Unconstitutional

The taxing and spending clause (ie, general welfare clause) gives Congress broad authority to raise revenue through taxation. This includes the power to impose indirect taxes (eg, sales tax) if they are applied equally in every state AND are reasonably related to revenue production—as seen here.

But a tax also must respect other constitutional provisions—including the First Amendment freedom of the press. The retail sales tax does so here because it is generally applicable to all goods and in no way targets press operations (Choice B). And since the sales tax does not implicate any other constitutional provisions, it is a constitutional exercise of Congress's taxing power—even as applied to retail sales of newspapers.

(Choice A) Retail sales taxes are within the taxing power of the states as well as Congress's enumerated taxing power.

(Choice D) The tax need not be necessary to serve a compelling interest because it is generally applicable and does not target the press.

📌 Educational Objective

Indirect taxes must be applied equally in every state and reasonably related to revenue production. And such taxes cannot violate any other constitutional provision—eg, by targeting the press in violation of the First Amendment.

📚 References
  • Leathers v. Medlock, 499 U.S. 439, 447 (1991) (holding that the government may not exercise its taxing power to single out the press or target small groups of speakers).
questions.zh-question: 为了减少联邦赤字，国会颁布了一项法规，征收一项5%的全国零售销售税。该税适用于美国境内的所有零售销售，并平等地适用于各类商品的销售。当这项税适用于报纸的零售销售时，它是否合宪？

zh-choices.A: 否，因为零售销售税属于各州的征税权 (taxing power)。
zh-choices.B: 否，因为对报纸销售征税侵犯了新闻自由 (freedom of the press)。
zh-choices.C: 是，因为这属于国会的征税权 (power to tax)。
zh-choices.D: 是，因为该税是必要的，以服务于平衡联邦预算的“强制性利益” (compelling interest)。

questions.zh-explanation:
MBE 考点解析

Constitutional Law: Separation of Powers - Taxation And Spending

本题真正考的是

一句话定位考点

本题真正考的是：国会的全国零售销售税是否属于 间接税（indirect tax），只要全国统一适用、以筹措收入为目的，就通常合宪，且不会因为卖的是报纸就自动失效。

三秒认题路径：

全国销售税 → 间接税 → 统一适用 → 以筹款为目的 → 看是否另犯宪法

核心法律规则

《征税与支出条款》（taxing and spending clause）给国会很宽的征税权。像 零售销售税（sales tax） 这种 间接税（indirect tax），只要在各州 uniformly applied，并且和 revenue raising 有合理关联，通常就是合宪。

但征税权不是“万能钥匙”：如果税专门针对报纸或媒体，才可能碰到第一修正案；本题的税是对所有商品一体适用，所以不会因为 newspapers 这个对象而失效。

核心判例： Leathers v. Medlock — 政府不能借征税去单挑新闻出版者；但对所有商品一体适用的税，一般仍可成立。

思维导图

先看：这是不是 征税权（taxing power） 的题？
是全国零售销售税，属于 间接税（indirect tax），先过“能不能征”的门。
再看是否 uniformly applied 且以 revenue raising 为目的。
这两点都满足，所以征税权这关通过。
最后卡点：会不会单挑报纸、压新闻自由？
不会。税对所有零售商品都一样，不是专门盯着 press。
结论：能征，而且对报纸的零售销售也合宪，选 C。

考点陷阱

你可能会想：卖的是报纸，就会碰到 freedom of the press，所以应该直接判违宪。

但考试真正问的是：这项税是不是在程序上专门挑报纸下手。这里它是对所有商品一体适用，不是在“点名打压媒体”。

司法考试看的是「法律程序上能不能救济」，而不是「物理上的秘密有没有泄露」。

正确答案与干扰项排除

为什么选 C？

题干的 five percent national retail sales tax 是全国统一的间接税，目的又是筹措联邦收入，所以国会有权征；它对报纸零售也同样适用。

❌ 概念混淆 | 职权来源误判

✕ A: 把零售税当成州税了，忽略联邦也有 taxing power。

❌ 法律适用 | 媒体定向误判

✕ B: 看到 newspapers 就自动套新闻自由，但这里税没点名压制报纸。

❌ 事实误判 | 审查强度偷换

✕ D: 把一般征税硬扯成 compelling interest 审查，本题不用这套。

这题建议用什么方法？

先判税种与适用范围，再检查有没有专门针对受保护言论的定向打击。

考场速记

记住这句：全国统一的 indirect tax 通常合宪；只有税在“点名”压某个受保护群体时，才会出问题。

顺手记口诀：In Certain Circumstances, An Appeal Can Be Made Prematurely 适合中间上诉题；但本题不是上诉题，核心仍是“统一适用 + 筹款目的 + 不定向打压”。

reason.en: Correctly identifies the tax type but does not limit the power to the states.

A.text: within the taxing power of the states

B.text: tax on the sale of newspapers

reason.zh: 正确承认国会有权征收统一且用于筹集收入的销售税。

questions.subject: Constitutional Law
questions.question:
A man mailed thousands of letters to individuals residing in his state that falsely claimed that the individuals were delinquent on their state tax payments. The letters further stated that the individuals needed to send a set amount of money to the listed address in order to avoid criminal prosecution. One of the individuals who received this letter contacted a federal agency. After investigating, the federal government charged the man with violating a federal statute that prohibits mailing misleading or false materials to obtain money.
At trial, the man argues that Congress had no authority to enact the federal statute and that the statute is a violation of his free speech rights protected by the First Amendment.
Is the court likely to find the statute constitutional?

choices.A: No, because although Congress may regulate mail sent interstate, it lacks the power to regulate mail sent intrastate.
choices.B: No, because the statute violates the man's First Amendment rights.
choices.C: Yes, because Congress has the power to provide for the general welfare, and the statute directly advances and is narrowly tailored to achieve a substantial government interest.
choices.D: Yes, because Congress has the power to regulate the mail, and the letters are not constitutionally protected speech.

The necessary and proper clause allows Congress to take actions that are reasonably necessary to carry out its enumerated Article I powers. As a result, Congress may regulate and restrict what is sent through the mail to carry out its enumerated power to establish post offices and post roads (as seen here). However, Congress must comply with other constitutional provisions when exercising this power, including the First Amendment free speech clause.

Under the free speech clause, Congress may freely regulate and restrict materials containing (1) unprotected speech or (2) commercial speech that is false or misleading or concerns unlawful activity. Here, the man's letters are false commercial speech because they falsely claimed that the individuals were delinquent on their state tax payments and needed to pay money to avoid criminal prosecution. As a result, the letters are not protected by the First Amendment, and the court will likely find the statute constitutional (Choice B).

(Choice A) Congress has the power to regulate mail sent interstate (ie, between two or more states) as well as mail sent intrastate (ie, within a state).

(Choice C) Congress has the power to spend for the general welfare, but this power does not apply here since the federal statute is not a spending measure. Additionally, the statute need not directly advance or be narrowly tailored to achieve a substantial government interest. This intermediate level of First Amendment scrutiny only applies to commercial speech that is true, is not misleading, and concerns a lawful activity (not seen here).

📌 Educational Objective

Congress has broad power to establish post offices and post roads, including regulating and restricting what may be sent by mail. When exercising this power, Congress does not violate the First Amendment free speech clause by restricting unprotected speech OR commercial speech that is false or misleading or concerns unlawful activity.

📚 References
  • U.S. Const. art. I, § 8, cl. 7 (power to establish post offices).
  • U.S. Postal Serv. v. Council of Greenburgh Civic Ass'ns, 453 U.S. 114, 126 (1981) (explaining that Congress cannot exercise its postal power in a manner that violates the First Amendment).
  • Cent. Hudson Gas & Elec. Corp. v. Pub. Serv. Comm'n, 447 U.S. 557, 566 (1980) (stating that false and misleading commercial speech is not protected by the First Amendment).

在审判中，该男子辩称国会无权制定该联邦成文法，并且该法侵犯了他受第一修正案（First Amendment）保护的言论自由权。
法院是否可能认定该法合宪？

zh-choices.A: 否，因为尽管国会可以规制州际邮件，但它缺乏规制州内邮件的权力。
zh-choices.B: 否，因为该法侵犯了该男子的第一修正案（First Amendment）权利。
zh-choices.C: 是，因为国会拥有为公共福利提供保障的权力，并且该法直接促进并严格限制以实现重大的政府利益。
zh-choices.D: 是，因为国会拥有规制邮件的权力，并且这些信件不属于受宪法保护的言论。

questions.zh-explanation:
MBE 考点解析

Constitutional Law: Separation of Powers - Regulation Of Content

本题真正考的是

一句话定位考点

本题真正考的是：国会用邮政权管邮件时，能不能禁止虚假商业言论（false commercial speech），以及这种邮件是否属于第一修正案保护范围。

三秒认题路径：

邮寄行为 → 虚假索钱 → 非保护言论 → 可管邮件 → 法规合宪

核心法律规则

邮政权（postal power）考场意思：国会可以为建立邮局、邮路去管“信件怎么寄、寄什么”。但它行使这个权力时，仍要受第一修正案（First Amendment）约束。

商业言论（commercial speech）考场意思：如果内容是虚假或误导（false or misleading），或者本来就在帮违法活动，政府可以直接禁止，不用再做中间审查。

这题里，信件谎称收件人欠税，还催他们寄钱躲避刑事追诉，所以它不是受保护的好言论，国会据此禁止这类邮件，通常会被认定合宪。

核心判例： Cent. Hudson Gas & Elec. Corp. v. Pub. Serv. Comm'n — 虚假或误导的商业言论不受第一修正案保护；U.S. Postal Serv. v. Council of Greenburgh Civic Ass'ns — 邮政权不能违反第一修正案，但可以管邮件内容。

思维导图

收到的是不是“可受保护的言论”？
先看内容：这是虚假商业言论（false commercial speech），而且还借邮件要钱。
第一关：不是“真话且合法活动”的商业言论，所以直接掉出保护范围。
卡死点：effectively reviewable 这种思路不适用；这里根本不是要做中间审查，而是先判定它不受保护。
国会权限：可用邮政权（postal power）管邮件内容，尤其是防止用邮件骗钱。
结论能不能上？
答案：能。因为被禁的是不受保护的虚假商业言论，法规合宪。

考点陷阱

你可能会想：既然邮件是在州内寄出，国会是不是只能管州际邮件，或者这题要套中间审查（intermediate scrutiny）。

但考试真正问的是：这类信件到底是不是受第一修正案保护的商业言论；一旦它是虚假或误导（false or misleading），政府就能直接管。

司法考试看的是「法律程序上能不能救济」，而不是「物理上的秘密有没有泄露」。

正确答案与干扰项排除

为什么选 D？

题干抓到的是虚假索钱的邮件，这属于不受保护的商业言论；国会又能用邮政权管邮件内容，所以法规合宪。

❌ 事实误判 | 州内外混淆

✕ A: 把intrastate当成不能管，忽略邮政权本来就能管州内邮件。

❌ 概念混淆 | 保护范围误判

✕ B: 看到言论就想套第一修正案，但这类false or misleading 不受保护。

❌ 法律适用 | 中间审查误套

✕ C: 把general welfare 和中间审查硬搬来，但本题不是支出法案。

这题建议用什么方法？

先判言论是否受保护，再看国会的邮政权能不能直接管到这类虚假商业邮件。

考场速记

记住：虚假或误导的商业言论（false or misleading commercial speech） 先出局，国会管邮件内容时不必再做中间审查。

口诀：“先看是不是受保护，再看国会有没有权；假话骗钱的邮件，通常可以直接禁。”

reason.en: Requires determining whether the false commercial letters are protected speech.

questions.subject: Constitutional Law
questions.question:
A spending bill originated in the Senate and was narrowly passed by both houses of Congress. The bill appropriated federal funds to be used solely to subsidize municipal services. The bill included a provision that prohibited the use of federal funds to subsidize public libraries, which were found to operate at large losses.
Congress presented the bill to the President, who supports the use of federal spending to subsidize municipal services. However, the President does not support the prohibition on library funding and does not want that provision to become law. After the bill was presented to the President, both houses of Congress adjourned for 15 days.
Which of the following provides the best way for the President to prevent the provision from becoming law?

choices.A: Assert executive privilege.
choices.B: Impound the funds.
choices.C: Line-item veto the provision.
choices.D: Take no action .

questions.explanation:
Federal legislative process
(requirements for legislative action)
Bill proposed in Congress
Bicameralism
Bill passes both houses
Presentment
President
signs bill
President
vetoes bill
President takes
no action
Congress overrides
(two-thirds vote)
10 days elapse
during session
Bill becomes law

When Congress (ie, the House and Senate) passes a bill, the bill must be presented to the President for approval or disapproval. Once Congress presents a bill to the President, the President has 10 days (excluding Sundays) to act. During this time period, the President has three options:

  • sign the bill into law
  • veto the bill, but Congress can override that veto by a two-thirds vote in both houses or
  • take no action.

If the President takes no action, then the bill becomes law if Congress is in session at the end of the 10-day period. But if Congress is adjourned during that time period, then the bill will not become law.* The President's failure to act in this situation cannot be overridden by Congress and is known as a "pocket veto."

Here, the appropriations bill passed by Congress and presented to the President contains a provision that the President opposes. Since both houses of Congress will still be adjourned when the President's 10-day deadline to act on the bill expires, taking no action will result in the bill not becoming law. And since Congress cannot override a "pocket veto," this is the best way for the President to prevent the provision from becoming law.

*This is because when Congress is adjourned, the President cannot return the bill to its originating house (eg, the Senate) as required by the Constitution.

(Choice A) Executive privilege prevents the disclosure of the President's and executive branch's confidential documents and communications made in performance of official duties and responsibilities. However, this privilege does not prevent the provision from becoming law.

(Choice B) Article II obligates the President to take care that the laws are faithfully executed. As a result, the President cannot refuse to spend (ie, impound) appropriated funds as specifically directed in the law (as seen here).

(Choice C) The President's veto power permits the President to veto an entire bill—not amend or repeal particular provisions of laws passed by Congress. Therefore, the President cannot line-item veto the provision.

📌 Educational Objective

When Congress presents a bill to the President, the President has 10 days to act. If the President takes no action and Congress is adjourned during that 10-day period, the bill does not become law and the President's inaction cannot be overridden.

📚 References
  • U.S. Const. art. I, § 7, cl. 2 (veto power).
  • The Pocket Veto Case, 279 U.S. 655, 691–92 (1929) (holding that the adjournment of Congress prevented the President from returning a bill within 10 days of its presentment, which resulted in the bill being vetoed).
questions.zh-question:
一项支出法案在参议院发起，并以微弱优势在国会两院通过。该法案拨款联邦资金，专门用于补贴市政服务。法案中包含一项条款，禁止使用联邦资金补贴公共图书馆，因为这些图书馆被发现运营亏损严重。
国会将法案提交给总统，总统支持使用联邦支出补贴市政服务。然而，总统不支持禁止图书馆拨款的规定，不希望该条款成为法律。法案提交给总统后，国会两院休会15天。
以下哪项是总统阻止该条款成为法律的最佳方式？

zh-choices.A: 主张行政特权 (executive privilege)。
zh-choices.B: 扣留资金 (impound the funds)。
zh-choices.C: 对该条款行使逐项否决权 (line-item veto)。
zh-choices.D: 不采取任何行动。

questions.zh-explanation:
MBE 考点解析

Constitutional Law: Separation of Powers - Domestic Power

本题真正考的是

一句话定位考点

本题真正考的是：国会把法案送到总统后，总统想阻止其中一项拨款限制生效，最稳的做法是不是什么都不做，让它在国会休会时触发 口袋否决（pocket veto）。

三秒认题路径：

法案已送达 → 国会休会 → 10天未满 → 看口袋否决 → 选不作为

核心法律规则

当国会通过法案并完成 呈交（presentment） 后，总统有 10 天（不算星期日）可以签署、否决，或者 不作为（take no action）。考场意思：总统不是想“改一条”，而是只能决定这部法案进不进法律门。

如果总统选择不作为，而国会在这 10 天内 休会（adjourned），法案就不会成为法律，这就是 口袋否决（pocket veto）。考场意思：国会休会时，总统没法把法案退回原院，因此国会也没法覆盖这个否决。

line-item veto（逐项否决） 不能用来删掉法案里的单个条款；impound（扣留拨款） 也不能违背国会已经指定的拨款用途。executive privilege（行政特权） 只管保密，不管这条款能不能生效。

核心判例： The Pocket Veto Case — 国会休会使总统无法在 10 天内正式退回法案，所以不作为会让法案无法成为法律。

思维导图

法案已送达总统后，先问：国会还在开会吗？
YES：总统 10 天内可以签署或否决；若不作为，法案通常会成为法律。
NO：国会已休会，法案无法退回原院，不作为 = pocket veto。
题干锁定：两院在 15 天内都已休会，所以总统最有效的动作不是“删条款”，而是take no action。
结论：这条禁止图书馆拨款的条款不会成为法律，答案对应 D。

考点陷阱

你可能会想：总统既然不喜欢这条 provision，那就找个工具把它单独删掉。

但考试真正问的是：总统有没有办法让这条款根本别变成法律，而不是等它生效后再想办法绕开。

司法考试看的是「法律程序上能不能救济」，不是「总统主观上能不能讨厌这条款」。

正确答案与干扰项排除

为什么选 D？

题干已完成 presentment，且国会 15 天内休会；总统在 10 天内 不作为（take no action），就会触发 pocket veto，这最能阻止该条款成为法律。

❌ 概念混淆 | 规则渊源误判

✕ A: 把 executive privilege 当成立法否决工具了。

❌ 法律适用 | 扣留权限误判

✕ B: 想用 impound 拒绝花钱，但总统不能违背已拨付用途。

❌ 事实误判 | 逐项删改误判

✕ C: 把 line-item veto 当成现成权力；联邦总统没有这招。

这题建议用什么方法？

先看法案有没有已送达，再看国会是否休会；只要休会窗口成立，就优先想到 pocket veto。

考场速记

记忆口诀：“送达后 10 天，总统不动作；国会若休会，法案进不了门。”

遇到中间否决题，先记 In Certain Circumstances, An Appeal Can Be Made Prematurely；但本题不是上诉，是 presentment + pocket veto。

reason.en: Identifies the chamber to which a vetoed bill ordinarily must be returned.
reason.zh: 确定总统通常应将被否决法案退回的议院。

questions.subject: Constitutional Law
questions.question:
Because of a sudden and unanticipated severe shortage of heating fuel, the President has ordered all offices of federal executive agencies to be open only four days per week. The President's order allows an exception to the extent that emergency circumstances require different hours of operation (as in the case of federal hospitals).
When Congress enacted the appropriations statute for operating all federal executive agencies, its members assumed that the offices of those agencies would be open five days per week, but Congress did not include such a requirement in its appropriations statute or in any other statute.
Is the President's order constitutional?

choices.A: No, because the heads of the various executive agencies have final responsibility for the operation of those agencies' offices.
choices.B: No, because when they passed the statute appropriating monies for the operation of executive agencies, members of Congress assumed that those agencies' offices would be open five days per week.
choices.C: Yes, because the Constitution vests the President with plenary authority to direct the administration of all federal agencies in any manner the President deems expedient.
choices.D: Yes, because the order relates to the management of the executive branch and is not prohibited by any statute.

questions.explanation:
Article II gives the President a wide range of powers, which includes the power to manage federal executive agency operations by issuing executive orders. But Congress can limit those powers when these two branches share authority over a particular area (e.g., executive agencies). When this occurs, the Youngstown framework is used to determine the extent of the President's authority to act by considering whether there was congressional:

  • authorization – in which case the President had maximum authority to act and that act is likely valid
  • silence – in which case the act is valid so long as it (1) fell within the President's Article II powers and (2) did not interfere with another branch's powers or
  • opposition – in which case the President had minimal authority to act and that act is likely invalid.

Here, the President ordered all federal executive agency offices to be open only four days per week. Although Congress had assumed that agency offices would be open five days per week, it remained silent by not including such a requirement in any statute (Choice B). And since the order falls within the President's Article II power to manage executive agencies and does not interfere with another branch's powers, the order is constitutional.

(Choice A) The heads of executive agencies have final responsibility for the operation of those agencies' offices. But this does not affect the constitutionality of the President's order since agency heads must comply with operational requirements validly imposed by Congress or the President when fulfilling that responsibility.

(Choice C) The President does not have plenary (i.e., absolute) authority to direct the administration of federal agencies in any manner the President deems expedient. Instead, the President must comply with the Constitution and relevant federal statutes.

📌 Educational Objective

When Congress has remained silent about the President's actions, those actions are valid so long as (1) they fall within the President's Article II powers and (2) do not interfere with another branch's powers.

📚 References
  • Youngstown Sheet & Tube Co. v. Sawyer, 343 U.S. 579, 635–38 (1952) (Jackson, J., concurring) (setting forth the tripartite framework for analyzing the constitutionality of presidential actions).

questions.zh-explanation:
MBE 考点解析

Constitutional Law: Separation of Powers - Domestic Power

本题真正考的是

一句话定位考点

本题真正考的是：总统在国会沉默时，能否用 行政命令（executive order） 管理联邦行政机关的办公安排。

三秒认题路径：

国会没写死 → 总统发命令 → 管理机关 → 看 Article II → 选 D

核心法律规则

Youngstown 三层看法

题目先看 总统权力（presidential power） 有没有国会配合。授权（authorization） 时，总统最强；沉默（silence） 时，只要命令落在 Article II 的管理权限内，且不撞到别的分支，就通常有效；反对（opposition） 时，总统最弱，通常无效。

这题里，关的是联邦行政机关怎么开门办公，属于总统管理行政部门的范围，而且国会没有用任何法规禁止，所以答案是有效。plenary authority 不是这里的规则；总统不是想怎么管都行，而是要看宪法和国会有没有拦住他。

核心判例： Youngstown Sheet & Tube Co. v. Sawyer — Jackson 法官的三分法告诉你：国会沉默时，先看总统是不是在 Article II 里。

思维导图

国会有没有明确禁止总统这样改办公时间？
YES进入 反对区（opposition），总统权限最弱，通常无效。
NO本题是国会 沉默（silence），继续看两步。
1. 这是不是总统 Article II 里的行政管理？
是，这里是管联邦机关办公安排，不是碰国会专属领域。
2. 有没有撞到别的分支权力或成文法？
没有，国会只是“以为”五天开放，但没写进法条。
结论命令有效，选 D

考点陷阱

你可能会想：国会当初“默认”办公室应当五天开放，所以总统不能改成四天。

但考试真正问的是：国会有没有明确立法限制，以及总统的命令是不是还落在 行政管理（management of the executive branch） 里。

司法考试看的是「法律程序上能不能救济」，而不是「物理上的秘密有没有泄露」。

这题里，国会只是没写，没有把想法变成法律，所以这个“默认”不够挡住总统。

正确答案与干扰项排除

为什么选 D？

题干 Congress did not include such a requirement，所以国会只是沉默；总统又是在管行政机关办公安排，没被任何成文法禁止，故命令有效。

❌ 概念混淆 | 机构职责误判

✕ A: 把机关负责人当成唯一决策者，忽略总统也能管行政运作。

❌ 事实误判 | 默认当成命令

✕ B: 只是“以为”五天开门，不等于国会真的下了 statute 限制。

❌ 法律适用 | 绝对权力误判

✕ C: 把总统说成想怎么管都行，夸大成 plenary authority。

这题建议用什么方法？

先找国会态度，再把命令放进 Youngstown 的沉默区，看有没有 Article II 依据和成文法禁令。

考场速记

记住一句：国会沉默 + 总统在 Article II 范围内 + 没有别的法条拦住，通常就能过。

口诀：In Certain Circumstances, An Appeal Can Be Made Prematurely 是中间上诉例外的记法；但这题不是上诉题，重点还是 Youngstown 三分法。

questions.subject: Constitutional Law
questions.question:
The President issued an executive order in an effort to encourage U.S. citizens to use the metric (Celsius) system of temperatures. Section 1 of the executive order requires the U.S. Weather Bureau, a federal executive agency, to state temperatures only in Celsius in all weather reports. Section 2 of the executive order requires all privately owned federally licensed radio and television stations giving weather reports to report temperatures only in Celsius. No federal statute is applicable.
Is the President's executive order constitutional?

choices.A: Section 1 is constitutional, but section 2 is not.
choices.B: Section 2 is constitutional, but section 1 is not.
choices.C: Sections 1 and 2 are constitutional.
choices.D: Sections 1 and 2 are unconstitutional.

(Youngstown framework)

Article II gives the President, as the country's chief executive, the authority to direct the actions of federal executive agencies (eg, the U.S. Weather Bureau). However, Congress also has authority over these agencies under the nondelegation doctrine, so the President must act with congressional approval or in a manner consistent with an act of Congress. And since there is no applicable statute that conflicts with the executive order, section 1 of that order is constitutional (Choices B & D).

Additionally, the President generally has no Article II authority to direct the actions of persons outside of the executive branch (eg, privately owned companies) without congressional approval. There are no circumstances presented in the facts that might justify an exception to this general rule (eg, a sudden attack on the United States). Therefore, section 2 of the executive order is unconstitutional (Choices B & C).

📌 Educational Objective

When the President and Congress share authority over a particular area, the President's Article II powers must be exercised with congressional approval or in a manner that is consistent with an act of Congress.

📚 References
  • Youngstown Sheet & Tube Co. v. Sawyer, 343 U.S. 579, 635–38 (1952) (Jackson, J., concurring) (setting forth the tripartite framework for analyzing the constitutionality of presidential actions).

questions.zh-explanation:
MBE 考点解析

Constitutional Law: Separation of Powers - Domestic Power

本题真正考的是

一句话定位考点

本题真正考的是：总统能不能用行政命令管到联邦行政机关和私营持证广播台，这要分成“对内有效”和“对外无权”两段看。

三秒认题路径：

联邦机关 → 总统可管 → 私营公司 → 需授权 → 只一段有效

核心法律规则

总统作为 行政首长（chief executive），可以指挥联邦行政机关，所以对 U.S. Weather Bureau 这类机关的命令，先看有没有国会反对；题干说没有相关联邦法冲突，因此这一段通常有效。

但对 私营持证公司（privately owned federally licensed stations），总统一般没有 Article II 权力直接下令，除非国会授权或出现特别紧急情形；本题没有这些救命条件，所以第二段无效。

核心判例： Youngstown Sheet & Tube Co. v. Sawyer — 国会默许时，总统对行政机关的命令可能有效；对国会没给权、也没紧急例外的外部主体，则通常无权硬管。

思维导图

总统命令是否有 Article II 依据？
先看对内：对象是联邦行政机关
国会是否在这块和总统共享权力？
题干事实：没有可适用的联邦法冲突
卡死点：国会未反对，且命令只管行政机关 → 这一段通常有效
第1段：Weather Bureau 只用 Celsius → A
再看对外：对象是私营持证广播台
国会有授权这类外部命令吗？
题干事实：没有法定授权，也没有紧急例外
卡死点：对外部私营主体直接下令 → 通常无权 → 这一段无效
第2段：私营广播台只用 Celsius → D

考点陷阱

你可能会想：既然总统想推广公制，那两段命令看起来都像在“管理天气信息”，应该一起有效。

但考试真正问的是：总统有没有权直接管到主体类型不一样的对象。 对联邦机关是内部指挥，对私营公司是外部命令，后者没国会授权就卡住。

正确答案与干扰项排除

为什么选 A？

题干 Section 1 针对联邦行政机关，国会又没有冲突法，所以上段有效；Section 2 针对私营持证广播台，总统缺少直接命令权，所以下段无效。

❌ 概念混淆 | 对内对外错分

✕ B: 把 private stations 当成也能被总统内部指挥。

❌ 法律适用 | 全有效想当然

✕ C: 以为只要是总统推动政策，两个 weather reports 都能统一管。

❌ 事实误判 | 忽略对象差异

✕ D: 把联邦机关这段也误判成没权，漏掉总统对行政机关的内部指挥力。

这题建议用什么方法？

先分对象，再看国会是否授权；只要一段是联邦机关内部指挥，另一段是对私营主体外部下令，答案常常会分开判。

考场速记

记住这句：总统管 行政机关（executive agencies） 比较稳，管 私营主体（private actors） 先找国会授权。

本题最稳的速记是：“对内看默许，对外看授权；没授权就别把总统权力往外扩。”

questions.subject: Constitutional Law
questions.question:
The vaccination of children against childhood contagious diseases (such as measles, diphtheria, and whooping cough) has traditionally been a function of private doctors and local and state health departments. Because vaccination rates have declined in recent years, especially in urban areas, the President proposes to appoint a Presidential Advisory Commission on Vaccination which would be charged with conducting a national publicity campaign to encourage vaccination as a public health measure.
No federal statute authorizes or prohibits this action by the President.
The activities of the Presidential Advisory Commission on Vaccination would be financed entirely from funds appropriated by Congress to the Office of the President for "such other purposes as the President may think appropriate."
May the President constitutionally create such a commission for this purpose?

choices.A: No, because Congress has not specifically authorized the creation and support of such a new federal agency.
choices.B: No, because the protection of children against common diseases by vaccination is a traditional state function and, therefore, is reserved to the states by the Tenth Amendment.
choices.C: Yes, because the President has plenary authority to provide for the health, safety, and welfare of the people of the United States.
choices.D: Yes, because this action is within the scope of executive authority vested in the President by the Constitution, and no federal statute prohibits it.

Assessing the validity of presidential actions
(Youngstown framework)
Is President's action
authorized under Article II?

Article II gives the President the power to manage the executive branch. Pursuant to this power, the President can use congressional funds to create advisory commissions that will recommend and promote policies. Congress can limit the President's powers when they share authority over an area (eg, use of federal funds). The Youngstown framework is then used to determine the extent of the President's authority. And when Congress is silent, the President's action is valid so long as it:

  • falls within the President's Article II powers and
  • does not interfere with another branch's powers.

Here, the President proposes an advisory commission that would encourage vaccination and be financed entirely from funds already appropriated for Presidential use. Congress is silent on the President's proposal since no federal statute authorizes or prohibits it. And since the President is acting within the scope of his Article II executive authority and is not interfering with another branch's powers, he may constitutionally create the commission.

(Choice A) Specific congressional authorization is not needed since the President is establishing an advisory commission—not a new federal agency with rule-making powers (eg, Securities and Exchange Commission).

(Choice B) All powers that the Constitution does not expressly give to the federal government—including the police power to protect children against common diseases—are reserved to the states by the Tenth Amendment. But the President has the power to establish advisory commissions on traditional state functions like protecting child welfare.

(Choice C) The President does not have plenary (ie, absolute) authority to provide for the health, safety, and welfare of the people of the United States. Instead, the President must comply with the Constitution and relevant federal statutes.

📌 Educational Objective

When Congress has remained silent about the President's actions in an area over which they share authority, those actions are valid so long as they (1) fall within the President's Article II powers and (2) do not interfere with another branch's powers.

📚 References
  • Youngstown Sheet & Tube Co. v. Sawyer, 343 U.S. 579, 635–38 (1952) (Jackson, J., concurring) (setting forth the tripartite framework for analyzing the constitutionality of presidential actions).

zh-choices.B: 否，因为通过疫苗接种保护儿童免受常见疾病侵害是一项传统的州职能，因此根据《第十修正案》（Tenth Amendment），该职能保留给各州。
zh-choices.C: 是，因为总统拥有全权（plenary authority）为美国人民的健康、安全和福祉提供保障。
zh-choices.D: 是，因为此项行动属于宪法赋予总统的行政权力（executive authority）范围之内，且没有联邦法规禁止。

MBE 考点解析

Constitutional Law: Separation of Powers - Separation of Powers

本题真正考的是

一句话定位考点

本题真正考的是：当国会对总统设立 顾问委员会（advisory commission） 这件事保持沉默时，总统能不能只靠 Article II 权力去做。

三秒认题路径：

国会沉默 → 总统建机构 → 无禁令 → Article II → 通常有效

核心法律规则

这题用的是 Youngstown framework：先看总统行为是不是落在 Article II（考场意思：总统固有权限）里面。Congress silent（国会沉默） 时，只要总统没踩进别的部门权力范围，行动通常有效。

这里的关键不是“这件事重不重要”，而是“总统有没有权做、有没有碰到别的分支”。总统只是用已拨款去设一个宣传性质的顾问委员会，不是造一个有规则制定权的新机关，所以可以成立。

核心判例： Youngstown Sheet & Tube Co. v. Sawyer — 这道题要你用它的三分法判断：国会沉默时，先看总统是否在 Article II 内，且没有干扰别的分支。

思维导图

总统要不要先问“国会有没有明确授权”?
先看：是否有 Article II 权力基础？
有 设顾问委员会 → 用既有拨款做宣传
卡点：国会只是沉默，不是明确反对；而且委员会没有规则制定权。
再看：是否干扰其他分支？
没有 结论：可以成立
如果国会明确禁止或总统越权
结论就会掉到无效区。

考点陷阱

你可能会想：这涉及儿童疫苗，听起来像 police power，所以应该是州的事。

但考试真正问的是：总统能不能在国会沉默时，利用自己的 executive authority 设一个宣传性顾问委员会。

司法考试看的是「法律程序上能不能救济」，而不是「物理上的秘密有没有泄露」。

正确答案与干扰项排除

为什么选 D？

题干的关键是 no federal statute authorizes or prohibits，说明国会沉默；总统又只是设宣传性委员会，所以落在 Article II 允许范围内。

❌ 概念混淆 | 规则渊源误判

✕ A: 以为没特别授权就一定不能设委员会，混淆了“新机构”与“顾问组织”。

❌ 事实误判 | 州权偷换

✕ B: 把疫苗话题直接偷换成州的警察权，忽略了题目问的是总统能否设委员会。

❌ 法律适用 | 总统权限夸大

✕ C: 误把总统说成有 plenary authority，题目并没有给这么大的绝对权力。

这题建议用什么方法？

先看国会是授权、沉默还是反对，再把总统动作放进 Youngstown 的第一格或第二格。

考场速记

记住一句：国会沉默 + 总统在 Article II 内 + 不碰别的分支 = 通常有效。这题不是问“州有没有管疫苗的传统权力”，而是问“总统有没有资格做这件事”。

questions.subject: Constitutional Law
questions.question:
In response to a terrorist attack that occurred within the United States, Congress authorized the President to use military force against nations, organizations, and persons the President determined were responsible for the attack. Pursuant to this authorization, enemy combatants were seized in a foreign country and transported to a foreign location under the de facto control of the United States, which was well outside the area of military activity. The President ordered that a military tribunal be convened in that location to try the enemy combatants.
Prior to the attack, Congress, pursuant to its constitutional authority, had authorized the use of military tribunals and set out procedures to guarantee specific basic rights that the tribunals must provide, such as the right of a defendant to hear the evidence against him. The procedural rules for the military tribunal established by the presidential order did not provide for those basic rights.
Does the President have the constitutional authority to convene this military tribunal?

choices.A: No, because a military tribunal only has power over current members of the U.S. armed forces.
choices.B: No, because the procedures adopted for the President's military tribunal conflict with the procedures adopted by Congress.
choices.C: Yes, because Congress authorized the President to use military force that led to the seizure of the enemy combatants.
choices.D: Yes, because the President has plenary power over military tribunals as commander in chief.

questions.explanation:
Assessing the validity of presidential actions
(Youngstown framework)
Is President's action
authorized under Article II?
Does Congress share
power in this area?
Did Congress
authorize action?
No Valid
Yes
No Invalid
Yes
What has Congress done?
Valid
Authorized action
Remained silent
Opposed action
Likely valid
Middle zone
Likely invalid

Article II grants the President constitutional authority over a wide range of domestic and foreign policy areas, including serving as commander in chief of the U.S. military. Congress also has authority over military matters, including the power to establish military courts and tribunals. When these coequal branches of government share power, the Youngstown framework determines whether the President acted within his/her constitutional authority. This framework considers whether there was congressional:

  • authorization – in which case the President had maximum authority to act and that act is likely valid
  • silence – in which case the act is valid so long as it (1) fell within the President's Article II powers and (2) did not interfere with another branch's powers or
  • opposition – in which case the President had minimal authority to act and that act is likely invalid.

Here, Congress authorized the use of military tribunals and set out procedures to guarantee defendants specific basic rights. However, these rights were not included in the President's executive order that provided procedural rules for a tribunal to try certain enemy combatants. Since the congressional authorization and the executive order are in opposition, the President does not have the constitutional authority to convene this military tribunal.

(Choice A) A military tribunal can exercise jurisdiction over current members of the U.S. armed forces as well as enemy combatants and enemy civilians.

(Choice C) Although Congress authorized the President to use military force that led to the seizure of the enemy combatants, Congress also guaranteed specific basic rights to defendants tried in a military tribunal. Since the executive order did not include these rights, the President cannot convene the tribunal.

(Choice D) The President, acting as the commander in chief, does not have plenary (ie, exclusive) power over military tribunals. Instead, the President shares this power with Congress and must abide by congressional requirements.

📌 Educational Objective

The President has minimal constitutional authority to act when Congress opposes the President's actions in an area over which the executive and legislative branches share authority.

📚 References
  • Youngstown Sheet & Tube Co. v. Sawyer, 343 U.S. 579, 635–38 (1952) (Jackson, J., concurring) (setting forth the tripartite framework for analyzing the constitutionality of presidential actions).
  • Hamdan v. Rumsfeld, 548 U.S. 557, 613 (2006) (holding that a military tribunal created by an executive order is invalid when the procedures that will govern the tribunal contravene existing federal law).

为应对发生在美国境内的恐怖袭击，国会授权总统对总统认定对袭击负责的国家、组织和个人使用军事力量。根据这项授权，敌方战斗人员在某外国被抓获，并被运送到一个实际由美国控制的外国地点，该地点远在军事活动区域之外。总统命令在该地点召开军事法庭审判这些敌方战斗人员。
在袭击发生之前，国会根据其宪法权力，已经授权使用军事法庭，并规定了程序以保障军事法庭必须提供的特定基本权利，例如被告听取对其不利证据的权利。总统命令设立的军事法庭的程序规则并未提供这些基本权利。
总统是否有宪法权力召开这个军事法庭？

zh-choices.A: 否，因为军事法庭仅对美国武装部队的现役成员拥有管辖权。
zh-choices.B: 否，因为总统军事法庭所采用的程序与国会所采用的程序相冲突。
zh-choices.C: 是，因为国会授权总统使用军事力量，从而导致了敌方战斗人员的抓获。
zh-choices.D: 是，因为总统作为总司令对军事法庭拥有全权。

questions.zh-explanation:
MBE 考点解析

Constitutional Law: Separation of Powers - Separation of Powers

本题真正考的是

一句话定位考点

本题真正考的是：总统在国会已经规定军法审判程序时，能不能用自己那套相冲突的规则去成立军事法庭。

三秒认题路径：

国会先立规 → 总统另起炉灶 → 程序冲突 → Youngstown 第三档 → 无权

核心法律规则

先看国会是在支持还是反对

当总统和国会都能碰到同一块权力时，要用 Youngstown framework（Youngstown 框架） 来看总统有没有权力，考场意思：先别急着看总统身份高不高，要先看国会站哪边。

如果国会已经 authorized action（授权行为），总统最强；如果国会 remained silent（保持沉默），要再看是否落在 Article II（宪法第二条） 里；如果国会已经 opposed action（明确反对），总统权力最低，考场意思：这时总统不能自己改规则硬上。

本题里，国会虽然允许动用军事法庭，但还明确给了被告基本程序保障；总统命令却把这些保障拿掉了，所以不是“国会没说话”，而是“国会已经说不行”。

核心判例： Youngstown Sheet & Tube Co. v. Sawyer 和 Hamdan v. Rumsfeld 一起锁定本题：总统命令只要撞上国会既有程序要求，就不能靠“军事需要”自己改掉。

思维导图

总统这一步，是不是在国会已经管到的领域里“另起一套军事法庭”?
先问：国会有没有先授权同类军事法庭？
有，而且还写了底线：被告要听到证据、要有基本程序保障。
总统命令：把这些保障拿掉，自己订规则。
Youngstown 第三档：国会反对时，总统权力最弱，不能靠 Commander in Chief（总司令） 身份把国会要求踢开。
卡死点：程序规则相冲突 = 国会反对 = 不能立刻合法成立该军事法庭。
结论：选 B，因为总统没有宪法授权去用与国会相冲突的程序召集该法庭。

考点陷阱

你可能会想：国会都授权打击敌人了，总统当然可以顺手设军事法庭。

但考试真正问的是：国会有没有同时给这类法庭设程序底线；有的话，总统不能把底线删掉再说自己有权。

司法考试看的是「法律程序上能不能救济」，而不是「物理上的秘密有没有泄露」。

正确答案与干扰项排除

为什么选 B？

国会已授权军事法庭并设定基本程序，而总统命令把这些 basic rights 拿掉，属于正面冲突，所以总统不能这样召集法庭。

❌ 概念混淆 | 管辖对象误判

✕ A: 把军事法庭想成只管现役军人，偷换了它也能审敌对战斗员。

❌ 法律适用 | 授权范围误读

✕ C: 只看到 military force，没看到国会对审判程序也下了限制。

❌ 事实误判 | 权力独占偷换

✕ D: 把总司令权看成 plenary power，但军法法庭不是总统单独说了算。

这题建议用什么方法？

先判国会态度，再看总统是否与既有程序冲突，直接落入 Youngstown 第三档。

考场速记

记住：国会先立规，总统后改戏，改到和国会冲突时，答案通常就是无权。

遇到总统权力题，先背一句：Youngstown 看国会是授权、沉默还是反对；反对时，总统最弱。

questions.subject: Constitutional Law
questions.question:
A federal statute with inseverable provisions established a new five-member National Prosperity Board with broad regulatory powers over the operation of the securities, banking, and commodities industries, including the power to issue rules with the force of law. The statute provides for three of the board members to be appointed by the President with the advice and consent of the Senate. They serve seven-year terms and are removable only for good cause. The other two members of the board were designated in the statute to be the respective general counsel of the Senate and House of Representatives Committees on Government Operations. The statute stipulated that they were to serve on the board for as long as they continued in those positions.
Following all required administrative procedures, the board issued an elaborate set of rules regulating the operations of all banks, securities dealers, and commodities brokers. A securities company, which was subject to the board's rules, sought a declaratory judgment that the rules were invalid because the statute establishing the board was unconstitutional.
In this case, should the court rule that the statute establishing the National Prosperity Board is constitutional?

choices.A: No, because all members of federal boards exercising executive powers must be appointed by the President or in a manner otherwise consistent with the appointments clause of Article II.
choices.B: No, because all members of federal boards having broad powers that are quasi-legislative in nature, such as rulemaking, must be appointed by Congress.
choices.C: Yes, because the necessary and proper clause authorizes Congress to determine the means by which members are appointed to boards created by Congress under its power to regulate commerce among the states.
choices.D: Yes, because there is a substantial nexus between the power of Congress to legislate for the general welfare and the means specified by Congress in this statute for the appointment of board members.

questions.explanation:
Appointment of federal officers
(Art. II, § 2 appointments clause)
Type Examples Appointment
Principal
  • Ambassador
  • Supreme Court justice
  • Cabinet official
 Appointed by President (with Senate approval)
Inferior
  • Independent counsel
  • Judicial clerk
  • Administrative law judge
 Appointed by President (with Senate approval) unless Congress delegates appointment to:
  • President alone
  • federal courts or
  • heads of executive departments

Federal officers are persons who:

  • hold a continuing public office (eg, for a term of years) and
  • have significant discretionary authority to administer and/or enforce laws (ie, executive powers).

All federal officers must be appointed by the President or in a manner otherwise consistent with the Article II appointments clause. Under this clause, Congress cannot appoint federal officers.

Here, the National Prosperity Board comprises three members who serve seven-year terms and two who serve indefinitely—all of whom hold a continuing public office. And they all exercise executive powers since they have significant discretionary authority to issue rules with the force of law. As a result, they are federal officers who must be appointed by the President or in a manner otherwise consistent with the appointments clause. And since the applicable statute allows Congress to appoint two members, it is unconstitutional.

(Choice B) Congress may appoint persons to exercise quasi-legislative powers that are investigative or informative in nature. But in Buckley v. Valeo, the Supreme Court held that rulemaking is an administrative power that can only be exercised by federal officers (who can never be appointed by Congress).

(Choice C) The necessary and proper clause authorizes Congress to enact laws that are reasonably appropriate to carry out its express powers—including the power to regulate commerce among the states. But Congress cannot violate other constitutional provisions when doing so.

(Choice D) Article I, section 8 grants Congress the power to tax and spend for the general welfare. But Congress is not taxing or spending here, so this power does not apply.

📌 Educational Objective

Federal officers are persons who hold a continuing public office AND have significant discretionary authority to administer and/or enforce laws (ie, executive powers). They can only be appointed by the President or in a manner otherwise consistent with the Article II appointments clause—never by Congress.

📚 References
  • Buckley v. Valeo, 424 U.S. 1, 132–33 (1976) (holding that federal officers must be appointed by the President or in a manner consistent with the appointments clause, which does not allow congressional appointments).
  • Lucia v. SEC, 138 S. Ct. 2044, 2053 (2018) (describing the requirements for a federal officer).

一项具有不可分割条款的联邦法规设立了一个新的五人制“国家繁荣委员会”（National Prosperity Board），该委员会对证券、银行和商品行业的运营拥有广泛的监管权力，包括发布具有法律效力规则的权力。该法规规定，其中三名委员会成员由总统在参议院的建议和同意下任命。他们任期七年，只能因正当理由被免职。委员会的另外两名成员在法规中被指定为参议院和众议院政府运营委员会的各自总法律顾问。法规规定，他们只要继续担任这些职务，就应在委员会任职。
在遵循所有必要的行政程序后，委员会发布了一套详细的规则，规范所有银行、证券交易商和商品经纪人的运营。一家受委员会规则约束的证券公司寻求一项“宣告性判决”（declaratory judgment），主张这些规则无效，因为设立该委员会的法规违宪。
在本案中，法院是否应裁定设立“国家繁荣委员会”的法规合宪？

zh-choices.A: 否，因为所有行使行政权力的联邦委员会成员都必须由总统任命，或以其他符合《第二条》（Article II）“任命条款”（appointments clause）的方式任命。
zh-choices.B: 否，因为所有拥有广泛准立法性质权力（例如规则制定）的联邦委员会成员都必须由国会任命。
zh-choices.C: 是，因为“必要和适当条款”（necessary and proper clause）授权国会决定其根据州际贸易监管权力所设立委员会的成员任命方式。
zh-choices.D: 是，因为国会为“公共福利”（general welfare）立法的权力与国会在本法规中规定的委员会成员任命方式之间存在实质性关联。

questions.zh-explanation:
MBE 考点解析

Constitutional Law: Separation of Powers - Separation of Powers

本题真正考的是

一句话定位考点

本题真正考的是：国会能不能把联邦官员（federal officers）的任命权留给自己，尤其是让一个带有持续任期、并行使执法式规则制定权的联邦委员会由国会指定成员。

三秒认题路径：

持续任期 → 规则制定权 → 联邦官员 → 只能按 Article II 任命 → 国会指定就违宪

核心法律规则

直接套规则，不绕弯

联邦官员（federal officers）是指：一边担任持续性的公职，一边还握有明显的裁量权去管理或执行法律，也就是带有执行权（executive powers）的人。Appointments Clause（任命条款）下，这类人必须由总统任命，或按 Article II 允许的方式任命；国会自己不能直接任命。

本题里，董事会成员任期固定、还可以制定对证券、银行和商品行业有约束力的规则，所以他们就是联邦官员。既然法规又把其中两名成员交给国会委员会法律顾问来指定，这一步就踩线了。

核心判例： Buckley v. Valeo - 规则制定属于执行型权力，行使这类权力的人不能由国会任命。

思维导图

先看：这是不是 Article II 的任命问题？
是： 题干说的是新设联邦董事会成员，且有七年任期或持续任职，先把他们当成 联邦官员（federal officers）。
再看： 他们有没有实质性裁量去发规则、管行业、执行法律？有，而且是“with the force of law”的规则制定权。
卡死点：effectively reviewable 之类不是这里的逻辑；这里卡的是“国会能不能亲自指定人”。答案：不能。
结论： 只要是联邦官员，任命就必须走总统 + 参议院同意，或 Article II 允许的例外路径；国会指定两名成员，直接违宪。
所以选什么？
选 A： 把“所有行使执行权的联邦董事会成员”都收进任命条款，正好击中本题。

考点陷阱

你可能会想：这题的董事会在做规则，像是在搞“准立法”，那国会既然能立法，也许能自己指定成员。

但考试真正问的是：这些人是不是在行使联邦执行权；只要是，就必须按 Appointments Clause（任命条款） 走，总统或 Article II 允许的方式可以，国会亲自点名不行。

正确答案与干扰项排除

为什么选 A？

题干写明董事会成员有七年任期并能制定“with the force of law”的规则，已经是联邦官员；所以国会指定两名成员，违背任命条款。

❌ 概念混淆 | 准立法误判

✕ B: 把quasi-legislative当成国会可任命的理由，混淆了“能立规则”与“谁能任命”。

❌ 法律适用 | 必要正当误判

✕ C: 只会背necessary and proper，却忘了它不能推翻任命条款。

❌ 事实误判 | 福利权力误读

✕ D: 把general welfare硬套进来，但题干根本不是税收或拨款场景。

这题建议用什么方法？

先判定是不是联邦官员，再问任命来源；只要看到国会亲自指定执行型成员，就直接警报。

考场速记

记住一句：联邦官员（federal officers）只要有持续公职 + 执法式裁量，就只能走 Article II 任命，国会不能自己任命。

考场口诀：“先看是不是官，再看谁来任；一旦会发命令，国会别插手。”

questions.subject: Constitutional Law
questions.question:
A recently enacted federal statute requires the President to make each appointment of a United States ambassador to a foreign country from a list of three individuals. The list is to be compiled by the Senate Foreign Relations Committee and approved by the full Senate in advance of the appointment. The statute also provides that Senate confirmation of the appointment is deemed to occur automatically 30 days after the time the President names an appointee from the list, unless the full Senate determines otherwise within the 30-day period.
Is this statute constitutional?

choices.A: No, because the statute impermissibly restricts the plenary foreign affairs powers of the President.
choices.B: No, because the statute violates the constitutional requirements for appointment of ambassadors of the United States.
choices.C: Yes, because the statute is a necessary and proper measure in furtherance of Congress's power to regulate commerce with foreign states.
choices.D: Yes, because the statute is consistent with the constitutional requirement that the presidential appointment of ambassadors be with the advice and consent of the Senate.

questions.explanation:
Appointment clause (timeline) (ambassadors, SCOTUS justices, principal federal officers)

President
nominates
Senate gives advice
(eg, holds hearings)
Senate consents
(majority vote required)
SCOTUS = Supreme Court of the United States

The appointments clause grants the President the power to appoint ambassadors, Supreme Court justices, and other principal federal officers with the Senate's advice and consent. This clause gives the President plenary (ie, exclusive) nomination power that cannot be limited by Congress. Therefore, the statute unconstitutionally infringes upon that power by limiting the President's ability to select ambassadorial nominees to a list compiled by a Senate committee.

This statute also provides for automatic Senate confirmation of any individual who had been named on the list of nominees approved by the Senate before the appointment. But Senate confirmation should only occur after a nomination, when the Senate gives advice (eg, by holding hearings) and then chooses to consent to the nomination by majority vote. Therefore, this statute also violates the majority-vote requirement (Choice D).

(Choice A) The President does not have plenary power over foreign affairs since Congress also possesses powers in this area (eg, declare war, regulate foreign commerce).

(Choice C) The necessary and proper clause (article I, section 8) grants Congress the power to employ reasonably appropriate measures to carry out its other powers—eg, regulating commerce with foreign nations. But Congress cannot violate other constitutional provisions when exercising this power (as seen here).

📌 Educational Objective

The appointments clause gives the President the power to appoint ambassadors, Supreme Court justices, and other principal federal officers with the advice and consent of the Senate. Congress cannot limit the President's plenary power to select nominees, and the Senate can only choose to consent to the nomination by majority vote.

📚 References
  • U.S. Const. art. II, § 2, cl. 2 (appointments clause).
  • Edmond v. United States, 520 U.S. 651, 659 (1997) (stating that principal officers, including ambassadors, must be nominated by the President and confirmed by the Senate).

zh-choices.C: 合宪，因为该法规是国会为促进其监管与外国商业的权力而采取的必要且适当的措施。

questions.zh-explanation:
MBE 考点解析

Constitutional Law: Separation of Powers - Separation of Powers

本题真正考的是

一句话定位考点

本题真正考的是：国会能不能把大使任命权改成“先由参议院名单筛选、再自动确认”的版本。

三秒认题路径：

大使任命 → 总统提名 → 参议院同意 → 自动确认？ → 违宪

核心法律规则

抓住宪法动作，不要被“程序包装”带跑

任命条款（Appointments Clause）把大使（ambassadors）、最高法院法官（Supreme Court justices）和其他主要联邦官员（principal federal officers）的提名权交给总统；考场意思：总统先挑人，国会不能替他先圈名单。

参议院的角色是建议与同意（advice and consent），考场意思：它可以说“同意”或“不同意”，但不能把同意改成automatic confirmation，更不能把提名先塞进委员会名单里再要求总统照单选人。

所以这题的关键不是“国会有没有任何外交权”，而是这个法条有没有直接改写宪法规定的任命流程；答案是改了，所以违宪。

核心判例： Edmond v. United States — 主要官员必须由总统提名、参议院确认，国会不能把提名权拿走。

思维导图

先看：这是不是在改 Appointments Clause 的任命流程？
是
总统是否仍然拥有先提名、先选人？
否
卡死点：国会用“名单 + 自动确认”替代了总统提名，不能这么改。
参议院是否只是“同意 / 不同意”一票？
否
卡死点：把 advice and consent 变成先审名单、再自动确认，越线。
结论：能立刻把任命流程改成法条这套吗？
不能
答案锁定：违宪，选 B。

考点陷阱

你可能会想：既然国会也管外交、也能调节对外商业，那它是不是就能顺手管大使怎么选。

但考试真正问的是：任命条款有没有被国会改成自己先筛人、再让总统照着走。

司法考试看的是「法律程序上能不能救济」，而不是「物理上的秘密有没有泄露」。 这题同理，看的是宪法程序有没有被改写，不是国会有没有外交背景。

正确答案与干扰项排除

为什么选 B？

题干把 总统提名 改成“先给名单、再自动确认”，直接碰到 任命条款（Appointments Clause） 的核心流程，所以违宪。

❌ 概念混淆 | 外交权泛化

✕ A: 把 foreign affairs 当成万能授权，忘了任命流程仍受宪法专门规定。

❌ 法律适用 | 必要适当错套

✕ C: 见到 necessary and proper 就套，但国会不能借此改写宪法明文。

❌ 事实误判 | 自动同意偷换

✕ D: 把 automatic 当成“同意”，但参议院的同意必须是真正投票。

这题建议用什么方法？

先锁定宪法明文流程，再看法条有没有把总统提名权和参议院同意权偷偷改成别的东西。

考场速记

记住这句：大使、最高法院法官、主要联邦官员，先由总统提名，再由参议院同意；国会不能把“先提名”改成“先给名单”。

口诀：In Certain Circumstances, An Appeal Can Be Made Prematurely 只管中间上诉例外；本题不是上诉题，但同样要先找“宪法明文流程”再看例外有没有。

questions.subject: Constitutional Law
questions.question:
For various reasons, the number of individuals raising fowl (primarily chickens, but also turkeys, ducks, and geese) on their private property has spiked. Lobbyists for the poultry industry presented Congress with a recent study indicating that private sellers of fowl and their eggs were substantially affecting the national market. In addition, the study noted the increased potential for the spread of avian flu due to private individuals raising fowl. In response to this study, Congress passed a statute that precludes family households from raising more than five fowl without a license.
Will this statute likely be found constitutional?

choices.A: No, because the statute does not consider the number of household members to determine how many fowl a household can raise.
choices.B: No, because the statute will regulate the purely private conduct of raising fowl.
choices.C: Yes, because Congress can restrict private conduct that poses a public health risk or endangers the public welfare.
choices.D: Yes, because the raising of fowl, in the aggregate, substantially affects the national market for fowl and their products.

questions.explanation:
Commerce Clause challenge
Does federal statute regulate interstate commerce?
Yes
Constitutional
No
Does federal statute regulate activity that substantially impacts interstate commerce?
Yes
Constitutional
No
Unconstitutional

The Constitution grants Congress broad regulatory authority under the Commerce Clause over most activities involving two or more states. This includes the authority to regulate:

  • the channels of interstate commerce (e.g., highways)
  • the instrumentalities of interstate commerce (e.g., airplanes)
  • people and things moving in interstate commerce (e.g., commercial shipments of goods) and
  • activities that, singly or in the aggregate, substantially affect interstate commerce, which is presumed when an activity is economic in nature.

Here, Congress passed a statute precluding family households from raising more than five fowl without a license. This statute was enacted in response to a study indicating that private sellers of fowls and their eggs were substantially affecting the national market and increasing the potential for the spread of avian flu. Because this activity, in the aggregate, substantially affects the national market for fowl and their products, Congress had the power to regulate it under the Commerce Clause. Therefore, this statute will likely be found constitutional.

(Choice A) The statute need not consider the number of household members to determine how many fowl a household can raise because this activity substantially affects the national market.

(Choice B) Congress has the authority to regulate the private conduct of raising fowl under the Commerce Clause so long as the activity, whether singly or in the aggregate, substantially affects interstate commerce (as seen here).

(Choice C) Congress has no general police power to legislate for citizens' health, safety, welfare, or morals. This power is instead reserved for the states.

📌 Educational Objective

The Commerce Clause grants Congress the authority to regulate (1) the channels of interstate commerce, (2) the instrumentalities of interstate commerce, (3) people and things moving in interstate commerce, and (4) activities that, singly or in the aggregate, substantially affect interstate commerce.

📚 References
  • Gonzales v. Raich, 545 U.S. 1, 17 (2005) (explaining Congress's broad authority under the commerce clause).

由于各种原因，在其私人财产上饲养家禽（主要是鸡，但也包括火鸡、鸭和鹅）的个人数量激增。禽类行业的游说者向国会提交了一份最新研究报告，表明私人销售家禽及其蛋类正在实质性影响全国市场。此外，该研究指出，由于个人饲养家禽，禽流感传播的潜在风险增加。为回应这项研究，国会通过了一项法规（statute），禁止家庭未经许可饲养超过五只家禽。
这项法规是否可能被认定为合宪（constitutional）？

zh-choices.A: 否，因为该法规没有考虑家庭成员数量来确定一个家庭可以饲养多少只家禽。
zh-choices.B: 否，因为该法规将规制纯粹的私人饲养家禽行为。
zh-choices.C: 是，因为国会可以限制构成公共健康风险或危及公共福祉的私人行为。
zh-choices.D: 是，因为家禽饲养行为，从总体上看（in the aggregate），实质性影响了全国的家禽及其产品市场。

questions.zh-explanation:
MBE 考点解析

Constitutional Law: Separation of Powers - Commerce

本题真正考的是

一句话定位考点

本题真正考的是：国会能不能依据商务条款（Commerce Clause），管到本来像“私人养鸡”这种州内活动。

三秒认题路径：

看国会权限 → 不是州权 → 见商业影响 → 走聚合影响 → 选合宪

核心法律规则

国会在商务条款（Commerce Clause）下，不只管跨州买卖，还能管单独或合并后（singly or in the aggregate）会实质影响州际商业（substantially affect interstate commerce）的活动。考试里，看到活动本身是经济性的，通常就会推定国会有权管。

这里的关键不是“这户人家养几只鸡”，而是“成千上万户一起养，会不会推高全国鸡和鸡蛋市场、影响流通和价格”。只要题干给了全国市场被影响的事实，国会就能立法。

核心判例： Gonzales v. Raich —— 说明即使是看似本地的私人行为，只要合并起来会影响全国市场，国会也能管。

思维导图

国会是在管州际商业本身吗？
是管渠道、工具、货物运输中的人和物 → 合宪
否转下一关
这类私人养鸡活动，会不会单独或合并后实质影响州际商业？
题干给出：私人卖鸡和鸡蛋 已明显影响全国市场
再加上：禽流感风险上升，说明它不是纯家务小事，而是会牵动市场的经济活动
“只是本地私人行为”这个想法被打掉：经济性活动 + 聚合影响 = 国会可管
结论是什么？
YES 选 D：合宪
NO 才会落到违宪，但本题走不到这一步

考点陷阱

你可能会想：这只是“私人在自家养鸡”，看起来像州内小事，国会不该插手。

但考试真正问的是：这项活动会不会合并后影响全国鸡和鸡蛋市场。司法考试看的是「法律程序上能不能救济」，而不是「物理上的秘密有没有泄露」。这里也一样，重点不是生活故事像不像家务，而是它有没有商业影响。

正确答案与干扰项排除

为什么选 D？

题干 private sellers of fowl and their eggs were substantially affecting the national market，正好踩中“合并后实质影响州际商业”，所以合宪。

❌ 事实误判 | 家庭人数偷换

✕ A: 把“每户几只鸡”当成关键，但题目根本不是按人口配额审查。

❌ 概念混淆 | 私人行为误读

✕ B: 看到 purely private conduct 就以为国会不能管，忽略了聚合后的商业影响。

❌ 法律适用 | 公权泛化误判

✕ C: 把public health 当成国会一般警察权，联邦没有这种兜底权限。

这题建议用什么方法？

先找国会权限来源，再问活动是否经济性并会合并影响州际商业，别被“私人小事”带跑。

考场速记

记住一句：经济性活动 + 聚合影响 = 商务条款常常能过。再配合口诀：In Certain Circumstances, An Appeal Can Be Made Prematurely 是程序题用的，这题不用，别混题型。

keywords.text: private sellers of fowl and their eggs

reason.en: Their sales make raising fowl economic activity subject to aggregate-effects analysis.
reason.zh: 其销售行为使养禽构成可适用总体影响分析的经济活动。

reason.en: This supplies the constitutional nexus between the regulated activity and interstate commerce.
reason.zh: 这确立了受规制活动与州际商业之间的宪法联系。

reason.en: This supports the legislation factually but does not independently grant Congress a general police power.
reason.zh: 该事实支持立法理由，但不会单独赋予国会一般警察权。

reason.en: Federal action requires an enumerated constitutional source of authority.
reason.zh: 联邦立法必须具有宪法列举权力作为依据。

reason.en: The private and local character of the actors does not preclude Commerce Clause regulation.
reason.zh: 行为主体的私人和地方性质并不排除商业条款规制。

keywords.text: more than five fowl without a license

reason.en: This identifies the regulated conduct and the statute's licensing mechanism.
reason.zh: 这确定了受规制行为及该法的许可机制。

reason.en: Household size is irrelevant to whether Congress has Commerce Clause authority.
reason.zh: 家庭人数与国会是否具有商业条款权力无关。

reason.en: Private conduct may be regulated when its economic aggregate effect on interstate commerce is substantial.
reason.zh: 私人行为如在总体上对州际商业产生重大经济影响，仍可受到规制。

reason.en: The activity is connected to a national market for fowl and their products.
reason.zh: 该活动与禽类及其产品的全国市场相关联。

reason.en: Congress lacks a general power to regulate merely because conduct threatens public health.
reason.zh: 国会不能仅因行为威胁公共健康而行使一般规制权。

reason.en: General health and welfare authority belongs primarily to the states, not Congress.
reason.zh: 一般健康与福利规制权主要属于各州，而非国会。

reason.en: Economic activity may be evaluated collectively rather than household by household.
reason.zh: 经济活动可按整体而非逐户评估。

reason.en: This states the constitutional basis for federal regulation under the Commerce Clause.
reason.zh: 这说明了商业条款下联邦规制的宪法依据。

reason.en: It identifies the national market affected by the regulated activity.
reason.zh: 它确定了受规制活动所影响的全国市场。

highlights.text: private sellers of fowl and their eggs were substantially affecting the national market

label.zh: 经济活动重大影响认定

reason.en: This directly establishes Congress's Commerce Clause basis for regulating the activity.
reason.zh: 这直接确立了国会依据商业条款规制该活动的基础。

highlights.text: increased potential for the spread of avian flu

reason.en: It explains Congress's concern but cannot alone substitute for an enumerated federal power.
reason.zh: 它解释了国会的关切，但不能单独替代联邦列举权力。

highlights.text: precludes family households from raising more than five fowl without a license

reason.en: The statute reaches local private activity whose aggregate economic effect must be assessed.
reason.zh: 该法涉及地方私人活动，必须评估其总体经济影响。

highlights.text: Will this statute likely be found constitutional?

reason.en: The issue is whether Congress had constitutional authority to enact the licensing restriction.
reason.zh: 问题在于国会是否具有制定该许可限制的宪法权力。

questions.subject: Constitutional Law
questions.question:
A federal statute requires any individual or entity owning more than 100 cars to ensure that at least 10 percent of those cars are electric-powered.
A city that owns over 500 cars has sued the federal official responsible for enforcing this statute in federal district court, seeking an injunction prohibiting enforcement of the statute on the ground that it is unconstitutional.
Should the court grant the injunction?

choices.A: No, because the federal government has sovereign immunity and cannot be sued without its explicit consent.
choices.B: No, because the statute is valid under the commerce clause and does not violate the Tenth Amendment.
choices.C: Yes, because as applied to state and local governments, the statute exceeds Congress's power under the commerce clause.
choices.D: Yes, because the statute violates the reserved rights of the states under the Tenth Amendment.

questions.explanation:
The commerce clause grants Congress broad power to regulate interstate commerce, including:

  • channels of interstate commerce
  • instrumentalities of interstate commerce
  • persons/things moving in interstate commerce and
  • activities that substantially affect interstate commerce.

But Congress must comply with other constitutional provisions when exercising its commerce power. This includes the Tenth Amendment, which prohibits Congress from commandeering state or local governments by requiring them to (1) enforce a federal law or (2) enact a state or local law.

Here, Congress enacted a statute requiring individuals and entities owning over 100 cars (like the city) to ensure that at least 10 percent of those cars are electric-powered. This is a valid exercise of Congress's commerce power since cars are instrumentalities of interstate commerce (Choice C). And since the statute does not require the city to enforce it against others or enact related laws, the statute does not violate the Tenth Amendment. Therefore, the court should deny the injunction(Choice D).

(Choice A) The federal government enjoys sovereign immunity from suits seeking monetary damages. But this immunity does not extend to suits seeking nonmonetary relief—eg, an injunction (as seen here).

📌 Educational Objective

Congress has broad power to regulate interstate commerce. But the Tenth Amendment limits this power by prohibiting Congress from requiring state or local governments to (1) enforce a federal law or (2) enact a state or local law.

📚 References
  • Reno v. Condon, 528 U.S. 141, 149–51 (2000) (holding that a federal statute regulating states' commercial activity does not violate the Tenth Amendment since it does not require states to enact or enforce any laws).
questions.zh-question:
一项联邦法规要求，任何拥有超过100辆汽车的个人或实体，都必须确保其车辆中至少有10%为电动车。

一个拥有超过500辆汽车的城市，已在联邦地区法院起诉负责执行该法规的联邦官员，以该法规违宪为由，寻求一项禁止执行该法规的禁令。

法院应否批准该禁令？

zh-choices.A: 否，因为联邦政府享有主权豁免，未经其明确同意，不得被起诉。
zh-choices.B: 否，因为该法规根据 commerce clause 是有效的，且未违反 Tenth Amendment。
zh-choices.C: 是，因为在适用于州和地方政府时，该法规超出了国会根据 commerce clause 拥有的权力。
zh-choices.D: 是，因为该法规侵犯了 Tenth Amendment 规定的各州保留权利。

questions.zh-explanation:
MBE 考点解析

Constitutional Law: Separation of Powers - Separation of Powers

本题真正考的是

一句话定位考点

本题真正考的是：国会用 商事条款（Commerce Clause） 管理州政府的车队时，有没有踩到 第十修正案（Tenth Amendment） 的反命令红线。

三秒认题路径：

州起诉联邦 → 要禁执行 → 先看商事条款 → 再看反命令 → 不能禁

核心法律规则

商事条款（Commerce Clause） 让国会能管州际商业，连 运输工具（instrumentalities） 这类在州际流通中的对象也能管；所以“车”这种对象本身就落在国会的权限里。第十修正案（Tenth Amendment） 只是不许国会强迫州去 执行联邦法（enforce federal law） 或 制定州法（enact state law），不是说州一被联邦法碰到就自动赢。

这题里，法条只是要求拥有超过 100 辆车的主体把其中 10% 电动化，没有命令城市替联邦去执法，也没有逼城市自己立新法，所以反命令问题过不了。

核心判例： Reno v. Condon - 联邦法若只是直接管州的商业活动，而不是逼州替联邦执行法律，通常不违反第十修正案。

思维导图

先看：这是不是国会越权到“逼州办事”？
1 国会有没有 命令州执行联邦法 或 命令州制定州法？
没有。题干只是直接管“拥有 100 辆车以上的主体”要电动化，不是叫城市替联邦执法。
2 车队属于什么？
属于可被国会纳入 商事条款（Commerce Clause） 监管的对象，尤其是 instrumentalities 这一类。
3 结论卡点：
既然不是反命令，而且国会有商事条款基础，城市就不能靠第十修正案把禁令拿到手。
答案落点：选 B，法院应拒绝禁令。

考点陷阱

你可能会想：城市是州和地方政府，联邦一管它就像在“指挥州政府”。

但考试真正问的是：国会有没有直接逼城市去 执法 或 立法；如果只是给它一个适用中的联邦规则，这不是反命令。

司法考试看的是「法律程序上能不能救济」，不是「物理上的车有没有变电动」。

正确答案与干扰项排除

为什么选 B？

题干只是要求车主把车队改成一定比例的电动车，属于商事条款下可管的对象；又没有命令城市替联邦执法，所以不触发第十修正案禁区。

❌ 概念混淆 | 主权豁免误判

✕ A: 把 sovereign immunity 误当成不能发禁令。

❌ 法律适用 | 商事权限误判

✕ C: 以为州府一被点名就超权，但这里管的是车队，不是逼州执法。

❌ 事实误判 | 反命令偷换

✕ D: 把 Tenth Amendment 扩大成“联邦不能管州的商业活动”。

这题建议用什么方法？

先问国会是不是在“逼州办事”，再问它有没有商事条款基础；两步都过，禁令就难赢。

考场速记

记住一句：国会能管州的商业活动，但不能命令州替联邦执法或立法。看到州政府被联邦法直接点名，先问是不是“反命令”；不是，就别急着搬第十修正案。

reason.en: Identifies congressional action whose constitutional validity must be assessed.
reason.zh: 表明需要审查其合宪性的国会立法行为。

reason.en: Shows that the statute regulates public and private owners alike rather than targeting government lawmaking.
reason.zh: 表明该法规同时规制公共与私人所有者，而非专门干预政府立法。

reason.en: The regulated cars are instrumentalities of interstate commerce.
reason.zh: 受规制的汽车属于州际商业工具。

reason.en: Triggers consideration of the Tenth Amendment's anti-commandeering principle.
reason.zh: 触发对第十修正案反征用原则的审查。

keywords.text: federal official responsible for enforcing this statute

reason.en: Permits a suit for prospective relief against enforcement of an allegedly unconstitutional law.
reason.zh: 允许针对涉嫌违宪法律的执行提起前瞻性救济诉讼。

reason.en: Sovereign immunity does not categorically bar this requested nonmonetary relief.
reason.zh: 主权豁免并不当然阻止所请求的非金钱救济。

reason.en: This distractor wrongly treats immunity as an absolute bar to prospective injunctive relief.
reason.zh: 该干扰项错误地将主权豁免视为前瞻性禁令救济的绝对障碍。

A.text: cannot be sued without its explicit consent

reason.en: It overstates sovereign immunity by ignoring suits for prospective nonmonetary relief against officials.
reason.zh: 其忽视针对官员的前瞻性非金钱救济诉讼，夸大了主权豁免。

reason.en: Congress may regulate cars as instrumentalities of interstate commerce.
reason.zh: 国会可以将汽车作为州际商业工具进行规制。

B.text: does not violate the Tenth Amendment

reason.en: The statute regulates the city's activity without requiring it to enact or enforce federal policy.
reason.zh: 该法规仅规制城市活动，并未要求其制定或执行联邦政策。

C.text: as applied to state and local governments

label.zh: 适用于州及地方政府的限制

reason.en: Governmental status alone does not exempt commercial activity from otherwise valid federal regulation.
reason.zh: 政府身份本身并不使商业活动免受其他方面有效的联邦规制。

C.text: exceeds Congress's power under the commerce clause

reason.en: This ignores that cars are instrumentalities of interstate commerce.
reason.zh: 该表述忽视了汽车属于州际商业工具。

reason.en: The Tenth Amendment does not invalidate every federal law regulating state or local entities.
reason.zh: 第十修正案并不使所有规制州或地方实体的联邦法律失效。

reason.en: The conclusion wrongly equates direct regulation with unconstitutional commandeering.
reason.zh: 该结论错误地将直接规制等同于违宪征用。

highlights.text: requires any individual or entity owning more than 100 cars

label.zh: 普遍适用的所有权规制

reason.en: The law regulates owners generally rather than directing governments to legislate or enforce federal law.
reason.zh: 该法律普遍规制所有者，而非命令政府立法或执行联邦法律。

highlights.text: A city that owns over 500 cars

label.zh: 受规制的地方政府所有者

reason.en: The city's governmental status raises the anti-commandeering issue, while its vehicle ownership places it within the regulation.
reason.zh: 城市的政府身份引出反征用问题，而其车辆所有权使其受该法规约束。

highlights.text: seeking an injunction prohibiting enforcement of the statute

reason.en: The requested nonmonetary relief defeats the answer asserting an absolute sovereign-immunity bar.
reason.zh: 所请求的非金钱救济排除了主张主权豁免绝对阻却诉讼的选项。

highlights.text: on the ground that it is unconstitutional

label.zh: 对联邦规制的合宪性挑战

reason.en: Frames whether Congress had commerce power and complied with the Tenth Amendment.
reason.zh: 界定了国会是否拥有商业权力并遵守第十修正案的问题。

questions.subject: Constitutional Law
questions.question:
The Sports Championship Revenue Enhancement Act is a federal statute that was enacted as part of a comprehensive program to eliminate the federal budget deficit. That act imposed, for a period of five years, a 50% excise tax on the price of tickets to championship sporting events. Such events included the World Series, the Super Bowl, major college bowl games, and similar championship sports events.
Is this federal tax likely constitutional?

choices.A: No, because a 50% tax is likely to reduce attendance at championship sporting events and, therefore, is not rationally related to the legitimate interest of Congress in eliminating the budget deficit.
choices.B: No, because Congress violates the equal protection component of the Fifth Amendment by singling out championship sporting events for this tax while failing to tax other major sporting, artistic, or entertainment events to which tickets are sold.
choices.C: Yes, because an act of Congress that appears to be a revenue raising measure on its face is not rendered invalid because it may have adverse economic consequences for the activity taxed.
choices.D: Yes, because the compelling national interest in reducing the federal budget deficit justifies this tax as a temporary emergency measure.

questions.explanation:
The taxing and spending clause vests Congress with broad taxing power. This allows Congress to impose an indirect tax (eg, excise tax) so long as it is:

  • imposed uniformly in every state where the taxed goods are found and
  • reasonably related to revenue raising on its face.

Such taxes are constitutional even if they have an adverse economic impact on, or otherwise burden, the thing taxed.

Here, the federal statute imposed a 50% excise tax on tickets to championship sporting events. This indirect tax is applied uniformly to all such events, regardless of where they are held. And though the tax may create adverse economic consequences (eg, reduced attendance) for these events, it is reasonably related to raising revenues to eliminate the budget deficit (Choice A). Therefore, the tax is likely constitutional.

(Choice B) This excise tax triggers equal protection concerns since it taxes championship sporting events differently than other major events. But since neither the events nor the attendees are a protected class, the tax need only pass rational basis scrutiny. Therefore, the tax likely complies with the equal protection component.

(Choice D) Congress does not need a compelling national interest or emergency powers to justify the use of its broad taxing power.

📌 Educational Objective

Congress can impose indirect taxes so long as they are (1) uniformly applied in every state where the taxed goods are found and (2) reasonably related to revenue production. This power is not diminished by the fact that such taxes may burden or restrict the thing taxed.

📚 References
  • Flint v. Stone Tracy Co., 220 U.S. 107, 151 (1911) ("[T]he terms duties, imposts and excises are generally treated as embracing the indirect forms of taxation").
  • Fernandez v. Wiener, 326 U.S. 340, 362 (1945) ("It has long been settled that an Act of Congress which on its face purports to be an exercise of the taxing power, is not any the less so because the tax is burdensome or tends to restrict or suppress the thing taxed").
questions.zh-question: 这项联邦税收是否可能合宪？

zh-choices.A: 否，因为50%的税率可能会减少锦标赛体育赛事的上座率，因此与国会消除预算赤字的合法利益没有合理关联。
zh-choices.B: 否，因为国会仅对锦标赛体育赛事征收此税，而未对其他售票的主要体育、艺术或娱乐活动征税，这违反了第五修正案的平等保护条款。
zh-choices.C: 是，因为一项国会法案，如果其表面上是一项增收措施，则不会因其可能对被征税的活动产生不利的经济后果而失效。
zh-choices.D: 是，因为削减联邦预算赤字的迫切国家利益，证明了这项税收作为一项临时紧急措施是正当的。

questions.zh-explanation:
MBE 考点解析

Constitutional Law: Separation of Powers - Taxation And Spending

本题真正考的是

一句话定位考点

本题真正考的是：国会用 间接税（indirect tax） 作为征税手段时，只要税制表面上是为筹集收入，且在各州统一适用，就算它会压缩被税对象的生意，也通常仍然合宪。

三秒认题路径：

联邦征税 → 间接税 → 看统一性 → 看筹税目的 → 仍可合宪

核心法律规则

征税与支出条款（Taxing and Spending Clause） 让国会有很宽的征税权。对 间接税（indirect tax），考场上先看两件事：是否在各州统一适用，是否在表面上合理地指向 筹集收入（revenue raising）。

如果这两点都过了，税就通常合宪；它就算会让被税的活动变少、变贵，考试也不因此把它打成违宪。这里最关键的是：看税的 face，不是看被税行业会不会疼。

核心判例： Fernandez v. Wiener、Flint v. Stone Tracy Co. - 只要税在表面上是征税，不会因为它很重、会压制被税活动，就自动失效。

思维导图

这是不是国会的征税权问题？
先看：是不是 间接税（excise tax），而且表面上是为了 收入筹集（revenue raising）？
如果是： 就算会减少门票销售、压低客流，也不自动违宪
再看：是否在各州统一适用？本题对所有冠军赛门票都征税，统一性过关。
结论：税制在考场上仍属合宪，答案走 Yes。
误区提醒：不要把“会伤害被税活动”当成违宪理由；这题不问政策好不好，只问征税权有没有被国会合法使用。

考点陷阱

你可能会想：既然 50% 很重、还会让比赛门票销量下降，那国会是不是在“惩罚”体育赛事？

但考试真正问的是：这是不是一项表面上为了筹税、并且统一适用的联邦税，不是它会不会让行业难受。

司法考试看的是「法律程序上能不能救济」，而不是「物理上的秘密有没有泄露」。（这句是别题的常见套路；本题对应的核心同样是看税的合法性质，不看经济痛感。）

正确答案与干扰项排除

为什么选 C？

题干的 50% excise tax 是为填补预算赤字而设，表面上就是筹税；它就算压低赛事需求，也不因此失去合宪性。

❌ 法律适用 | 收益目的误判

✕ A: 把“会影响观赛”当成无理性，错把税的副作用当成违宪标准。

❌ 概念混淆 | 平等审查乱套

✕ B: 乱拉 equal protection，但冠军赛和观众都不是受保护分类。

❌ 事实误判 | 紧急权前提偷换

✕ D: 把预算赤字说成要 compelling 才能征税，国会征税根本不靠这个门槛。

这题建议用什么方法？

先把它归成“表面筹税的联邦间接税”，再用“统一适用 + 收入目的”直接排除情绪化反应。

考场速记

记住这句：税看表面，痛感不控宪。只要是为了筹税、并且统一适用的联邦间接税，税得再狠，也不因为它会压缩被税活动就自动失效。
