questions.subject: Constitutional Law
questions.question:
The House of Representatives passed a bill imposing a tax on all insurance premiums for policies covering shipments of goods to foreign countries. The legislative record states that the purpose of this export tax is to subsidize the marine insurance industry. The tax applies to all goods manufactured or grown in every state. The bill passed the Senate and was signed into law by the President.
Pursuant to the statute, a company paid the tax on insurance premiums for policies that cover goods exported to its foreign subsidiaries. The company filed a claim for a tax refund and was denied. The company filed suit alleging that the tax is unconstitutional.
Is this federal tax likely constitutional?

choices.A: No, because Congress does not have the power to tax exported goods or closely related services.
choices.B: No, because the tax does not reasonably relate to raising revenue.
choices.C: Yes, because Congress's taxing power is unlimited.
choices.D: Yes, because the tax is necessary to serve a compelling government interest.

questions.explanation:
The taxing and spending clause gives Congress broad power to tax and spend for the general welfare (ie, any public purpose). However, this power is not unlimited and must comply with other constitutional provisions—including the export clause. The export clause prohibits federal taxation of:

  • exported goods, which are goods leaving the U.S. and shipped to foreign countries and
  • services and activities closely related to the export process—eg, insurance premiums paid to cover the shipment of exported goods (as seen here).

Therefore, the federal tax on insurance premiums for policies covering shipments of goods to foreign countries is not within Congress's power to tax and is unconstitutional. (Choice A)

(Choice B) The tax in this case is reasonably related to raising revenue because its purpose is to raise funds that will be used to subsidize the marine insurance industry. But this issue is irrelevant because the tax is an unconstitutional export tax.

(Choice D) Federal export taxes are never valid, even if the government shows that they are necessary to serve a compelling interest (ie, satisfy strict scrutiny).

📌 Educational Objective

Congress has broad power to tax and spend for the general welfare. However, Congress can never impose taxes on exported goods or on services and activities closely related to the export process.

📚 References
  • U.S. Const. art. I, § 9 (export clause).
  • United States v. Int'l Bus. Machs. Corp., 517 U.S. 843, 846–47 (1996) (explaining that the export clause prohibits federal taxation of exported goods and services and activities closely related to the export process).
questions.zh-question:
为了减少联邦赤字，众议院通过了一项法案，对所有承保货物运往国外的保单的保险费征税。立法记录表明，这项出口税的目的是补贴海事保险业。该税适用于在每个州制造或种植的所有商品。该法案经参议院通过，并由总统签署成为法律。

根据该法规，一家公司为其承保出口到国外子公司的货物的保单支付了保险费税。该公司申请退税但被驳回。该公司提起诉讼，声称该税违宪。

这项联邦税是否可能合宪？

zh-choices.A: 否，因为国会无权对出口商品征税。
zh-choices.B: 否，因为该税与增加财政收入没有合理关联。
zh-choices.C: 是，因为该税是为了服务于一项紧迫的政府利益所必需的。
zh-choices.D: 是，因为该税在每个州统一适用。

questions.zh-explanation:
MBE 考点解析

Constitutional Law: Separation of Powers - Taxation And Spending

本题真正考的是

一句话定位考点

本题真正考的是：出口条款（export clause）会不会挡住联邦政府对出口相关保险费征税。

三秒认题路径：

联邦税 → 出口相关 → 看出口条款 → 禁止征税 → 选 A

核心法律规则

税收与支出权（taxing and spending power）考场意思：国会当然能为公共目的征税，但这不是无限权力，仍要服从宪法限制。

这里的关键限制是出口条款（export clause），考场意思：凡是针对出口货物（exported goods），或与出口过程紧密相关的服务（closely related services），联邦都不能征税。

所以一旦题目出现给出口货物买保险、运送、装船这类和出口流程绑在一起的费用，考场上就别再想“是不是为了筹钱”了，直接看它是不是被出口条款卡死。

核心判例：United States v. International Business Machines Corp. — 它把“出口货物”和“紧密相关的出口服务”一起锁进了禁止征税的范围。

思维导图

联邦税收先问：是不是在碰出口相关项目？
1.是出口货物（exported goods）吗？
一旦是，联邦不能直接征税。
2.不是货物，也要问：是不是紧密相关服务（closely related services）？
像给出口货物买保险这种，仍然被出口条款挡住。
3.别被“为了筹款”带偏。
就算目的合理，只要对象踩进出口条款，还是无效。
结论：本题这项保险费税 → 违宪 → 选 A

考点陷阱

你可能会想：这税是为了补贴海上保险业，看起来也算有财政目的，所以应该能过。

但考试真正问的是：税收对象是不是碰到了出口货物或出口过程紧密相关的服务。

司法考试看的是「法律程序上能不能救济」，而不是「物理上的秘密有没有泄露」。 这题同样是看“征税对象能不能碰”，不是看国会动机好不好看。

正确答案与干扰项排除

为什么选 A？

题干税的是给出口货物投保的保险费，这属于出口过程紧密相关项目，出口条款直接挡住联邦征税，所以违宪。

❌ 法律适用 | 目的相关误判

✕ B: 盯着raise revenue就想选，但目的正当也救不了出口税。

❌ 概念混淆 | 权力绝对化

✕ C: 把征税权想成unlimited，忽略了出口条款这道硬限制。

❌ 事实误判 | 审查标准偷换

✕ D: 把compelling government interest硬套进来，征税权这里不用这套标准。

这题建议用什么方法？

先抓征税对象，再看有没有出口条款禁区，别被“筹资目的”带跑。

考场速记

记忆口诀：出口相关就先停，联邦不能碰出口货物和紧密相关服务。

这类题只要看到出口税、出口保险、出口运输，先想：是不是已经踩进export clause 的禁区。

reason.en: The Export Clause reaches taxes on services closely related to exporting goods.
reason.zh: 出口条款涵盖对与货物出口密切相关的服务征税。

keywords.text: shipments of goods to foreign countries

reason.en: Shipment of goods abroad triggers the Export Clause prohibition.
reason.zh: 将货物运往国外触发出口条款的禁止规定。

reason.en: The stated subsidy purpose cannot validate a prohibited export tax.
reason.zh: 所述补贴目的不能使被禁止的出口税合法化。

keywords.text: filed a claim for a tax refund

reason.en: This establishes the company's procedural route for challenging the tax.
reason.zh: 这确立了公司挑战该税的程序途径。

keywords.text: goods exported to its foreign subsidiaries

reason.en: Actual exportation confirms that the taxed insurance covers protected export activity.
reason.zh: 实际出口证实被征税的保险涵盖受保护的出口活动。

reason.en: This identifies the ultimate issue for judicial resolution.
reason.zh: 这确定了法院需要解决的最终争议。

A.text: does not have the power to tax

reason.en: Congress's broad taxing power remains subject to the Export Clause.
reason.zh: 国会广泛的征税权仍受出口条款限制。

A.text: exported goods or closely related services

reason.en: This correctly includes both exported goods and services closely tied to exportation.
reason.zh: 这正确涵盖出口货物及与出口密切相关的服务。

B.text: does not reasonably relate to raising revenue

reason.en: The tax raises subsidy funds, and its revenue relationship does not cure the Export Clause violation.
reason.zh: 该税确实筹集补贴资金，且其收入关联不能消除对出口条款的违反。

label.zh: 征税权无限的错误表述

reason.en: Congress's taxing power is broad but expressly limited by other constitutional provisions.
reason.zh: 国会征税权虽广泛，但明确受其他宪法规定限制。

D.text: necessary to serve a compelling government interest

reason.en: A compelling interest cannot justify a federal tax prohibited by the Export Clause.
reason.zh: 重大政府利益不能为出口条款所禁止的联邦税提供正当理由。

highlights.text: imposing a tax on all insurance premiums for policies covering shipments of goods to foreign countries

reason.en: This directly describes a tax on services closely related to the export process.
reason.zh: 该表述直接说明这是对与出口过程密切相关的服务征税。

highlights.text: purpose of this export tax is to subsidize the marine insurance industry

reason.en: A public subsidy purpose does not create an exception to the Export Clause.
reason.zh: 公共补贴目的不会构成出口条款的例外。

highlights.text: goods exported to its foreign subsidiaries

reason.en: The foreign destination confirms that the insured goods are exports.
reason.zh: 境外目的地证实投保货物属于出口货物。

highlights.text: Is this federal tax likely constitutional?

reason.en: The issue requires applying a constitutional limitation on Congress's taxing power.
reason.zh: 该问题要求适用对国会征税权的宪法限制。

questions.subject: Constitutional Law
questions.question:
Congressional committees heard testimony from present and former holders of licenses issued by state vocational licensing boards. According to the testimony, the boards had unfairly manipulated their disciplinary proceedings in order to revoke the licenses of some license holders as a means of protecting favored licensees from competition.
In response, Congress enacted a statute prescribing detailed procedural requirements for the disciplinary proceedings of all state vocational licensing boards. The statute requires the state boards to provide licensees with adequate notice and opportunity for an adjudicatory hearing in all disciplinary proceedings. The statute also prescribes membership criteria for state vocational licensing boards, designed to ensure that the boards are likely to be neutral.
Which of the following provides the best source of authority for this federal statute?

choices.A: Section 5 of the Fourteenth Amendment.
choices.B: The general welfare clause of Article I, Section 8.
choices.C: The privileges and immunities clause of Article IV, Section 2.
choices.D: The takings clause of the Fifth Amendment.

questions.explanation:
Fourteenth Amendment protections
Clause Applicability
Equal protection Discriminatory treatment of similarly situated people
Due process Substantive – deprivation of life, liberty, or property without adequate justification
Procedural – deprivation of life, liberty, or property without adequate process
Privileges or
immunities*		 Interference with rights of national citizenship
*Rarely a correct answer.

Section 5 of the Fourteenth Amendment gives Congress the power to enact appropriate legislation to enforce the rights guaranteed by the amendment (eg, procedural due process). Legislation is appropriate under this section when it:

  • seeks to remedy or prevent state action that violates the Fourteenth Amendment and
  • is narrowly tailored—ie, its requirements are congruent with and proportional to the violations it addresses.

A violation of procedural due process occurs when the state fails to follow certain procedures when it intentionally deprives a person of a life, liberty, or property interest (eg, vocational license). These procedures include giving the person notice and a meaningful opportunity to be heard by a neutral decision-maker.

Here, state vocational licensing boards apparently violated procedural due process by unfairly manipulating their disciplinary proceedings. Congress attempted to remedy this by enacting a statute prescribing detailed procedural requirements for such proceedings in all states. This statute is narrowly tailored since its requirements—ie, adequate notice and a hearing before a neutral board—are the basic standards of procedural fairness. Therefore, section 5 of the Fourteenth Amendment is the best source of authority for this statute.

(Choice B) The Article I, section 8 general welfare clause empowers Congress to spend for the general welfare (ie, for any public purpose). But this clause does not apply because the statute is not a spending measure.

(Choice C) The privileges and immunities clause of Article IV, section 2 prohibits states from improperly discriminating against citizens of other states. Since this statute does not address discrimination against citizens of other states, this clause does not apply.

(Choice D) The Fifth Amendment takings clause prohibits governmental taking of private property for public use without just compensation. But this clause only applies to real or personal property—not vocational licenses.

📌 Educational Objective

Congress can enforce Fourteenth Amendment rights through legislation that (1) seeks to remedy or prevent state violations of the amendment and (2) is narrowly tailored—ie, its requirements are congruent with and proportional to the violations it addresses.

📚 References
  • Tennessee v. Lane, 541 U.S. 509, 520 (2004) (explaining that Congress can enact laws to remedy or prevent Fourteenth Amendment violations if there is congruence and proportionality between the injury and the law).
questions.zh-question:
国会委员会听取了由州职业执照颁发委员会签发执照的现任和前任持有者的证词。根据证词，这些委员会不公正地操纵其纪律处分程序，以撤销某些执照持有者的执照，以此作为保护受其偏袒的执照持有者免受竞争的一种手段。

作为回应，国会颁布了一项法规，为所有州职业执照颁发委员会的纪律处分程序规定了详细的程序性要求。该法规要求州委员会在所有纪律处分程序中，向执照持有者提供充分的通知和进行裁决听证的机会。该法规还规定了州职业执照颁发委员会的成员资格标准，旨在确保委员会可能保持中立。

以下哪一项为此联邦法规提供了最佳的权力来源？

zh-choices.A: 《第十四修正案》第五条。
zh-choices.B: 《第一条》第八款的普遍福利条款。
zh-choices.C: 《第四条》第二款的特权与豁免条款。
zh-choices.D: 《第五修正案》的征用条款。

questions.zh-explanation:
MBE 考点解析

Constitutional Law: Separation of Powers - Procedural Due Process Applied

本题真正考的是

一句话定位考点

本题真正考的是：国会能否用第十四修正案第5款，去纠正州职业执照机关对程序正当程序（procedural due process）的侵犯。

三秒认题路径：

州机关乱办案 → 剥夺执照 → 国会出规程 → 看第5款 → 能不能救济州侵权

核心法律规则

第十四修正案第5款（Section 5 of the Fourteenth Amendment）给国会权力去执行该修正案保障的权利，考场意思：国会可以针对州政府已经在违反宪法的地方出手纠正。

程序正当程序（procedural due process） 的考场意思：州要剥夺 生命、自由或财产利益（life, liberty, or property interest） 时，得给 通知（notice）、被听见的机会（opportunity to be heard），而且要在 中立决定者（neutral decision-maker） 面前进行。

国会立法要站得住，关键是 congruence and proportionality：既要想修补或预防州对第十四修正案的侵害，又要和问题的严重程度相称。这里州执照委员会被指控操纵纪律程序，所以国会要求统一的通知、听证和中立委员会，正好是在补程序正当程序的洞。

核心判例： Tennessee v. Lane — 说明国会可以在第5款下，用“成比例、相称”的方式修补或预防州对第十四修正案权利的侵犯。

思维导图

州职业执照纪律程序被指控偏袒，国会想用联邦法把程序标准统一起来？
先问：州有没有在 procedural due process 上出问题？
乱用纪律程序，剥夺执照利益
再问：国会立法是在补救州侵权，还是在做别的事？
要求通知 + 听证 + 中立委员会
关键卡点：规则是否 congruent and proportional？
卡死点：不是乱管全国，而是只把最基本的程序公平补上
结论：第5款给权力，选 A

考点陷阱

你可能会想：国会只是想“规范州执照机构”，所以是不是该找一般联邦权力来源。

但考试真正问的是：联邦法是不是在修补州对第十四修正案的违反，而不是在找一个泛泛的管理权限。

司法考试看的是「法律程序上能不能救济」，而不是「物理上的秘密有没有泄露」。

正确答案与干扰项排除

为什么选 A？

题干 state vocational licensing boards 被指控操纵纪律程序，正是在补救程序正当程序侵害；国会要求通知、听证和中立决定者，正好符合第5款的授权范围。

❌ 法律适用 | 花钱权误套

✕ B: 把 general welfare 当成管一切的权力，但这不是支出法案。

❌ 概念混淆 | 州际歧视错位

✕ C: 误把州际平等待遇条款拿来套，但题干根本没在讲外州公民歧视。

❌ 事实误判 | 财产权偷换

✕ D: 看到 takings 就联想补偿，但执照不是本题要保护的被征收财产。

这题建议用什么方法？

先看国会是在补救哪一种州违宪，再检查立法是否只是把最基本程序补齐。

考场速记

记住一句：国会要用第十四修正案第5款，得是“补救州侵权 + 成比例相称”。

如果题目在问联邦法能不能管州程序，先想：是不是在修补 procedural due process。是的话，优先看第5款。

keywords.text: licenses issued by state vocational licensing boards

reason.en: Vocational licenses are protected property interests for procedural due process purposes.
reason.zh: 职业执照属于受程序性正当程序保护的财产利益。

reason.en: State revocation triggers the requirement for constitutionally adequate procedures.
reason.zh: 州政府撤销执照会触发宪法所要求的适当程序。

reason.en: Adequate notice is a core safeguard of procedural due process.
reason.zh: 充分通知是程序性正当程序的核心保障。

label.zh: 有意义的陈述意见机会

reason.en: A meaningful hearing is required before the state deprives a person of a protected license.
reason.zh: 州政府剥夺受保护的执照前，必须提供有意义的听证机会。

reason.en: Decision-maker neutrality is another basic component of procedural due process.
reason.zh: 裁决者的中立性也是程序性正当程序的基本组成部分。

reason.en: This provision authorizes congruent and proportional legislation enforcing procedural due process against states.
reason.zh: 该条款授权国会制定相称且成比例的立法，以对州执行程序性正当程序保障。

reason.en: The clause supports spending measures, but this statute regulates state procedures without spending funds.
reason.zh: 该条款支持支出措施，但本法是在不涉及联邦支出的情况下规制州程序。

reason.en: This clause concerns discrimination against out-of-state citizens, which the statute does not address.
reason.zh: 该条款针对对外州公民的歧视，而本法并未处理此类问题。

reason.en: License revocation implicates procedural due process rather than a taking for public use.
reason.zh: 撤销执照涉及程序性正当程序，而非为公共用途征收财产。

highlights.text: the boards had unfairly manipulated their disciplinary proceedings in order to revoke the licenses

label.zh: 州违反程序性正当程序

reason.en: This identifies state action depriving licensees of protected interests through unfair procedures.
reason.zh: 该事实表明州通过不公正程序剥夺执照持有人的受保护利益。

highlights.text: provide licensees with adequate notice and opportunity for an adjudicatory hearing

reason.en: Notice and a hearing directly remedy the identified procedural due process violations.
reason.zh: 通知和听证直接补救所发现的程序性正当程序侵害。

highlights.text: designed to ensure that the boards are likely to be neutral

reason.en: Neutrality makes the statute closely tailored to constitutional procedural requirements.
reason.zh: 中立性要求使该法规与宪法程序要求紧密对应。

highlights.text: all state vocational licensing boards

reason.en: Because the regulated entities are state boards, Fourteenth Amendment enforcement power is implicated.
reason.zh: 由于受规制实体是州委员会，因此涉及第十四修正案执行权。

questions.subject: Constitutional Law
questions.question:
A statute passed by both houses of Congress and signed by the President created a federal agency to regulate consumer financial products such as credit cards, student loans, and mortgages. The federal statute authorizes the agency to issue regulatory rules, conduct administrative proceedings, and initiate suits in federal court on behalf of consumers. A statutory provision establishes that the agency is led by a single director who must be appointed by the President with the advice and consent of the Senate. The provision also states that the director serves a five-year term and can only be removed from office by the President for good cause.
Is the provision allowing the director to be removed by the President for good cause constitutional?

choices.A: No, because the President may remove a federal executive officer only with the advice and consent of the Senate.
choices.B: No, because the provision amounts to an unconstitutional legislative interference with an executive function.
choices.C: Yes, because Congress may require the President to show good cause to remove a federal executive officer.
choices.D: Yes, because the provision is part of a statute that was passed by both houses of Congress and signed by the President.

questions.explanation:
Appointment and removal of executive officers

The Constitution divides the federal government into three coequal branches that possess distinct powers (ie, separation of powers). Article II vests the executive power in the President, including the power to faithfully execute federal laws. Since it is impossible for one person to carry out this power, federal executive officers may be appointed pursuant to the appointments clause to assist the President.

The Constitution is silent about the removal of federal executive officers, but the U.S. Supreme Court has repeatedly held that the President has absolute authority to remove such officers absent two exceptions. This means that Congress cannot impose any removal restrictions, including good-cause requirements, except for officers who either:

  • belong to a multimember body that is balanced along partisan lines and exercises no executive power (eg, committees that conduct investigations on behalf of Congress) or
  • lack policymaking or administrative authority (eg, independent counsel who investigates and prosecutes alleged crimes by government officials).

Here, Congress created a federal agency headed by a single director. The director exercises significant executive power and administrative authority by issuing regulatory rules, conducting administrative proceedings, and initiating suits in federal court. As a result, the President has the absolute authority to remove the director. The provision requiring good cause for removal therefore amounts to an unconstitutional legislative interference with an executive function (Choice C).

(Choice A) The President must appoint certain federal executive officers (eg, cabinet secretaries) with the advice and consent of the Senate. However, the Senate's advice and consent is not required for the President to remove such officers.

(Choice D) The removal provision is part of a statute that satisfied the federal legislative process because it was passed by both houses of Congress and signed by the President. But the provision is still an unconstitutional legislative interference with an executive power.

📌 Educational Objective

The President has absolute authority to remove federal executive officers. Congress may impose restrictions on this power only for officers who (1) belong to a multimember body that is balanced along partisan lines and exercises no executive power or (2) lack policymaking or administrative authority.

📚 References
  • Seila Law Ltd. Liab. Corp. v. Consumer Fin. Prot. Bureau, 140 S. Ct. 2183, 2197–2200 (2020) (explaining that the President has the absolute power to remove federal executive officers subject to very narrow exceptions).
questions.zh-question:
由国会两院通过并经总统签署的一项法规设立了一个联邦机构，以监管信用卡、学生贷款和抵押贷款等消费金融产品。该联邦法规授权该机构发布监管规则、进行行政程序，并代表消费者在联邦法院提起诉讼。一项法规条款规定，该机构由一名单一的主任领导，该主任必须由总统经参议院建议和同意后任命。该条款还规定，该主任任期五年，且只有在有正当理由（good cause）的情况下才能被总统免职。

允许总统以正当理由免去该主任职务的条款是否合宪？

zh-choices.A: 否，因为总统只有在获得参议院的建议和同意后才能罢免联邦行政官员。
zh-choices.B: 否，因为该条款构成了对行政职能的违宪立法干预。
zh-choices.C: 是，因为国会可以要求总统在罢免联邦行政官员时须有正当理由。
zh-choices.D: 是，因为该条款是经国会两院通过并由总统签署的法规的一部分。

questions.zh-explanation:
MBE 考点解析

Constitutional Law: Separation of Powers - Domestic Power

本题真正考的是

一句话定位考点

本题真正考的是：国会能不能用“good cause”卡住总统对单一行政首长的撤换权。

三秒认题路径：

单一局长 → 总统任命 → good cause限撤免 → 行政权受卡 → 通常违宪

核心法律规则

总统撤免权（removal power）的默认规则是：President 对行使执行权的联邦官员通常可以直接撤免，不需要国会替他加一道门槛。good cause 限制考场意思：国会不是不能碰撤免问题，但只能在非常窄的例外里动手。

这里的关键是，单一主任（single director）还拥有制规、行政裁决和起诉权，属于实打实的行政权；所以把撤免改成“只能有正当理由”就是在直接掐总统的执行链条。

核心判例： Seila Law LLC v. CFPB — 单一首长 + 强行政权 + good cause 撤免限制，结论就是通常违宪。

思维导图

先看：这是不是在卡总统撤免执行官？
是：单一主任，负责制规、裁决、起诉，明显在做行政工作。
默认规则：总统对这类执行官通常有撤免权。
卡死点：Congress 不能随便加 good cause 门槛；这会把执行权绑住。
例外检查：只有极窄例外才可能保留限制，比如多成员、两党平衡、且不行使执行权，或根本没有政策/行政权。
本题落点：两条例外都不在。
结论：good cause 条款违宪 → 选 No，理由是国会非法干预行政权。

考点陷阱

你可能会想：既然法案是国会两院通过、总统也签了，那撤免条款当然有效。

但考试真正问的是：国会有没有权限把总统的执行权“锁死”一部分；答案是没有。

司法考试看的是「法律程序上能不能救济」，而不是「物理上的秘密有没有泄露」。

正确答案与干扰项排除

为什么选 B？

题干写的是单一主任被赋予实质行政权，却又被 good cause 锁住撤免；这就是国会对行政权的越界干预。

❌ 概念混淆 | 任命撤免错位

✕ A: 把 advice and consent 误当成撤免也要 Senate 点头。

❌ 法律适用 | 例外范围误读

✕ C: 题干是单一执行官，不是能随便加 good cause 的窄例外。

❌ 事实误判 | 程序通过偷换

✕ D: 通过了立法程序，不代表这个条款就没碰到行政权边界。

这题建议用什么方法？

先认撤免权，再看官员类型；只要是单一强执行官，good cause 限制就先高度可疑。

考场速记

记住一句：总统管执行官，国会别乱卡撤免；单一首长 + 实质行政权 + good cause，优先想到 Seila Law。

再补一句口诀：In Certain Circumstances, An Appeal Can Be Made Prematurely 是中间上诉记忆法，但这题不需要上诉例外，重点只在撤免权。

questions.subject: Constitutional Law
questions.question:
Congress enacted a statute that authorized the construction of a monument commemorating the role of the United States in liberating a particular foreign nation during World War II. Another statute appropriated $3 million for the construction.
When the United States became involved in a bitter trade dispute with the foreign nation, the President announced that he was canceling the monument's construction and that he would not spend the appropriated funds. Although the actual reason for the President's decision was the trade dispute, the announcement stated that the reason was an unexpected rise in the federal deficit.
Assume that no other statutes apply.
Is the President's decision constitutional?

choices.A: No, because the President failed to invoke his foreign affairs powers in his announcement.
choices.B: No, because the President is obligated to spend funds in accordance with congressional directions.
choices.C: Yes, because the President is vested with inherent executive power to control federal expenditures.
choices.D: Yes, because the President's decision is a valid exercise of his foreign affairs powers.

questions.explanation:
Congress's taxing & spending powers (U.S. Const. art. I, sec. 8, cl. 1)
Taxing
  • Direct taxes – must be:
    • apportioned evenly among states and
    • reasonably related to revenue raising
  • Indirect taxes – must be:
    • uniformly applied in every state and
    • reasonably related to revenue raising
  • Export taxes – always unconstitutional
Spending
  • Funds must be spent for general welfare
  • Conditions on receipt of funds must:
    • be clearly stated & unambiguous
    • be reasonably related to federal interest in funded program
    • not require states to engage in unconstitutional activity and
    • not unduly coerce states into accepting

The taxing and spending clause gives Congress very broad spending power, which it exercises by proposing appropriations bills. Once an appropriations bill becomes law, the President must spend the appropriated funds as specifically directed in the law. That is because Article II obligates the President to take care that the laws are faithfully executed. Therefore, the President's decision not to spend the appropriated funds for the monument's construction is unconstitutional.

(Choices A & D) The President can never refuse to spend funds that are subject to a mandatory appropriation—even where foreign affairs are directly involved.

(Choice C) The Constitution does not vest the President with inherent executive power to control federal expenditures. Instead, the President must spend federal funds in accordance with congressional directives.

📌 Educational Objective

An appropriations statute is a valid exercise of Congress's spending power. And the President must take care that the law is faithfully executed by spending the appropriated funds as specifically directed in the statute.

📚 References
  • U.S. Const. art. II, § 3 (take care clause).
  • Train v. New York, 420 U.S. 35, 41 (1975) (requiring the EPA Administrator to spend the full amount authorized by the valid federal statute despite the President's order to withhold such funds).
  • 63C Am. Jur. 2d Public Funds § 37 (2019) (explaining that the President and the executive branch do not have the power to impound congressionally appropriated funds).
questions.zh-question:
国会颁布了一项法令，授权建造一座纪念碑，以纪念美国在第二次世界大战期间解放某个特定外国所扮演的角色。另一项法令为该建设拨款300万美元。

当美国与该外国卷入激烈的贸易争端时，总统宣布他将取消纪念碑的建造，并且他不会支出这笔已拨款的资金。尽管总统做出此项决定的真实原因是贸易争端，但公告中声称的原因是联邦赤字的意外上升。

假设没有其他法令适用。

总统的决定是否合宪？

zh-choices.A: 否，因为总统在他的公告中未能援引其外交事务权力。
zh-choices.B: 否，因为总统有义务根据国会的指示支出资金。
zh-choices.C: 是，因为总统被授予控制联邦支出的固有行政权力。
zh-choices.D: 是，因为总统的决定是对其外交事务权力的有效行使。

questions.zh-explanation:
MBE 考点解析

Constitutional Law: Separation of Powers - Taxation And Spending

本题真正考的是

一句话定位考点

本题真正考的是：国会已经通过并拨款后，总统（President）能不能因为自己不同意而拒绝执行这笔强制性支出。

三秒认题路径：

已拨款 → 总统拒花 → 有无裁量 → Take Care Clause → 不能拒付

核心法律规则

拨款法（appropriations statute）一旦生效，总统（President）就要按国会写的用途去花钱。忠实执行条款（Take Care Clause）的考场意思：行政部门负责执行法律，不是挑着执行。

所以，只要国会明确拨了这笔钱，总统（President）就不能把它“扣住”不花，这种做法叫 impoundment，本题通常不被允许。

核心判例： Train v. New York —— 最高法院要求行政官员按法定数额把钱花完，不能用总统命令把国会拨款扣住。

思维导图

先看：这是不是国会已经生效的拨款（appropriation）？
是国会授权建纪念碑，又另拨 $3 million。
再看：总统（President）能不能自己决定不花？
默认不能。Take Care Clause 要求他执行法律，不是改写预算。
卡死点：就算借口写成“财政赤字”，也改变不了国会已定用途。
结论：终局答案是 B，因为必须按国会指令支出。
否如果不是强制拨款，才可能讨论别的裁量；本题不是这个路子。

考点陷阱

你可能会想：总统说自己是为了foreign affairs，是不是就能停掉这笔钱。

但考试真正问的是：国会已经立法拨款后，行政部门能不能自己改成“不执行”。

司法考试看的是「法律程序上能不能救济」，而不是「物理上的秘密有没有泄露」。

本题里真正致命的不是外交冲突，而是总统把国会命令当成可选项。

正确答案与干扰项排除

为什么选 B？

题干已经有国会拨款与明确用途，总统却决定不花这笔 appropriated funds，所以违反了按国会指令执行法律的要求。

❌ 概念混淆 | 规则渊源误判

✕ A: 把外交理由当成权限来源，foreign affairs 不是停拨款的开关。

❌ 法律适用 | 总统裁量误套

✕ C: 以为总统能自己管联邦开支，但国会已定用途时他没有这种 inherent executive 权力。

❌ 事实误判 | 外交借口偷换

✕ D: 题干只有贸易争端，没有给总统独立改写拨款的授权。

这题建议用什么方法？

先看是不是国会已拨款，再直接问总统有没有扣款不花的裁量。

考场速记

记住一句：国会拨款 → 行政执行，不是总统想停就停。

遇到中间上诉才背这个口诀：In Certain Circumstances, An Appeal Can Be Made Prematurely，对应 injunction、certification、class action 等法定例外；本题不是上诉题，但同样要先看谁有最终决定权。

questions.subject: Constitutional Law
questions.question:
Congress passed a bill prohibiting the President from granting a pardon to any person who has not served at least one-third of the sentence imposed by the court that convicted the person. The President vetoed the bill, claiming that it was unconstitutional. Nevertheless, Congress passed it over his veto by a two-thirds vote of each house.
Is this act of Congress constitutional?

choices.A: No, because a presidential veto based upon constitutional grounds may be overridden only with the concurrence of three-fourths of the state legislatures.
choices.B: No, because it interferes with the plenary power of the President to grant pardons.
choices.C: Yes, because it is a necessary and proper means of carrying out the powers of Congress.
choices.D: Yes, because it was enacted over the President's veto by a two-thirds vote of each house.

questions.explanation:
The Constitution gives each branch of government separate and distinct powers that generally cannot be exercised by another branch. This establishes a system of checks and balances that prevents concentration of power. The President (i.e., executive branch) has the distinct power to enforce laws. This includes the plenary (i.e., absolute) power to grant reprieves and pardons to persons who commit federal offenses (except in cases of impeachment). And since the other branches cannot interfere with this power in any way, this act of Congress is unconstitutional.

(Choice A) Article II grants the President the power to veto a bill for any reason, which can only be overridden by a two-thirds vote in each house of Congress. A three-fourths vote of the state legislatures is generally part of the constitutional amendment process—not the federal legislative process.

(Choice C) The necessary and proper clause gives Congress the power to use reasonably appropriate means to carry out its other powers. But it cannot violate other constitutional provisions when doing so (as seen here).

(Choice D) Although the bill was enacted into law over the President's veto by a two-thirds vote of each house of Congress, it is unconstitutional since it interferes with the President's plenary power to issue pardons.

📌 Educational Objective

Under the separation-of-powers doctrine, each branch of government has separate and distinct powers that generally cannot be exercised by another branch—e.g., Congress and the judiciary cannot interfere with the President's plenary power to grant reprieves and pardons.

📚 References
  • U.S. Const. art. II, § 2, cl. 1 (pardon power).
  • Schick v. Reed, 419 U.S. 256, 266 (1974) (stating that Congress cannot alter the President's pardon power).
questions.zh-question:
国会通过了一项法案，禁止总统向任何未服满定罪法院所判刑期至少三分之一的人授予赦免。总统以该法案违宪为由予以否决。尽管如此，国会以两院三分之二的多数票推翻了总统的否决。

国会的这项法案是否合宪？

zh-choices.A: 不合宪，因为基于宪法理由的总统否决，只有在获得四分之三州立法机构的同意后才能被推翻。
zh-choices.B: 不合宪，因为它干涉了总统授予赦免的绝对权力。
zh-choices.C: 合宪，因为这是国会行使其权力的一种必要且适当的手段。
zh-choices.D: 合宪，因为它是国会两院以三分之二的多数票推翻总统否决后颁布的。

questions.zh-explanation:
MBE 考点解析

Constitutional Law: Separation of Powers - Domestic Power

本题真正考的是

一句话定位考点

本题真正考的是：国会能不能用立法限制总统的赦免权（pardon power）；答案是不能，因为这是总统的专属权力。

三秒认题路径：

国会限赦免 → 总统否决 → 仍被推翻 → 但碰到专属权力 → 还是违宪

核心法律规则

只记这条就够做题

《宪法》赋予总统赦免权（pardon power），考场意思：这是总统自己能做、国会不能插手改条件的权力。国会可以立法，但不能把总统的赦免权改成“必须先服满三分之一刑期才行”。

因此，哪怕法案已经被两院三分之二票数推翻了总统否决，违宪这个结论也不会变；问题不在于法案有没有通过，而在于它有没有碰到总统的专属权力边界。

核心判例： Schick v. Reed — 国会不能改写总统的赦免权，所以附加这种服刑门槛的法律无效。

思维导图

先问：这是国会立法在管总统的专属权力吗？
是 碰到赦免权（pardon power）就卡死：国会不能附加“先服刑三分之一”这种条件。
再看 总统虽已否决，但法案被两院三分之二推翻，只说明它成了法；不说明它就合宪。
结论 只要立法干预总统的专属赦免权，最终答案就是：No，选 B。
顺手排除：别把“通过程序”当成“实体合宪”。

考点陷阱

你可能会想：既然国会已经用两院三分之二把总统否决推翻了，那这个法案应该就稳了。

但考试真正问的是：国会有没有权力去改总统的赦免权（pardon power），而不是这部法案有没有走完立法程序。

司法考试看的是「法律程序上能不能救济」，而不是「物理上的秘密有没有泄露」。 这里同样是看权力边界，不是看政治上谁赢了。

正确答案与干扰项排除

为什么选 B？

题干直接限制总统的pardon条件，国会越界碰到总统专属权力，所以结论就是违宪。

❌ 概念混淆 | 否决覆写误判

这题建议用什么方法？

考场速记

记忆口诀：总统的赦免权（pardon power）是专属权力，国会不能加条件、不能改门槛；“通过了”不等于“合宪了”。

遇到权力分配题，先问：这是不是某一分支的专属权力？是的话，另一分支通常不能插手。

questions.subject: Constitutional Law
questions.topic: Power To Enforce The Thirteenth, Fourteenth, And Fifteenth Amendments (Civil War Amendments)
questions.question:
A proposed federal statute would prohibit all types of discrimination against minorities on the basis of their race in every business transaction executed anywhere in the United States by any person or entity, governmental or private.
Is this proposed federal statute likely to be constitutional?

choices.A: No, because it would invade the powers reserved to the states by the Tenth Amendment.
choices.B: No, because it would regulate purely local transactions that are not in interstate commerce.
choices.C: Yes, because it could reasonably be viewed as a means of enforcing the provisions of the Thirteenth Amendment.
choices.D: Yes, because it could reasonably be viewed as an exercise of Congress's authority to enact laws for the general welfare.

questions.explanation:
Congress's power to enforce the Civil War Amendments
Amendment Effects Congress's enforcement powers
Thirteenth Prohibits government & private actors from engaging in slavery/involuntary servitude
  • Prohibit badges/incidents of slavery
  • Override state 11th Amendment immunity
Fourteenth Prohibits states from denying equal protection, due process, or privileges/immunities of national citizenship
  • Remedy/prevent violations with proportional & congruent legislation
  • Override state 11th Amendment immunity
Fifteenth Prohibits states & federal government from denying or abridging voting rights based on race, color, or previous servitude
  • Ban methods of voter discrimination
  • Override state 11th Amendment immunity

Section 1 of the Thirteenth Amendment prohibits all government and private entities from engaging in slavery or involuntary servitude. And the Section 2 enforcement clause gives Congress the power to forbid any racial discrimination that can reasonably be viewed as a "badge or incident of slavery" (eg, discrimination in housing, education, or employment). Since racial discrimination against minorities in business transactions can reasonably be viewed as a relic of slavery, the proposed federal statute banning this conduct is likely constitutional.

(Choice A) The Tenth Amendment reserves to the states all powers that the Constitution does not expressly grant to the federal government (eg, police powers). But the Thirteenth Amendment expressly grants Congress the authority to enact legislation addressing slavery and involuntary servitude (as seen here).

(Choice B) The fact that the statute would regulate purely local transactions that do not have a substantial effect on interstate commerce shows that it cannot be supported by the commerce clause. But Congress can still enact this statute pursuant to its power to enforce the Thirteenth Amendment.

(Choice D) The taxing and spending clause gives Congress the authority to tax or spend for the general welfare—not to enact any type of law for this purpose (eg, prohibiting discrimination).

📌 Educational Objective

The Thirteenth Amendment (1) prohibits all government and private entities from engaging in slavery or involuntary servitude and (2) empowers Congress to ban any type of racial discrimination that can reasonably be viewed as a badge or incident of slavery.

📚 References
  • Patterson v. McLean Credit Union, 491 U.S. 164, 192 (1989) (explaining that the Thirteenth Amendment empowers Congress to identify the badges and incidents of slavery and to legislate to end them).

zh-choices.B: 否，因为它将监管不属于州际贸易的纯粹地方性交易。
zh-choices.C: 是，因为它可以被合理地视为执行 Thirteenth Amendment 条款的一种方式。

questions.zh-explanation:
MBE 考点解析

Constitutional Law: Separation of Powers - Power To Enforce The Thirteenth, Fourteenth, And Fifteenth Amendments (Civil War Amendments)

本题真正考的是

一句话定位考点

本题真正考的是：国会能不能用第十三修正案（Thirteenth Amendment）的执行权，禁止全国范围内一切针对少数族裔的种族歧视。

三秒认题路径：

私人交易歧视 → 第十三修正案 → badges/incidents → 国会可禁 → 选 C

核心法律规则

只抓这条规则

第十三修正案（Thirteenth Amendment）第1款直接禁止奴隶制（slavery）和强迫劳役（involuntary servitude），对象不只限于政府，也包括私人。

第2款给国会执行权（enforcement power），可以禁止任何合理上可看成badges or incidents of slavery的种族歧视，所以这里的商业歧视法案可以落在这个口袋里。

这不是靠商业条款（commerce clause）硬撑，也不是靠“为了公益就能立法”的泛化说法；本题真正的授权来源是第十三修正案。

核心判例：Patterson v. McLean Credit Union — 说明国会可以识别并清除奴隶制的“标记与残余”，所以种族歧视法案可被第十三修正案托住。

思维导图

题干先问：国会能不能管“所有人、所有地点、所有商业交易”里的种族歧视？
先找授权：不是先看商业条款，而是先看第十三修正案（Thirteenth Amendment）。
第1步：它管的是奴隶制/强迫劳役，并且直接约束私人。
第2步：国会可打击badges or incidents of slavery，也就是奴隶制遗留痕迹。
卡死点：商业歧视可被看成奴隶制残余，所以不必被commerce clause卡住。
结论：法案可合宪，选 C。

考点陷阱

你可能会想：这法案管的是全国范围内的私人交易，像是在抢州的权力，或者它不是典型商业活动，所以国会没权管。

但考试真正问的是：第十三修正案（Thirteenth Amendment）本身就给了国会打击奴隶制残余的权力，不必绕到commerce clause或第十修正案（Tenth Amendment）。

司法考试看的是「法律程序上能不能救济」，而不是「物理上的秘密有没有泄露」。这题对应的思路也是一样：先找真正的宪法授权，再不要被“地方性”“私人交易”这些表面词带跑。

正确答案与干扰项排除

为什么选 C？

题干的种族歧视可以合理看成奴隶制的残余，第十三修正案（Thirteenth Amendment）允许国会直接禁止这种做法，所以法案合宪。

❌ 概念混淆 | 规授权源误判

✕ A: 把Tenth Amendment当成绝对挡板，忽略了第十三修正案本来就给了国会权力。

❌ 法律适用 | 商业条款误套

✕ B: 只盯interstate commerce，忘了这里还有别的宪法授权来源。

❌ 事实误判 | 公益授权偷换

✕ D: 把general welfare说成万能立法权，其实它不是任意禁歧视的空白支票。

这题建议用什么方法？

先找国会授权来源，再判断题干是不是奴隶制残余（badge or incident of slavery）。

考场速记

记住这句：第十三修正案不仅禁奴隶制，也让国会能清理它的“残余痕迹”；看到种族歧视、住房、教育、就业这类题，先想这条。

口诀：“看见奴隶制残余，先找第十三修正案；看见私人歧视，不要只盯商业条款。”

reason.en: Requires identifying an enumerated constitutional source of congressional authority.
reason.zh: 需要确定国会立法权的宪法依据。

reason.en: Defines the broad conduct Congress seeks to prohibit.
reason.zh: 界定国会试图禁止的广泛行为。

keywords.text: on the basis of their race

reason.en: Connects the statute to badges or incidents of slavery under the Thirteenth Amendment.
reason.zh: 将该法规与第十三修正案下的奴隶制标志或遗留影响联系起来。

reason.en: Shows that the prohibition extends beyond governmental conduct.
reason.zh: 表明该禁令不仅适用于政府行为。

reason.en: The Thirteenth Amendment permits congressional regulation of both governmental and private conduct.
reason.zh: 第十三修正案允许国会规制政府和私人行为。

reason.en: The Tenth Amendment does not limit a power expressly granted by the Thirteenth Amendment.
reason.zh: 第十修正案不限制第十三修正案明确授予国会的权力。

label.zh: 第十修正案联邦主义保留原则

reason.en: It is inapplicable because Congress has an express enforcement power here.
reason.zh: 因国会在此拥有明确的执行权，该修正案不适用。

reason.en: Locality may limit Commerce Clause authority but not Thirteenth Amendment enforcement power.
reason.zh: 地方性可能限制商业条款权力，但不限制第十三修正案执行权。

reason.en: The statute need not rely on the Commerce Clause.
reason.zh: 该法规无需以商业条款为依据。

reason.en: Congress may reasonably identify racial discrimination as a badge or incident of slavery.
reason.zh: 国会可合理认定种族歧视属于奴隶制的标志或遗留影响。

C.text: enforcing the provisions of the Thirteenth Amendment

reason.en: This is the correct constitutional source for regulating the described private racial discrimination.
reason.zh: 这是规制题述私人种族歧视的正确宪法依据。

reason.en: Congress must rely on a constitutionally granted legislative power.
reason.zh: 国会必须依据宪法授予的立法权。

label.zh: 一般福利税收与支出目的

reason.en: The general welfare language authorizes taxing and spending, not an independent regulatory power.
reason.zh: 一般福利条款授权征税和支出，而非独立的规制权。

highlights.text: discrimination against minorities on the basis of their race

label.zh: 与奴隶制相关的种族歧视

reason.en: Racial discrimination may be treated as a badge or incident of slavery.
reason.zh: 种族歧视可被视为奴隶制的标志或遗留影响。

highlights.text: in every business transaction

reason.en: The statute reaches discrimination in commercial dealings regardless of their location.
reason.zh: 该法规规制商业交易中的歧视，不受交易地点限制。

highlights.text: governmental or private

reason.en: Unlike the Fourteenth Amendment, the Thirteenth Amendment can reach private conduct.
reason.zh: 与第十四修正案不同，第十三修正案可以规制私人行为。

highlights.text: likely to be constitutional

reason.en: Frames the need to identify a valid source of congressional authority.
reason.zh: 要求确定国会立法权的有效宪法来源。

questions.subject: Constitutional Law
questions.question:
A U.S. senator made a speech on the floor of the Senate accusing a low-level purchasing officer employed by a federal agency of wasting millions of dollars of taxpayer money by purchasing many more office supplies than the agency needed. The accusation was demonstrably false, and the senator was negligent in making it.
The purchasing officer has sued the senator for defamation, alleging only that the accusation was false and that the senator was negligent.
What is the most appropriate ground for the court to dismiss the purchasing officer's complaint?

choices.A: The federal government is constitutionally immune from suit without its consent, and it has not consented to suits of this kind.
choices.B: The First Amendment guarantees members of Congress an unqualified right to speak on matters of public concern at any place and time without having to fear adverse legal consequences.
choices.C: The First Amendment protects public officials from defamation liability for statements made in their official capacity, unless the plaintiff alleges and proves that the statement was false and uttered with actual malice.
choices.D: The speech or debate clause of Article I, section 6 of the Constitution wholly insulates members of Congress from tort liability for statements made on the floor of Congress.

questions.explanation:
Speech or debate clause
(immunity for members of Congress & their aides)
Conduct Examples Immunity
Legislative
activity
  • Statements made on House or Senate floor
  • Drafting & enacting legislation
  • Conducting investigations & research
  • Committee hearings & reports
  • Preparing & distributing reports within Congress
 Immunity from criminal &
civil liability
Nonlegislative
activity
  • Statements made outside Congress
  • Republishing statements made in Congress
  • Writing newsletters & press releases
  • Bribery
 No immunity

Under the speech or debate clause of Article I, section 6, members of Congress are immune from criminal and civil liability for any official legislative activity—eg, speeches given on the House or Senate floor. This ensures that members of Congress are free to represent their constituents' interests without fear that they will later be liable in court for that representation.

Here, the senator made a speech on the Senate floor that falsely and negligently accused the purchasing officer of wasting millions of dollars of taxpayer money. Therefore, the most appropriate ground for the court to dismiss the officer's complaint is that the speech or debate clause wholly insulates the senator from tort liability.

(Choice A) The federal government is constitutionally immune from suit without its consent. However, this immunity does not extend to suits against federal legislators in their individual capacities (as seen here).

(Choice B) Members of Congress do not have an unqualified right to speak on matters of public concern without fear of adverse legal consequences. But the speech or debate clause insulates them from liability for any speech that occurs in the course of official legislative activity.

(Choice C) The First Amendment heightens the standard for proving defamation when the plaintiff is a prominent public official. In that case, the plaintiff must prove that the defendant's statement was false and made with actual malice. But the speech or debate clause protects members of Congress from defamation liability for statements made in their official capacity—regardless of whether the plaintiff can meet that heightened standard.

📌 Educational Objective

The speech or debate clause immunizes members of Congress from criminal and civil liability for official legislative activities—eg, speeches given on the House or Senate floor.

📚 References
  • Hutchinson v. Proxmire, 443 U.S. 111, 130 (1979) (stating that a speech made on the Senate floor would be wholly immune from a defamation suit).
  • 77 Am. Jur. 2d United States § 7 (2019) (explaining that the speech or debate clause grants legislative immunity).
questions.zh-question:
一名美国参议员在参议院议场发表演讲，指控某联邦机构的一名低级别采购员因采购了远超该机构所需数量的办公用品，而浪费了数百万美元的纳税人资金。该指控明显是虚假的，且该参议员在提出指控时存在过失。

该采购员以诽谤为由起诉了该参议员，仅指控该言论是虚假的且参议员存在过失。

法院驳回该采购员诉状的最恰当理由是什么？

zh-choices.A: 联邦政府未经其同意享有宪法规定的诉讼豁免权，且其并未同意此类诉讼。
zh-choices.B: 第一修正案保障国会议员享有在任何时间、任何地点就公共关注事务发表言论的绝对权利，而无需担心承担不利的法律后果。
zh-choices.C: 第一修正案保护公职人员在以其官方身份发表言论时免于承担诽谤责任，除非原告指控并证明该言论是虚假的且带有实际恶意。
zh-choices.D: 宪法第一条第六款的言论或辩论条款，使国会议员完全免于因在国会议场上发表的言论而承担侵权责任。

questions.zh-explanation:
MBE 考点解析

Constitutional Law: Separation of Powers - Immunities And Privileges

本题真正考的是

一句话定位考点

本题真正考的是：国会议员在国会山庄内的正式立法言论，是否受到《宪法》第一条第六款 言论或辩论条款（speech or debate clause） 保护，所以能不能直接被告诽谤。

三秒认题路径：

国会发言 → Senate floor → 立法活动 → 绝对豁免 → 直接驳回

核心法律规则

《宪法》第一条第六款的 言论或辩论条款（speech or debate clause），保护国会议员在正式立法活动（official legislative activity）中的言行，考场意思：只要是议场内履职，就能挡住刑事和民事责任。

在参议院或众议院发言（speech on the floor） 就是最典型的立法活动，考场意思：这不是“普通说话”，而是职务行为，所以即使内容是假的、也可能是疏忽说错了，仍然先被免责任。

这类保护比 actual malice 还强，考场意思：原告就算能证明诽谤的传统要件，也还是会被这道宪法豁免先拦下。

核心判例： Hutchinson v. Proxmire — 最高法院明确说，参议院议场上的发言，对诽谤诉讼是全面豁免的。

思维导图

先看这句是不是 国会正式立法活动（official legislative activity）？
YES： Senate floor 发言 → 立法活动核心区 → 言论或辩论条款（speech or debate clause） 直接保护
结果： 民事诽谤诉讼也挡掉
NO： 议场外重述、通讯、新闻稿、招待应酬 → 通常不受保护
本题结论： 选 D：议场发言享有绝对豁免

考点陷阱

你可能会想：既然原告只是告 诽谤（defamation），那就去套 actual malice 和“公众人物”那套标准。

但考试真正问的是：这不是在比“诽谤证明门槛”，而是在问国会议员在 议场发言（speech on the floor） 这一步，先不先被宪法豁免挡住。

司法考试看的是「法律程序上能不能救济」，而不是「物理上的秘密有没有泄露」。

正确答案与干扰项排除

为什么选 D？

题干关键点是 Senate floor 发言；这属于正式立法活动，所以 言论或辩论条款（speech or debate clause） 直接给国会议员民事豁免。

❌ 概念混淆 | 主体豁免误判

✕ A: 把 federal government 的主权豁免，偷换成议员个人责任。

❌ 法律适用 | 言论自由误套

✕ B: 把 public concern 当成国会议员的无限发言通行证。

❌ 事实误判 | 公众官员混淆

✕ C: 误把 actual malice 当成本题的决定门槛。

这题建议用什么方法？

先抓发言地点和身份，再问是不是立法活动；是的话，直接看宪法豁免，不要先套诽谤标准。

考场速记

记住一句：国会正式立法活动（official legislative activity），就先想 言论或辩论条款（speech or debate clause）。

这题的速记口诀是：议场内发言，先看豁免；议场外行为，才谈责任。

question_analysis.skill_tested: Identify legislative immunity for floor speech

reason.en: Identifies a person protected by the Speech or Debate Clause.
reason.zh: 表明该主体属于言论或辩论条款保护的人员。

keywords.text: on the floor of the Senate

reason.en: Places the statement within protected legislative activity.
reason.zh: 表明该言论属于受保护的立法活动。

reason.en: Would support defamation liability absent legislative immunity.

questions.subject: Constitutional Law
questions.question:
At a hearing on legislation supported by the president, a senator made a slanderous statement about the president. Later that day, the senator, during an interview with a reporter, repeated the statement, seeking to motivate citizens to contact their congresspersons and encourage them to vote against the legislation. After learning of the senator's statement, the president made an official statement at a press conference maligning the senator, falsely accusing her of taking bribes, and encouraging the rest of the Senate to vote in favor of the legislation.
If a civil suit for money damages is filed against either the president or the senator because of the statements, who may properly be held liable?

choices.A: Both the president and the senator, because each exceeded the immunity of their offices.
choices.B: Neither the president nor the senator, because neither exceeded the immunity of their offices.
choices.C: The president only, because he exceeded his executive immunity.
choices.D: The senator only, because she exceeded her legislative immunity.

questions.explanation:
Immunity for Members of Congress
General
rule		 Absolute immunity from civil and criminal actions for statements & conduct made in regular course of legislative process (e.g., speeches on floor of Congress, committee hearings, reports)*
Exceptions
  • Prosecution for crime (e.g., bribery) when crime does not require proof of legislative acts or inquiring into motive behind such acts
  • Civil suits related to speeches made outside of Congress or republication of defamatory statement originally made in Congress
*This applies to congressional aides if legislator performing same acts would be immune.

The president enjoys absolute immunity for civil damages related to acts performed as part of the president’s executive responsibilities. However, the president does not have immunity for civil actions based on (1) conduct that occurred before the president took office or (2) acts unrelated to the performance of the president’s executive responsibilities.

Here, the president made a statement falsely accusing the senator of taking bribes and encouraging the rest of the Senate to vote in favor of the legislation. The president made this statement while in office, and it was related to an act performed as part of his executive responsibilities, affording him absolute immunity. And because the president did not exceed the immunity of his office, the president may not be held liable (Choices A and C).

Similarly, the Article I, Section 6 Speech or Debate Clause gives members of Congress absolute immunity from criminal and civil liability for official legislative activities. This includes any speech made on the House or Senate floor—regardless of whether the speech relates to pending legislative business. However, a member of Congress does not have absolute immunity for:

  • criminal prosecution when the crime does not require proof of legislative acts or inquiring into the motive behind such acts or
  • speeches made outside of Congress or the republication of a defamatory statement originally made in Congress.

Here, the senator made a slanderous statement about the president at a legislative hearing. Because the senator made this statement during her official legislative activity, she has absolute immunity. However, the senator then republished this slanderous statement during an interview outside of Congress, thereby exceeding the scope of her legislative immunity (Choice B). Therefore, the senator may be held liable.

📌 Educational Objective

The president enjoys absolute immunity for civil damages related to acts performed as part of the president’s executive responsibilities. And members of Congress have absolute immunity from criminal and civil liability for official legislative activities but not the republication of a defamatory statement originally made in Congress.

📚 References
  • Hutchinson v. Proxmire, 443 U.S. 111 (1979) (holding that absolute immunity for legislative members does not apply to the republication of a defamatory statement originally made in Congress).
questions.zh-question:
在一次关于总统支持的立法的听证会上，一位参议员发表了针对总统的诽谤性言论。当天晚些时候，该参议员在接受记者采访时重复了该言论，旨在激励公民联系他们的国会议员并鼓励他们投票反对该立法。在得知该参议员的言论后，总统在新闻发布会上发表官方声明，诽谤该参议员，虚假指控她收受贿赂，并鼓励参议院其他成员投票支持该立法。
如果因这些言论而对总统或参议员提起寻求金钱赔偿的民事诉讼（civil suit for money damages），谁可能被依法追究责任？

zh-choices.A: 总统和参议员均可，因为他们各自都超出了其职务豁免权（immunity of their offices）。
zh-choices.B: 总统和参议员均不可，因为他们均未超出其职务豁免权（immunity of their offices）。
zh-choices.C: 仅总统可，因为他超出了其行政豁免权（executive immunity）。
zh-choices.D: 仅参议员可，因为她超出了其立法豁免权（legislative immunity）。

questions.zh-explanation:
MBE 考点解析

Constitutional Law: Separation of Powers - Federal interbranch relationships

本题真正考的是

一句话定位考点

本题真正考的是：国会议员的 言论与辩论条款（Speech or Debate Clause） 只保护正式立法活动；把国会里说过的诽谤话带到国会外重复，就会失去豁免。

三秒认题路径：

国会议员 → 国会内发言 → 国会外重复 → 豁免失效 → 选 D

核心法律规则

言论与辩论条款（Speech or Debate Clause）给国会议员对正式立法活动的民事和刑事绝对豁免，考场意思：你只要是在国会听证、议场发言、正式立法流程里说的，就先按“不能追责”处理。重复发表（republication）不算立法活动，考场意思：你把国会里的诽谤话拿去国会外接受采访再说一遍，就已经跳出保护圈。总统绝对豁免（absolute immunity）只保护其职务范围内的官方行为，考场意思：这里总统是在任内以官方身份就政策发表声明，所以通常不追究民事赔偿。

核心判例： Hutchinson v. Proxmire — 国会外重复国会内的诽谤言论，不受立法豁免保护。

思维导图

先看谁在说话、在哪说话
总统：任内官方记者会发言 → 属于执行职务 → 通常有绝对豁免，不能判赔
参议员：国会听证中发言 → 正式立法活动 → 先有豁免
关键跳出点：采访中再次重复诽谤 → 国会外重复，不在豁免内
结论：总统不担责，参议员因国会外重复而可被追责 → 选 D

考点陷阱

你可能会想：两个人都和国会、政策有关，所以都该有豁免。

但考试真正问的是：豁免保护的是“正式立法活动”，不是“跟立法沾边的任何发言”。

司法考试看的是「法律程序上能不能救济」，而不是「物理上的秘密有没有泄露」。

所以参议员在听证里说过一次还不够，后来又在国会外采访里重复，命题人就是要你抓住这个“出圈”动作。

正确答案与干扰项排除

为什么选 D？

题干里参议员先在听证中发言，后来又在国会外采访中重复 slanderous statement，后者已经超出立法豁免，所以只她可能担责。

❌ 概念混淆 | 豁免范围误判

✕ A: 把 absolute immunity 当成无限通行证了。

❌ 事实误判 | 采访重复漏读

✕ B: 漏看参议员后来在国会外又重说了一遍。

❌ 法律适用 | 总统豁免套错

✕ C: 把总统的 executive responsibilities 保护套到参议员身上了。

这题建议用什么方法？

先分人物，再看言论地点：国会内先有豁免，国会外重复立刻出界。

考场速记

记忆口诀：In Certain Circumstances, An Appeal Can Be Made Prematurely 是中间上诉用的；这题别乱套，记住国会议员只护“国会内正式立法活动”，国会外重复（republication outside Congress） 就会失去豁免。
